Key partners and customers: Its chips are used in products from Samsung, Huawei, Honor, Xiaomi, OPPO, OnePlus, Edifier, Pine64, and Fairphone.
Organization type: The company is a privately held semiconductor company.
Business model: The company makes money through chip sales.
Scale and maturity: The company is an emerging player competing with major semiconductor companies in the audio chip segment.
Geography: The company is based in China and operates in the global consumer electronics semiconductor market.
Beyond audio: Audio is the company's entire focus, centered on wireless audio and audio-centric wearable SoCs.

points.name: Dialog Semiconductor
points.description: London semiconductor company designing power management and audio integrated circuits for wireless earbuds.
points.bullets:
A semiconductor company that designs and sells highly integrated power management, Bluetooth Low Energy SoCs, and audio integrated circuits for portable devices and wearables. It builds audio DSP codecs and ANC codecs, and licenses third-party DSP intellectual property to integrate into its chips. It targets consumer electronics brands needing specialized, low-power wireless and audio processing silicon.
1. A semiconductor company that designs low-power SoCs and audio codecs sold as finished chips running in consumer devices.
2. Integrated circuits combining ARM Cortex-M processors, Bluetooth Low Energy radios, audio codecs, and licensed Tensilica HiFi Audio/Voice DSP cores.
3. Active noise cancellation, beamforming, noise suppression, acoustic echo cancellation, and always-on voice activation.
4. The company provides its technology as finished semiconductor chips.
5. The chips are designed into true wireless earphones, smart ear-worn devices, wearables, virtual reality remotes, human interface devices, smartphones, and tablets.
6. The company sells to consumer electronics brands and portable device manufacturers.
7. Its chips are designed into end-user consumer devices by electronics brands.
8. It combines low-power wireless connectivity, power management, and advanced audio processing with integrated security features on a single chip.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It licensed DSP IP from Cadence Design Systems, partnered with Sensory for voice recognition, and is a promoter of the ULE Alliance.
Organization type: The organization is a subsidiary of a publicly traded semiconductor company.
Business model: It makes money through semiconductor chip sales.
Scale and maturity: It is an established, well-known semiconductor provider acquired by a larger parent company in 2021.
Geography: The company is based in London, United Kingdom.
Beyond audio: Beyond audio, the company develops power management ICs, Bluetooth Low Energy SoCs, and secure connectivity solutions.

points.name: Synaptics
points.description: US semiconductor company building Edge AI processors, wireless connectivity chips, and integrated audio solutions.
points.bullets:
A publicly traded semiconductor company that designs and sells edge AI processors, microcontrollers, and wireless connectivity chips, incorporating audio, voice, and speech processing capabilities for IoT device makers.
1. A chip company that designs AI-native IoT processors and microcontrollers, sold as packaged semiconductors and development boards that run in customers' edge devices.
2. Multimodal edge AI processors and microcontrollers built on Arm cores and neural processing units using an open-source MLIR-based compiler toolchain.
3. Audio processing, voice recognition, speech processing, and integrated audio and haptics reproduction.
4. The capabilities are delivered in silicon chips, wireless combo modules, and software development kits.
5. Smart appliances, point-of-sale terminals, wearables, smart home devices, and conference room systems.
6. IoT device manufacturers, consumer electronics brands, and enterprise hardware developers.
7. Its chips are designed into smart appliances and IoT devices by consumer electronics brands and enterprise hardware manufacturers.
8. It is the first strategic silicon partner to put Google's Coral NPU architecture into production, combining it with an open-source MLIR compiler and runtime.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Strategic partners include Google Research for the Coral NPU, Arm for processor cores, Vesper for MEMS microphones, INVENTVM for audio amplifiers, and Microsoft for Teams-certified audio.
Organization type: A publicly traded semiconductor company being acquired by a larger publicly traded semiconductor manufacturer.
Business model: Revenue is generated through semiconductor chip sales and development kit hardware.
Scale and maturity: A multi-billion dollar enterprise targeted for acquisition in an all-stock transaction valued at approximately seven billion dollars.
Geography: Based in San Jose, California, operating globally through distribution partners.
Beyond audio: Beyond audio, the organization develops human-machine interface technologies including touchpads, fingerprint sensors, display controllers, video processing, and wireless connectivity.

points.name: Maxim Integrated
points.description: San Jose semiconductor company designing analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits, including smart amplifiers and power management chips for earphones.
points.bullets:
A semiconductor company that designs, manufactures, and sells analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits, including audio amplifiers, power management chips, and AI microcontrollers, for consumer electronics and portable audio device manufacturers.
1. A semiconductor company that designs and manufactures analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits sold as chips for embedded hardware applications.
2. The core technology consists of analog front ends, Class-D amplifier topologies with integrated boost converters, and power management integrated circuits using single-inductor multiple-output buck-boost regulators.
3. Audio capabilities include high-efficiency digital input Class-D amplification, dynamic speaker management, and speaker characterization for optimized output.
4. The organization delivers its technology as finished integrated circuits, along with associated graphical design software and hardware evaluation kits.
5. The chips are used in portable audio devices, true wireless stereo earphones, small wearables, and intelligent edge devices.
6. The company sells to consumer electronics device manufacturers, wearable brands, and audio component manufacturers.
7. Its integrated circuits are designed into end-user wearable and portable audio products by consumer electronics brands and component manufacturers.
8. Its approach combines integrated power management circuitry and dynamic speaker management directly into its audio amplifier chips to increase efficiency and output in small form factors.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The organization is a subsidiary of Analog Devices and supplies smart amplifier chips to PUI Audio.
Organization type: The organization is a subsidiary brand of a publicly traded semiconductor company.
Business model: The company makes money through the direct sales of semiconductor integrated circuits, evaluation kits, and associated software.
Scale and maturity: The organization is a well-established, publicly traded semiconductor entity that operated independently for decades before being acquired.
Geography: The company is based in San Jose, California, USA, and operates as part of a global semiconductor business.
Beyond audio: Beyond audio, the organization designs and manufactures a broad portfolio of power and battery management ICs, sensors, interface ICs, communications solutions, digital ICs, embedded security, and microcontrollers for various markets.

points.name: Microchip Technology Inc.
points.description: US semiconductor company making Bluetooth audio chips for true wireless earbuds.
points.bullets:
A semiconductor company that designs and manufactures microcontrollers, mixed-signal, analog, and Flash-IP solutions, including Bluetooth audio system-on-chips and DSP-enabled microcontrollers for embedded control and audio applications.
1. A chip company that designs and sells semiconductors, Bluetooth audio SoCs, and microcontrollers with DSP capabilities, delivered as finished hardware components and certified modules.
2. Integrated circuits and system-on-chips combining Bluetooth 5 compliance, high-resolution audio codecs, wireless stereo technology, and embedded 32-bit DSP processing.
3. High-fidelity wireless audio streaming, high-resolution Bluetooth audio decoding, true wireless stereo RF stability, and real-time 3D gesture processing.
4. Chips, certified modules, on-chip software libraries, graphical configuration tools, and development kits.
5. True wireless earbuds, gaming headphones, wearable fitness trackers, sound measuring instruments, and embedded control systems.
6. Audio system designers, consumer electronics brands, and embedded control engineers.
7. Its chips are designed into finished consumer audio products like gaming headphones and true wireless earbuds by consumer electronics brands.
8. It integrates licensed third-party high-resolution audio codecs directly into its Bluetooth audio system-on-chips alongside its broad embedded control portfolio.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It partners with Sony to integrate LDAC audio codec technology and its chips are used by Audeze in gaming headphones.
Organization type: A publicly traded semiconductor company.
Business model: Chip sales, certified module sales, and developer tool distribution.
Scale and maturity: A large, established global semiconductor manufacturer.
Geography: Based in Chandler, Arizona, USA, operating worldwide.
Beyond audio: It provides a broad range of microcontrollers, FPGAs, analog components, and sensors for diverse embedded control markets beyond audio.

points.name: CEVA
points.description: Publicly traded IP company licensing DSPs and wireless audio platforms for connected devices.
points.bullets:
An IP licensor that licenses silicon and software IP for connectivity, sensing and inference to device makers. It licenses audio and voice DSP cores, wireless audio platforms, audio front-end software, spatial audio software, neural processors and sensor fusion algorithms.
1. A silicon and software IP licensor whose DSP cores, NPUs and software algorithms are integrated by chip vendors and OEMs into their system-on-chips and finished hardware devices.
2. VLIW and SIMD audio DSPs, low-power neural processors, RF and baseband Bluetooth radios, and neural network-based algorithms running on-device at the edge.
3. Acoustic echo cancellation, beamforming, noise suppression, voice activation, speech recognition, spatial audio rendering, head tracking, EVS voice coding and Bluetooth audio streaming.
4. Licensed IP cores, NPUs, wireless platforms and software algorithms delivered as integrateable design assets for semiconductor and device manufacturers.
5. Earbuds, hearing aids, smart TVs, soundbars, gaming headsets, car infotainment systems, smart speakers, wearables, mobile phones and IoT devices.
6. Chip companies, consumer electronics OEMs, automakers and developers building edge devices.
7. Its licensed IP cores and algorithms are integrated by chip vendors into their semiconductors and by OEMs into their finished consumer electronics products.
8. It bundles wireless connectivity RF and baseband IP with audio DSPs and voice processing software to provide turnkey edge platforms for hearables and wearables.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Strategic member of RISC-V International, with collaborations with Synopsys, VisiSonics, Intel and Actions Technology.
Organization type: Publicly traded company listed on NASDAQ.
Business model: IP licensing fees and per-unit royalties for shipped devices incorporating its cores and software.
Scale and maturity: A mature public company with more than 22 billion shipped devices and over 400 customers.
Geography: Based in the United States with a global customer base.
Beyond audio: The company also licenses wireless connectivity IP for Bluetooth, Wi-Fi and UWB alongside sensor fusion and motion tracking technologies for IoT, automotive and industrial markets.

points.name: Actions Technology
points.description: Semiconductor company designing low-power wireless audio chips and edge AI audio SoCs for IoT devices.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor company that designs and sells low-power edge AI audio SoCs integrating licensed third-party Bluetooth and DSP IP along with its own compute-in-memory neural processing, for consumer electronics and IoT device makers.
1. A chip company that designs and sells wireless audio and edge AI audio SoCs that run in customers' battery-powered devices.
2. Heterogeneous triple-core architectures combining ARM CPUs, HiFi5 DSPs and SRAM-based mixed-mode compute-in-memory NPUs, alongside licensed Bluetooth intellectual property.
3. Real-time voiceprint classification, ambient sound classification, low-latency private wireless audio and Bluetooth AI audio processing.
4. Finished semiconductor chips and accompanying AI development tools.
5. Battery-powered IoT devices and consumer wireless audio products.
6. Consumer electronics brands and IoT device makers.
7. Its chips are designed into battery-powered wireless audio and IoT devices by consumer electronics brands.
8. Mixed-mode SRAM-based compute-in-memory technology is integrated with a HiFi5 DSP to deliver TOPS-level AI computing at milliwatt-level power consumption for small models.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Ceva-Waves and ARM.
Organization type: Privately held or publicly traded semiconductor company.
Business model: Chip sales.
Scale and maturity: Established semiconductor company with multiple shipping audio SoC families.
Geography: Based in China.
Beyond audio: The organization's focus is entirely on semiconductor and audio technology.

points.name: Triad Magnetics
points.description: US pro audio company manufacturing analog audio transformers for signal processing equipment.
points.bullets:
A component manufacturer that designs and builds audio transformers and custom magnetics for professional audio equipment makers, providing standard and custom parts for analog signal processing.
1. A component maker that builds analog audio transformers and sells them as finished components for integration into professional audio equipment.
2. Passive magnetic components using transformer windings for analog audio signal conditioning.
3. Impedance matching, DC blocking, and low-distortion signal transfer across the 20 Hz to 20 kHz audio spectrum while preserving analog warmth.
4. Finished hardware components sold directly to equipment manufacturers.
5. Mixing consoles, equalizers, and guitar amplifiers.
6. Professional audio equipment manufacturers.
7. Its transformers are designed into professional audio hardware by equipment brands.
8. It modernizes vintage transformer designs to contemporary manufacturing tolerances while preserving heritage analog character.
points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held manufacturing company.
Business model: Direct sale of hardware components.
Scale and maturity: A long-established company with a history dating to the 1950s and hybrid global manufacturing.
Geography: Based in Perris, California, with high-volume manufacturing in the Philippines and China.
Beyond audio: The company builds magnetics and transformers beyond the audio sector.

points.name: dCS
points.description: British high-end audio manufacturer building premium digital-to-analog converters and digital source components.
points.bullets:
A high-end audio equipment manufacturer that builds premium digital-to-analog converters, disc transports, and external master clocks for audiophiles and audio professionals. The company adapts signal conversion expertise originally developed for radar systems into digital audio source components for home and reference playback systems.
1. A maker of professional and consumer audio equipment that sells finished hardware components used in digital audio source chains.
2. Proprietary Ring DAC technology combining reconfigured circuit boards and discrete analog output stages to perform high-resolution digital-to-analog signal conversion.
3. High-transparency digital-to-analog conversion with reduced distortion, improved linearity, and clock synchronization for SACD and CD playback.
4. Finished hardware products including standalone DACs, SACD and CD transports, combination player/DAC units, and external master clock accessories.
5. High-end home audio systems, reference playback setups, and audiophile listening environments.
6. Audiophiles and high-end audio consumers.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to consumers for use in premium home audio playback systems.
8. Proprietary Ring DAC architecture adapted from radar signal conversion expertise, delivering discrete circuit designs rather than off-the-shelf converter chips.
points.profile:
Organization type: Privately held audio electronics manufacturer.
Business model: Hardware sales of premium digital audio components.
Scale and maturity: An established company with over thirty years in digital audio and a track record of world-first products including the first 24-bit DAC for home use.
Geography: Based in Cambridge, UK.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: DSP Group
points.description: Semiconductor company developing voice processing chips and low-power AI silicon for smart devices.
points.bullets:
A semiconductor company that designs and sells audio system-on-chip solutions, voice processing chipsets, and DECT wireless communication silicon for consumer electronics device makers. It builds low-power AI inference SoCs and digital signal processors that deliver integrated voice enhancement and far-field voice recognition capabilities for smart devices.
1. A semiconductor company that designs low-power audio and voice processing SoCs and wireless communication chipsets sold as integrated circuits to device manufacturers.
2. Audio digital signal processors and system-on-chips running voice processing algorithms, active noise cancellation technology, and DECT wireless communication silicon.
3. Acoustic echo cancellation, noise suppression, beamforming, far-field support, always-on voice functionality, barge-in, active noise cancellation, and two-way wireless voice.
4. Chips, chipsets, and modules delivered to device manufacturers for embedding in finished hardware.
5. Smartphones, smart home nodes, voice-enabled smart devices, action cameras, and voice assistant modules.
6. Consumer electronics device makers, smart home device manufacturers, and voice assistant module makers.
7. Its chips and chipsets are designed into consumer electronics devices by device manufacturers.
8. It combines integrated audio DSPs, low-power AI inference SoCs, and ULE wireless communication silicon within a single semiconductor portfolio.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A subsidiary of Synaptics, with its technology used in Samsung phones, GoPro cameras, and iFLYTEK speech recognition software, and a promoter of the ULE Alliance with Philio-Tech and Libre.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand of a publicly traded semiconductor company.
Business model: Semiconductor and chipset sales.
Scale and maturity: Acquired in 2021, with established design wins in major consumer electronics brands and a global provider footprint.
Geography: A global provider of semiconductor solutions.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on voice processing, audio, and wireless communication semiconductor technology.

points.name: Conexant Systems
points.description: Semiconductor company designing audio CODECs and processors with noise cancellation for headsets and smart home devices.
points.bullets:
A semiconductor company that designs and markets audio codecs and embedded processors with companion audio processing software for smart home, PC and headset applications.
1. A chip company that designs audio codecs and embedded processors, sold as packaged semiconductors with reference software that run in consumer devices.
2. Audio codecs integrate analog front ends, Class-H and Class-D amplifiers, ARM Cortex microcontrollers and dual-core DSPs alongside digital audio processing algorithms.
3. The company delivers active noise cancellation, ambient noise inclusion, wake-on-voice, noise reduction for VoIP and speech recognition, and intelligent speaker protection.
4. The organization provides packaged chips, USB-C-compliant codec families and audio processing software suites.
5. The technology is used in headsets, smartphones, PCs, tablets, gaming headsets and smart home devices.
6. The company sells to consumer electronics device makers and PC OEMs.
7. Its chips and software are designed into headsets, PCs and smart home products by consumer electronics brands.
8. The company integrates active noise cancellation, wake-on-voice and ambient inclusion alongside audio codecs in single-chip USB-C solutions.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The organization is an Amazon Alexa voice services partner and its software meets Intel and Google automatic speech recognition performance requirements; it uses ARM Cortex processor technology and was acquired by Synaptics.
Organization type: The company is a subsidiary brand acquired by a publicly traded semiconductor company.
Business model: The organization makes money through chip sales and bundled software.
Scale and maturity: The company is an established semiconductor provider acquired by Synaptics in 2017.
Geography: The company operates in China and globally, with presence at events such as Mobile World Congress Shanghai.
Beyond audio: Beyond audio, the company designs video processing solutions.

points.name: TSMC
points.description: Taiwanese semiconductor foundry manufacturing advanced low-power chips for wireless audio devices.
points.bullets:
A semiconductor foundry that manufactures chips designed by other companies, including processes and lines optimized for audio applications. It fabricates MEMS, ultra-low-leakage radio and processor chips, and other semiconductor devices for chip companies. It provides wafer fabrication services on advanced and specialized nodes for fabless design companies.
1. A semiconductor foundry that manufactures chips designed by customers and sells fabricated wafers.
2. Silicon and MEMS fabrication processes across nodes including 22nm ultra-low-leakage, 28nm CMOS, 40nm, and 55nm low-power.
3. MEMS fabrication for audio applications and ultra-low-leakage process manufacturing for low-power audio and radio chips.
4. Fabricated wafers and manufactured chips delivered to fabless chip designers.
5. Earbuds, hearing aids, smart speakers, and other audio devices that use fabricated chips.
6. Fabless semiconductor companies and chip designers.
7. Its fabricated wafers are used by chip companies that design and sell semiconductors for audio devices.
8. It offers MEMS fabrication services specifically optimized for audio applications alongside advanced low-power nodes.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Apple, Nvidia, AMD, Nordic Semiconductor, Microsoft, Renesas, and Cadence.
Organization type: A publicly traded company.
Business model: Wafer fabrication and chip manufacturing services.
Scale and maturity: The dominant global semiconductor foundry manufacturing the most advanced chip designs.
Geography: Based in Hsinchu, Taiwan, with global manufacturing operations.
Beyond audio: A general-purpose semiconductor foundry serving all major semiconductor markets.

points.name: Mistral AI
points.description: French AI company developing speech-to-text models, voice agents, and text-to-speech APIs.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer that builds large language models and generative speech models, providing transcription, text-to-speech, and voice-agent software for enterprises, developers, and public institutions.
1. An AI model developer whose speech models run in the cloud behind APIs and are also released as downloadable open-weight models for self-deployment.
2. Large generative language and speech models based on neural networks, hosted in cloud infrastructure and distributed as open weights.
3. The company delivers batch and real-time speech-to-text transcription, speaker diarization, word-level timestamps, context biasing, zero-shot voice cloning, and multilingual text-to-speech generation.
4. Customers access the models through cloud APIs, a voice-agent software development kit, an audio testing playground, and downloadable open-weight model files.
5. The models are used in live voice applications, transcription services, and conversational AI agents.
6. The company sells to enterprises, developers, and public institutions.
7. Its models are accessed directly by developers and enterprises through cloud endpoints or self-deployed on controlled infrastructure.
8. The company distinguishes itself by offering sovereign, European-hosted AI infrastructure alongside open-weight model releases for self-deployment.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company builds its voice-agent software using the LiveKit framework and distributes model weights on Hugging Face, while operating infrastructure powered by Nvidia GPUs.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held startup.
Business model: The company makes money through API usage billed per token or character, and commercial software licenses.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2023, the company has raised billions in funding and holds a valuation exceeding ten billion dollars.
Geography: The company is based in Paris, France, and operates cloud regions in Europe, the United States, and globally.
Beyond audio: Beyond audio, the company develops general large language models, small language models, coding models, and consumer chatbot applications.

points.name: Asahi Kasei Microdevices (AKM)
points.description: Japanese semiconductor manufacturer making Velvet Sound audio chips and processors.
points.bullets:
A semiconductor manufacturer that develops and sells audio integrated circuits, including digital-to-analog converters, analog-to-digital converters, and audio codecs, as well as sensor hardware and clock generators for consumer electronics and automotive applications.
1. A semiconductor company that designs and manufactures audio ICs and analog front-end components, sold as physical chips to electronics manufacturers.
2. Analog and mixed-signal integrated circuit designs utilizing audio-optimized LSI manufacturing processes to achieve low-distortion, low-noise, and high-resolution signal conversion.
3. High-resolution audio digital-to-analog and analog-to-digital conversion, multi-channel audio processing, active noise cancelling, asynchronous sample rate conversion, and low phase noise clock generation.
4. Physical semiconductor chips sold to electronics manufacturers for integration into their hardware designs.
5. Portable audio products, smartphones, true wireless stereo earbuds, automotive audio systems, and high-fidelity audio components.
6. Consumer electronics brands, portable audio device manufacturers, smartphone makers, and automotive electronics designers.
7. Its chips are designed into consumer electronics and automotive hardware by equipment manufacturers.
8. It utilizes a proprietary low-distortion, high signal-to-noise ratio integrated circuit architecture marketed specifically for high-fidelity audio applications.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A subsidiary of Asahi Kasei Corporation and a partner that embeds lightweight artificial intelligence models into its advanced sensor hardware.
Organization type: A subsidiary electronic components manufacturer of a publicly traded parent chemical and materials corporation.
Business model: Sales of semiconductor components and integrated circuits to hardware manufacturers.
Scale and maturity: A major global supplier of sensing devices and integrated circuits with a long-standing presence in the audio market.
Geography: Based in Japan with global manufacturing operations and offices.
Beyond audio: The company also produces millimeter-wave radar modules, magnetic sensors, optical sensors, and other electronic components beyond audio.

points.name: Renesas
points.description: Japanese semiconductor company producing microcontrollers and processors for voice recognition and edge AI audio applications.
points.bullets:
A semiconductor company that designs and manufactures microcontrollers, processors, and power management integrated circuits, providing edge AI hardware and reference designs for voice recognition and audio amplification in automotive, industrial, and IoT applications.
1. A semiconductor company that designs microcontrollers and processors integrating AI accelerators and NPUs, sold as chips and reference designs that run on-device in customers' embedded systems.
2. Microcontrollers and microprocessors with integrated DRP-AI accelerators and Arm Cortex cores with Ethos-U NPUs for on-device edge AI and real-time control.
3. Low-power voice recognition, voice user interfaces, and audio amplification.
4. Finished silicon chips, power management ICs, and reference designs for voice interfaces.
5. Automotive systems, industrial equipment, factory automation, robotics, and IoT devices.
6. Device makers, OEMs, and industrial manufacturers.
7. Its chips and reference designs are integrated by OEMs into embedded systems for automotive and industrial applications.
8. Integrates dedicated AI accelerators and NPUs alongside microcontroller cores for low-power edge AI processing in embedded systems.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Acquired Dialog Semiconductor for BLE SoCs and power management, and collaborated with DSP Concepts on the TalkTo Voice Reference Design and Cyberon for voice user interface solutions.
Organization type: A publicly traded semiconductor company.
Business model: Chip sales, power management IC sales, and reference designs.
Scale and maturity: A major, well-established semiconductor manufacturer operating globally.
Geography: Based in Japan, operating globally.
Beyond audio: Produces semiconductors for automotive, industrial, and IoT applications with a focus on edge AI, microcontrollers, and power management.

points.name: ESS Technology
points.description: US fabless semiconductor company designing high-performance audio converter chips for audio equipment.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor company that designs and markets high-performance audio converters, amplifiers, and integrated circuits for mobile, consumer, automotive, and professional audiophile systems.
1. A semiconductor company that designs high-performance audio chips sold to equipment manufacturers for integration into their hardware.
2. Mixed-signal and analog integrated circuits utilizing HyperStream modulation, integrated digital signal processing, and multi-level Class-D amplifier topologies.
3. High-resolution digital-to-analog and analog-to-digital conversion, headphone amplification, speaker protection, signal boosting, and USB audio bridging.
4. Physical semiconductor chips, integrated CODECs, companion voltage regulators, and reference designs.
5. USB-C audio dongles, headsets, mobile devices, digital audio players, headphone amplifiers, audio interfaces, studio equipment, and automotive processors.
6. Consumer electronics brands, audiophile equipment manufacturers, and professional audio hardware makers.
7. Its semiconductor chips are designed into finished audio hardware by consumer electronics and professional audio brands.
8. Focuses on achieving ultra-high dynamic range and low distortion in its converter products through proprietary modulation and integration.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Chips are used in hardware products from Sennheiser, Topping, Shanling, MOTU, AudioQuest, Questyle, and Goldhorn.
Organization type: A privately held fabless semiconductor company.
Business model: Semiconductor chip sales.
Scale and maturity: A company in operation for three decades with 51 to 200 employees.
Geography: Based in San Jose, California, United States.
Beyond audio: A pure-play audio semiconductor company with its entire focus on high-performance audio and signal processing integrated circuits.

points.name: New Japan Radio
points.description: Japanese semiconductor company entering the MEMS microphone market.
points.bullets:
A semiconductor company that manufactures electronic components, specifically entering the market for MEMS microphones.
1. A semiconductor company that designs and manufactures MEMS microphone components for integration into hardware products.
2. Microelectromechanical systems technology fabricated as miniature acoustic transducers.
3. Acoustic sensing and sound capture.
4. Finished semiconductor hardware components.
5. Device manufacturers requiring acoustic input components.
6. Its microphone components are designed into electronic hardware products by consumer electronics brands.
points.profile:
Organization type: A semiconductor company associated with Nisshinbo Micro Devices Inc.
Geography: Based in Tokyo, Japan.
Beyond audio: The company manufactures a range of electronic components beyond audio.

points.name: Firelight Technologies
points.description: Australian software company developing audio middleware for video games.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that builds interactive audio middleware for video game developers. The company provides an authoring environment for sound designers and composers and a cross-platform engine for real-time playback that integrates with game engines. It is a subsidiary brand acquired to expand its parent's capabilities in gaming and immersive audio.
1. A developer tools company whose platform sound designers and game developers use to author and implement interactive audio.
2. A real-time audio mixing and playback engine combined with an authoring environment for adaptive audio and haptic effects.
3. Real-time sound manipulation, adaptive music, interactive audio event authoring, and haptic effects integration.
4. Middleware software and plugins for game engines, offered under free and commercial licenses.
5. Video games across PC, console, and mobile platforms, integrating into commercial game engines and custom game technology.
6. Indie and professional game developers, sound designers, and composers.
7. Its middleware is integrated by game developers into their game engines and custom game technology.
8. It combines an authoring environment for sound designers with a cross-platform playback engine that integrates directly into major game engines.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Unity, Unreal Engine, Meta, Stable Audio, Sound Librarian, and Bose Corporation.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand of a publicly traded parent company.
Business model: Software licenses and subscriptions, including free licenses for indies and small game development companies.
Geography: Based in Melbourne, Australia.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is on interactive audio tools for game development.

points.name: StreamUnlimited
points.description: Austrian audio engineering company developing software and hardware modules for connected audio products and smart home integrations.
points.bullets:
An engineering services and module provider that supplies software, hardware modules, and integration services for connected audio products to consumer electronics and smart home manufacturers.
1. A system integrator and module developer that builds connected audio software stacks and pre-certified hardware modules, sold as licensed IP, finished modules, and engineering services for integration into customer products.
2. The core technology consists of audio streaming software stacks, networked amplification platforms, and multi-room synchronization algorithms running on embedded processors.
3. It delivers high-resolution multi-room audio streaming, networked speaker amplification, immersive audio format playback, and integration of conversational AI assistants.
4. Customers get it through licensed software development kits, reference designs, pre-certified hardware modules, and custom engineering services.
5. It is used in connected speakers, soundbars, networked passive speakers, and smart home audio systems.
6. It sells to high-end audio brands, CEDIA-channel integrators, mainstream consumer electronics manufacturers, and semiconductor companies.
7. Its software and modules are integrated by consumer electronics brands into their connected audio products.
8. It acts as a de facto global system integrator sitting between semiconductor vendors and audio brands, offering its own IP alongside modular, pre-certified hardware and software for fast time-to-market.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It partners with all major semiconductor companies, uses NXP's SR250 UWB solution, and was acquired by Bose.
Organization type: It is a privately owned company operating as a subsidiary brand within Bose's Audio Technology business.
Business model: It makes money through hardware module sales, software licenses, and engineering services.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2005 with over 120 employees, it was acquired by Bose in June 2026.
Geography: It is based in Vienna, Austria, with offices in Bratislava, Shenzhen, Osaka, and San Francisco, and operates globally.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on connected audio and IoT products.

points.name: Skullcandy
points.description: US consumer audio brand making affordable headphones and earbuds for youth and action-sports culture.
points.bullets:
A consumer audio brand that designs and sells headphones and earbuds for youthful, action-sports-oriented consumers, integrating licensed audio technologies and a companion app to deliver smart features and sound personalization.
1. An equipment maker that designs and sells finished wireless earbuds and headphones running licensed embedded software and signal processing.
2. Customized Bluetooth SoCs running licensed operating systems with embedded AI, integrated with licensed noise cancellation, spatial processing, and hearing personalization technologies.
3. Active noise cancellation, hands-free voice control, spatial audio processing, over-the-air firmware updates, and personalized sound based on in-app hearing tests.
4. Finished hardware products supported by a companion mobile application.
5. Wireless earbuds, over-ear headphones, smart glasses with associated true wireless earbuds, and lifestyle sport and action-sports settings.
6. Consumers seeking affordable, lifestyle-oriented audio products with bass-forward sound.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold direct to consumers through retail channels, incorporating software and signal processing technologies licensed from third-party providers.
8. The organization targets a youthful, adventurous consumer base with affordable, bold designs and strong bass, distinguishing its products from premium audio brands by licensing their high-end audio technologies for lower-cost devices.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Operates as a separate brand within its parent company Bose's Premium Consumer Audio business, having previously licensed technology from Bose, Bragi, and Mimi.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand of a privately held company, formerly an independent public company backed by private equity.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished consumer audio products.
Scale and maturity: A major player in the earbuds and headphone market, founded in 2003 and acquired by its parent company in 2026.
Geography: Based in Park City, Utah, USA, operating in the global consumer electronics market.
Beyond audio: The organization's entire focus is on consumer audio products and lifestyle branding.

points.name: Beats
points.description: Consumer audio brand making stylish, bass-forward headphones and sport-focused earbuds.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer audio equipment that designs and sells headphones, earbuds, and portable speakers directly to consumers.
1. A maker of finished audio hardware that is sold as physical products running on embedded processors.
2. The company's products use Bluetooth wireless connectivity, custom audio processing chips, active noise canceling algorithms, and biometric sensors.
3. The devices deliver active noise canceling, bass-optimized sound reproduction, heart-rate monitoring, and hands-free call processing.
4. Customers receive the company's audio technology through finished hardware products, including true wireless earbuds, over-ear headphones, and Bluetooth speakers.
5. The technology is used in consumer earbuds, sport headphones, and portable speakers.
6. The company sells directly to consumers.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to end users through retail channels.
8. The company is distinguished by its sport-focused and bass-heavy acoustic tuning, combined with integrated biometric monitoring and seamless integration with mobile operating systems.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company operates as a subsidiary of Apple and sources Bluetooth chips from Airoha.
Organization type: The company is a subsidiary brand of a publicly traded parent company.
Business model: The company makes money through hardware sales of finished audio products.
Scale and maturity: The organization was founded in 2008, raised $560 million in funding prior to acquisition, and currently has 201 to 500 employees.
Geography: The company is based in Culver City, California, USA.
Beyond audio: The company's entire focus is on consumer audio products.

points.name: INVENTVM Semiconductor
points.description: Italian semiconductor startup developing ultra-low-power amplifiers and MEMS speaker drivers for wearable audio devices.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor company that develops mixed-signal audio and power management integrated circuits, specializing in ultra-low-power wearable amplifiers, MEMS speaker drivers, and piezoelectric audio and haptic drivers for wearable and automotive applications.
1. A fabless chip company that designs mixed-signal audio and power management ICs and piezoelectric driver algorithms, sold as bare chips to device manufacturers.
2. Mixed-signal integrated circuits combining Class-D amplifiers, high-voltage drivers, boost converters, and power management, alongside digital signal processing algorithms for transducer control.
3. Ultra-low-power audio amplification, MEMS speaker driving, piezoelectric audio and haptic driving, dynamic speaker protection, and automotive audio diagnostics.
4. Bare semiconductor chips, reference platforms, and embedded DSP algorithms.
5. True wireless earbuds, audio glasses, hearing aids, smartwatches, AR/VR products, and automotive audio systems.
6. Consumer electronics device makers, wearable manufacturers, and automotive OEMs.
7. Its chips and driver algorithms are designed into wearable and automotive audio products by consumer electronics brands and automakers.
8. Its PiezoDrive technology integrates amplification, DSP, and transducer control to drive capacitive piezoelectric loads for combined audio and haptic output.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its PiezoDrive technology was supplied for an integrated audio and haptics solution by a named partner, and it has collaborated on reference designs with transducer manufacturers and audio software developers.
Organization type: Privately held semiconductor startup acquired by a publicly traded audio chip company.
Business model: Semiconductor chip sales.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2021 through a management buyout and acquired by a publicly traded parent in 2026.
Geography: Based in Pavia, Italy.
Beyond audio: The company's focus is exclusively on mixed-signal audio, haptic, and power management semiconductor design.

points.name: BdSound
points.description: Detroit technology company providing intelligent audio processing technology for in-vehicle conferencing.
points.bullets:
A technology company that provides intelligent audio processing technology for in-vehicle conferencing, collaborating with other firms on concept demonstrations.
1. An audio software developer whose intelligent audio processing technology is integrated into partner concept demonstrations.
2. The technology delivers intelligent audio processing for in-vehicle conferencing systems.
3. The processing is used in in-vehicle conferencing concepts.
points.profile: Geography: The organization is based in Detroit, Michigan, USA.

points.name: TDK Corporation
points.description: Japanese electronics manufacturer producing MEMS microphones, sensors, and electronic components including SoundWire-compliant audio devices.
points.bullets:
An electronics manufacturer that produces electronic components, sensors and finished MEMS microphones for consumer electronics, automotive and industrial device makers. It designs and fabricates high-performance acoustic sensors with integrated interfaces for voice pickup and edge AI keyword detection. It delivers these components as finished parts for direct integration into hardware products.
1. A component and equipment maker that builds finished MEMS microphones and electronic components sold as packaged hardware parts that run in end-user devices.
2. Micro-electromechanical systems, piezoelectric transducers, tunnel magnetoresistance sensors and analog electronic components fabricated as packaged integrated circuits.
3. Voice pickup, acoustic activity detection, keyword recognition, sound detection, wear detection and head tracking.
4. Finished packaged hardware components, including digital and analog MEMS microphones, inductors and capacitors.
5. True wireless stereo earbuds, smartphones, smart speakers, smartwatches, notebooks, security cameras, automotive audio buses, smart glasses and augmented reality headsets.
6. Consumer electronics device makers, automakers, industrial system manufacturers and telecommunications equipment providers.
7. Its microphone and sensor components are designed into consumer earbuds, smartphones and automotive systems by hardware brands.
8. It fabricates miniaturized, energy-efficient MEMS microphones with integrated digital interfaces that remove the need for a separate codec between the microphone and the system processor.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Owns the InvenSense and Knowles brands and supplies components for Analog Devices automotive audio bus networks.
Organization type: A publicly traded multinational electronics corporation.
Business model: Component and hardware sales to device manufacturers.
Scale and maturity: A legacy corporation founded in 1935 with over 100,000 employees.
Geography: Based in Tokyo, Japan, and operates globally.
Beyond audio: The organization produces passive components, power supplies, magnetic products, motion sensors and ultrasonic time-of-flight sensors for automotive, industrial and consumer markets beyond audio.

points.name: Orosound
points.description: Parisian startup developing AI-powered noise reduction technology for premium communication headsets.
points.bullets:
A maker of premium audio equipment and developer of AI-powered audio technologies. It builds finished headset hardware for professional communication and develops proprietary noise cancellation and voice enhancement algorithms, which it also licenses to chip companies.
1. An equipment maker that sells finished headsets and an AI model developer whose noise reduction and ANC algorithms run on partners' chips.
2. AI-based active noise cancellation algorithms, hybrid ANC and directional voice capture processing implemented on low-power processors.
3. Open-ear active noise cancellation, hybrid active noise cancellation, face-to-face conversation enhancement and directional voice recording.
4. Finished headsets sold to consumers and licensed IP or algorithms integrated by semiconductor vendors.
5. Office headsets, video conferencing, phone calls and open-ear audio devices.
6. Consumers, preorder backers and chip companies licensing the algorithms.
7. Its headsets are sold directly to end users and its algorithms are integrated by chip vendors into their processors.
8. It combines shipping its own finished open-ear and noise-cancelling headsets with licensing the underlying AI audio algorithms to semiconductor partners.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: GreenWaves and Amazon, and is a subsidiary of Syntiant.
Organization type: A privately held startup acquired by and operating as a subsidiary of a publicly traded chip company.
Business model: Hardware sales and IP or per-unit royalties.
Scale and maturity: A startup that raised crowdfunding in 2016 and was later acquired.
Geography: Based in Paris, France.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: AudioSourceRE
points.description: Irish audio software startup developing AI tools that isolate individual instruments and vocals from mixed audio recordings.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer that creates sound separation software and algorithms for professional audio applications, isolating individual audio elements like vocals, drums, and speech from complex mixed recordings, and is porting its technology to embedded systems for real-time use.
1. An AI model developer whose audio separation models run as software products and plugins on users' machines and are being ported to run on-device on embedded processors.
2. Machine learning models perform audio source separation to isolate individual stems and distinguish speech from background noise.
3. Vocal extraction, instrument isolation, speech separation, and noise reduction.
4. Desktop software applications, digital audio workstation plugins, and embedded IP.
5. Professional studios, post-production workflows, DJ setups, and embedded real-time audio systems.
6. Producers, DJs, remix artists, and chip companies seeking embedded audio separation.
7. Its software is used directly by audio professionals, and its IP is being integrated by chip vendors into their embedded processor platforms.
8. Over twenty years of dedicated research into sound separation algorithms distinguishes its approach from broader audio AI models.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its technology was demonstrated on processors from GreenWaves, and the company was acquired by Syntiant.
Organization type: Privately held startup operating as a subsidiary brand after acquisition.
Business model: Software licenses and subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: A startup established through over twenty years of research and acquired by a chip company.
Geography: Based in Cork, Ireland.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is on audio source separation technology.

points.name: GreenWaves Technologies
points.description: French semiconductor startup developing ultra-low-power AI processors for hearable devices.
points.bullets:
A fabless chip company that designs ultra-low-power RISC-V processors for AI inferencing and audio processing in battery-powered edge devices, providing chips and software development kits to device makers.
1. A fabless chip company whose processors and development kits run on-device in customers' hearable and IoT products.
2. Ultra-low-power RISC-V processors with dedicated neural network accelerators and a hardware sound filtering block for time-domain audio processing.
3. Adaptive noise cancellation, AI-powered sound elimination, audio enhancement, and keyword detection.
4. Processors, development boards, and software development kits.
5. True wireless stereo earbuds, hearables, and IoT sensor devices.
6. Hearable device makers, IoT device manufacturers, and audio software developers.
7. Its processors are designed into hearable and IoT products by consumer electronics brands.
8. It builds ultra-low-power RISC-V processors based on the open-source PULP architecture for battery-operated edge AI.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its processors are manufactured by GlobalFoundries on a 22nm FDX process and by TSMC on a 55nm LP process, and it partners with audio software companies including Orosound, AudioSourceRE, and Elevear.
Organization type: A fabless semiconductor startup.
Business model: Chip sales and development kit hardware.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2014 and liquidated in 2025.
Geography: Based in Grenoble, France.
Beyond audio: It also designs processors for computer vision and vibration sensing in industrial and consumer IoT devices.

points.name: Ambiq
points.description: US semiconductor company making ultra-low-power microcontrollers and AI processors for energy-efficient voice and sensor applications.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor company that designs ultra-low-power microcontrollers and system-on-chips for edge AI applications including audio processing. It provides SoCs built on its subthreshold power optimized technology, along with supporting software development kits and model zoos, for device makers building battery-constrained hearables, wearables, and IoT devices.
1. A semiconductor company that designs low-power microcontrollers and system-on-chips, sold as finished silicon and supported by SDKs and reference models that run on its own chips.
2. Subthreshold and near-threshold voltage transistor operation integrated with Arm Cortex-M4 and Cortex-M55 processors, Helium AI/ML instructions, and Arm Ethos-U85 neural processing units to minimize energy consumption during on-device inference.
3. Real-time neural network-based speech enhancement, noise suppression, and acoustic environment detection running on-device.
4. Finished silicon chips, evaluation boards, software development kits, AI runtimes, and open-source model zoos for edge deployment.
5. Hearables, hearing aids, smart rings, smart glasses, wearables, industrial sensors, and battery-powered IoT devices.
6. Consumer electronics device makers, wearable brands, IoT manufacturers, and embedded developers building battery-constrained edge devices.
7. Its chips are designed into hearables, wearables, and IoT devices by consumer electronics brands and integrated into third-party development platforms.
8. Patented subthreshold power optimized technology achieves extreme energy efficiency by operating transistors in the subthreshold region, enabling always-on AI inference in battery-constrained or battery-free devices.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company uses Arm processor architectures and neural processing units, collaborates with Bravechip on chiplet platforms, and its hardware is supported by the Edge Impulse development platform.
Organization type: A privately held semiconductor company.
Business model: Chip sales and semiconductor licensing.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2010, with over 300 million devices shipped.
Geography: Based in Austin, Texas, USA, supplying semiconductors to device makers worldwide.
Beyond audio: The organization develops ultra-low-power semiconductor and edge AI solutions spanning healthcare, wearables, industrial automation, and smart environments, with audio processing as one application of its hardware.

points.name: AAC Technologies
points.description: Chinese manufacturer building acoustic components and MEMS microphones for mobile devices.
points.bullets:
A component manufacturer that designs and builds micro-acoustic components, including MEMS microphones, speakers, and receivers, for consumer electronics brands. It packages MEMS dies acquired from semiconductor suppliers into finished acoustic components and also produces optics, haptics, and radio frequency modules.
1. An equipment and component maker that manufactures finished MEMS microphones, speakers, and receivers sold as physical hardware integrated into consumer devices.
2. Microelectromechanical systems and miniaturized acoustic transducers built from externally sourced MEMS die technology and packaged into conductive housings that shield internal components from RF interference.
3. Audio capture via analog, digital, and differential MEMS microphones, alongside audio playback through compact receivers and speakers.
4. Finished physical acoustic components and haptic modules delivered to device assembly lines.
5. Smartphones, TWS earbuds, wearable devices, notebooks, tablets, automotive cabins, and smart home applications.
6. Consumer electronics device manufacturers and smart device brands.
7. Its packaged acoustic components are designed into smartphones and wearables by consumer electronics brands.
8. A high-volume, vertically integrated precision manufacturing operation that miniaturizes acoustic components and packages externally sourced MEMS dies into finished microphone hardware.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Sources MEMS die from semiconductor manufacturers including Infineon and Omron, holds a strategic partnership with UltraSense Systems, and serves as a primary microphone supplier to a major smartphone brand.
Organization type: A publicly traded company.
Business model: Component and hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: A Fortune China 500 company founded in 1993 with over 40,000 employees, ranking among the top three global MEMS microphone suppliers by market share.
Geography: Based in China, dominating the Asia Pacific supplier landscape and serving global smart device clients.
Beyond audio: The company creates miniaturized technology solutions across multiple domains, including optics, haptics, radio frequency, antennas, and precision manufacturing.

points.name: Akustica Inc.
points.description: Bosch-owned silicon microphone manufacturer making MEMS microphones for consumer electronics.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of silicon MEMS microphone components that supplies audio input hardware for consumer electronic devices. It builds CMOS-based MEMS microphone products integrating an acoustic sensor with a pre-amplifier and analog-to-digital converter, selling them to consumer electronics brands.
1. A semiconductor component maker that builds silicon MEMS microphones sold as finished packaged hardware integrated into customers' devices.
2. CMOS-based microelectromechanical systems integrating a MEMS acoustic sensor with a silicon integrated circuit pre-amplifier and analog-to-digital converter.
3. Voice input capture, HD voice audio sensing, and analog-to-digital signal conversion with high signal-to-noise ratio and tight sensitivity matching.
4. Finished packaged silicon hardware components distributed through global electronics distributors.
5. Mobile phones, tablets, headsets, and small wearable consumer electronic devices.
6. Consumer electronics device manufacturers.
7. Its microphone components are designed into mobile phones, tablets, and wearables by consumer electronics brands.
8. It pioneered the use of CMOS processing to build MEMS microphone devices with the diaphragm formed in the CMOS metal layer.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A wholly-owned subsidiary of Robert Bosch GmbH, distributed globally by Mouser Electronics.
Organization type: A wholly-owned subsidiary of a publicly traded global technology and engineering company.
Business model: Component hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: An established, long-standing microphone manufacturer operating as a subsidiary of a major global technology corporation.
Geography: Based in the United States and operating globally through a worldwide distribution network.
Beyond audio: Its work is entirely focused on the development and manufacturing of MEMS microphone technology.

points.name: Hosiden Corporation
points.description: Japanese supplier packaging MEMS microphones and acoustic components for consumer electronics.
points.bullets:
A component manufacturer and contract production provider that builds acoustic components including MEMS microphones, electret condenser microphones, speakers, and receivers for device makers. It buys standard MEMS die and ASICs to package under its own brand, and offers OEM, ODM, and EMS contract production services. The company supplies acoustic components to consumer electronics brands.
1. An electronic component manufacturer that builds packaged MEMS microphones, electret condenser microphones, speakers, and receivers sold as finished hardware components.
2. Standard MEMS die and ASICs packaged into microphone modules, alongside traditional electret condenser microphone and transducer designs.
3. Sound capture with minimum signal-to-noise ratios of 60dB, sound reproduction, and touch sensing.
4. Finished hardware components supplied directly to device makers.
5. Handheld game players, mobile handsets, and medical equipment.
6. Consumer electronics brands and medical device manufacturers.
7. Its packaged microphones and transducers are designed into handheld game players and handsets by consumer electronics brands.
8. It is a packaging-focused vendor that buys standard MEMS die from semiconductor suppliers to package under its own brand rather than fabricating its own MEMS die.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A customer of Infineon, a supplier to Nintendo, and a supplier to Sony.
Organization type: A publicly traded company.
Business model: Component sales and contract production services.
Scale and maturity: A company founded in 1950 with 8465 employees, ranked sixth among MEMS microphone suppliers.
Geography: Based in Japan with a subsidiary and operations extending internationally.
Beyond audio: The company produces electronic components including electromechanical connectors, display components, and wireless components, alongside contract production services.

points.name: TDK InvenSense
points.description: US semiconductor company making MEMS microphones and motion sensors for consumer electronics.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of MEMS microphones and sensor platforms that provides audio capture components for consumer electronics and industrial applications. The organization builds digital and analog microphones with proprietary algorithms and firmware for mobile, wearable, smart home, automotive, and IoT devices.
1. A semiconductor manufacturer that designs and sells finished MEMS microphone hardware used in consumer electronics.
2. MEMS sensor elements combined with CMOS technology, built-in ADCs, and bandpass filters, accompanied by proprietary firmware and Acoustic Activity Detect algorithms for ultra-low-power edge detection.
3. High signal-to-noise ratio audio capture, wide dynamic range acoustic sensing, low-power keyword and voice command detection, and acoustic activity monitoring.
4. Finished hardware components sold as digital I2S or PDM output microphones and analog output microphones in surface-mount packages.
5. Smartphones, earbuds, smart glasses, AR/VR headsets, smart home devices, industrial tools, automotive systems, robotics, and AI voice applications.
6. Consumer electronics brands, industrial device manufacturers, and automotive electronics makers.
7. Its microphone components are designed into end-user electronic devices by hardware product manufacturers.
8. Integrates proprietary ultra-low-power Acoustic Activity Detect functionality directly into the microphone hardware to support edge and generative AI systems without requiring a host processor to wake.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A subsidiary of TDK Corporation, partnered with Sonion for MEMS microphones, and its components are used in Smart Citizen kits.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand of a publicly traded electronic components manufacturer.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished MEMS microphone components and sensor platforms.
Scale and maturity: A major global player with an estimated 8 to 10 percent market share in the global MEMS microphones market.
Geography: Based in San Jose, California, USA, operating globally as part of a multinational parent corporation.
Beyond audio: The organization develops a broad range of MEMS sensor platforms beyond audio, including accelerometers, gyroscopes, compasses, pressure sensors, and ultrasonic fingerprint sensors for motion, contextual awareness, and industrial applications.

points.name: Goertek
points.description: Chinese manufacturer producing acoustic components and MEMS microphones for consumer electronics and hearables.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of electronic components and acoustic products that makes MEMS microphones and acoustic modules for consumer electronics brands.
1. A component manufacturer that builds MEMS microphones and acoustic modules sold as finished hardware parts.
2. Microelectromechanical systems and acoustic engineering used to build miniaturized microphone components with high-fidelity sound reproduction and ultra-low energy consumption.
3. High-fidelity sound reproduction, miniaturization, durability, and noise suppression.
4. Finished hardware components and modules, including analog and digital MEMS microphones.
5. Smartphones, hearables, true wireless stereo earbuds, wearables, augmented reality devices, and automotive electronics.
6. Consumer electronics brands, smartphone manufacturers, and wearable device makers.
7. Its packaged microphones are designed into consumer electronics devices by device brands.
8. High-volume advanced manufacturing capacity focused on miniaturized acoustic components.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Notable partners and customers include Apple, Samsung Electronics, Xiaomi, Qualcomm, Infineon, and Omron.
Organization type: A publicly traded company.
Business model: Component and hardware module sales.
Scale and maturity: A large established public company founded in 2001 with over 111,000 employees.
Geography: Based in China, operating globally with a primary market presence in Asia Pacific.
Beyond audio: The organization also develops augmented reality display modules, including light waveguide models, and mixed reality reference designs.

points.name: Bosch Sensortec
points.description: German sensor company making MEMS microphones and bone conduction sensors for consumer electronics and hearing aids.
points.bullets:
A MEMS sensor component supplier that develops and sells acoustic and inertial sensors, including microphones and bone conduction sensors, for consumer electronics, hearing aids, and automotive applications.
1. A sensor company that designs and manufactures microelectromechanical systems, sold as physical components that are integrated into customers' devices.
2. Microelectromechanical systems designed for high sensitivity, ultra-low power consumption, and compact form factors.
3. Sound capture using high-sensitivity microphones and voice capture through high-bandwidth bone conduction sensing.
4. The sensing products are delivered as physical hardware components distributed through electronics distributors.
5. The components are used in smartphones, hearing aids, consumer electronics wearables, and IoT devices.
6. The company sells to consumer electronics device manufacturers and automotive tier-one suppliers.
7. Its sensors are designed into consumer electronic devices and hearing aids by hardware manufacturers.
8. Its acoustic sensors combine ultra-low power consumption with compact form factors for mobile and wearable applications.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The organization partners with Fraunhofer IPMS on tooling, collaborates with Aizip on integrated algorithms, and is distributed by Mouser.
Organization type: The organization is a subsidiary of the Bosch Group.
Business model: The company generates revenue through the sale of physical hardware components.
Scale and maturity: The company is a large, established subsidiary operating within a major global technology group.
Geography: The company is based in Stuttgart, Germany, and operates internationally.
Beyond audio: The organization produces inertial and environmental MEMS sensors alongside its acoustic components.

points.name: Vesper
points.description: Boston MEMS microphone manufacturer building smart sensors for consumer wearables.
points.bullets:
A maker of acoustic components that develops piezoelectric MEMS transducer technology, manufacturing microphones and accelerometers for consumer electronics device makers.
1. A sensor company that designs piezoelectric MEMS microphones and voice accelerometers sold as finished hardware components.
2. The core technology is piezoelectric micro-electromechanical systems, using piezoelectric materials to transduce acoustic signals and skull vibrations into electrical signals.
3. The components deliver acoustic capture, wake-on-sound voice activation, bone conduction voice pickup, hardware voice activity detection, tap detection and voice authentication.
4. Customers receive the technology as finished hardware components.
5. The components are used in true wireless earbuds, wearables, smart speakers and other battery-powered voice-activated devices.
6. The company sells to consumer electronics device brands, chip companies and acoustic component suppliers.
7. Its components are designed into finished consumer devices by electronics brands and selected for development kits by chip companies.
8. The piezoelectric MEMS architecture provides inherent robustness against water, dust and extreme environments while enabling near-zero power sensing.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: AAC, Synaptics, Applied Materials, Unisem, Amazon Alexa Fund, Bose, Qualcomm, Applied Ventures and Accomplice are partners, investors or platforms integrating the components.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held startup.
Business model: The company makes money through hardware sales of its MEMS components.
Scale and maturity: The organization has raised at least $26 million in funding and is scaling manufacturing from tens of millions to hundreds of millions of units annually.
Geography: The company is based in Boston, Massachusetts, USA, and operates internationally through manufacturing and customer partnerships.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on acoustic and sensor hardware.

points.name: BSE Co. Ltd.
points.description: South Korean company making MEMS microphones for smartphones.
points.bullets:
A MEMS microphone component supplier that packages MEMS die into microphones for smartphone makers.
1. A component supplier that builds MEMS microphones sold as finished hardware embedded in consumer electronics.
2. Microelectromechanical systems fabricated on silicon die and packaged into acoustic transducers.
3. Acoustic capture through MEMS microphone components.
4. Finished microphone hardware.
5. Smartphones.
6. Smartphone makers.
7. Its microphone components are designed into smartphones by consumer electronics brands.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A semiconductor company supplies the MEMS die, and smartphone brands integrate the finished microphones.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Component hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: A company with 850 employees ranked among the top global MEMS microphone suppliers.
Geography: Based in South Korea, supplying domestic smartphone manufacturers.
Beyond audio: The organization is focused entirely on supplying MEMS microphones.

points.name: Omron Corporation
points.description: Japanese electronics company supplying MEMS microphone dies to major audio component manufacturers.
points.bullets:
A MEMS component supplier that manufactures bare MEMS microphone dies and sells them to microphone package assemblers and consumer electronics manufacturers.
1. A MEMS die manufacturer that produces bare MEMS microphone dies and sells them as unpackaged components to assemblers.
2. The core technology consists of micro-electromechanical systems silicon dies that transduce acoustic pressure into electrical signals.
3. The dies provide the acoustic transduction element for MEMS microphones.
4. Customers receive the technology as bare MEMS dies.
5. The dies are used in MEMS microphones built for consumer electronics devices.
6. The organization sells to MEMS microphone package assemblers and consumer electronics manufacturers.
7. Its bare MEMS dies are packaged with companion ASICs by other manufacturers into finished MEMS microphones.
8. The company supplies bare MEMS dies rather than fully packaged MEMS microphone components.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The organization supplies its MEMS dies to STMicroelectronics, AAC, and Goertek.
Organization type: The organization is a Japanese electronics company.
Business model: The company makes money through the sale of MEMS dies.
Scale and maturity: The organization holds a 13 percent market share in the MEMS microphone market.
Geography: The company is based in Japan.

points.name: Sensata Technologies, Inc.
points.description: UK industrial technology company making MEMS microphones for consumer electronics.
points.bullets:
An industrial technology company and component manufacturer that makes MEMS microphones for device makers.
1. A component maker whose MEMS microphones are sold as discrete hardware parts.
2. Micro-electromechanical systems transducers convert acoustic sound waves into electrical signals.
3. Acoustic sensing and audio capture.
4. Finished hardware components.
5. Electronic devices requiring audio input.
6. Device manufacturers and consumer electronics brands.
7. Its microphone components are designed into electronic devices by manufacturers.
points.profile:
Organization type: A publicly traded industrial technology company.
Business model: Component and hardware sales.
Geography: Based in Swindon, UK, operating globally.
Beyond audio: A global industrial technology company with a broad portfolio of sensors and controls beyond audio components.

points.name: Sonion A/S
points.description: Danish audio technology company designing micro-acoustic components and MEMS microphones for hearing aids and earbuds.
points.bullets:
A component manufacturer that designs and produces MEMS microphones and micro-acoustic technologies for hearing instruments, in-ear monitors, earphones, and hearables.
1. A components manufacturer that designs MEMS microphones sold as finished hardware components that run in hearable and hearing-aid devices.
2. Micro-electromechanical systems and micromechanical acoustic transducers engineered for low power consumption and small form factors.
3. Acoustic capture with high signal-to-noise ratios, high sensitivity, low noise, low current draw, and low intermodulation distortion.
4. The components are sold as finished physical microphones integrated into customers' hardware devices.
5. Hearing aids, medical communication systems, in-ear monitors, earphones, and hearables.
6. Device manufacturers producing hearables, hearing instruments, and professional audio equipment.
7. Its microphone components are designed into hearing aids and earphones by consumer electronics and medical device brands.
8. It designs MEMS microphones optimized for extremely small footprints and very low power drain suited for hearing instruments.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It co-developed MEMS microphones with TDK-InvenSense.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Hardware component sales.
Scale and maturity: An established component supplier and recognized player in the MEMS microphone market.
Geography: Based in Denmark and operating in the global audio components market.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is on micro-acoustic and micromechanical components.

points.name: Bosch
points.description: German engineering company supplying MEMS microphones and intelligent audio analytics for automotive and industrial applications.
points.bullets:
A multinational engineering and technology company that manufactures MEMS microphones and sensors, develops acoustic AI analytics platforms, and produces commercial public address systems for automotive, industrial, and enterprise markets.
1. A diversified engineering and technology company that builds MEMS microphones, acoustic AI software, and commercial audio hardware, sold as finished components, software platforms, and installed systems.
2. MEMS sensor technology, acoustic AI analytics, IP-networked audio routing, and signal processing for sound detection and public address.
3. Firearm discharge detection, siren classification, engine component acoustic monitoring, multi-zone public address, and audio amplification.
4. Packaged MEMS microphones, AI software platforms, and finished commercial audio hardware.
5. Cars, laptops, industrial facilities, security installations, commercial venues, and broadcast facilities.
6. Automakers, consumer electronics brands, industrial enterprises, security integrators, and venue operators.
7. Its microphones are designed into laptops by consumer electronics brands, its acoustic AI is integrated into automotive testing by automakers, and its commercial audio systems are installed in venues by integrators.
8. It spans the value chain from MEMS microphone components and acoustic AI datasets to finished public address hardware, leveraging cross-sector engineering expertise.
