points.name: sensiBel
points.description: Norwegian technology company developing optical MEMS microphones with high SNR and dynamic range for studio-quality audio applications.
points.bullets:
A sensor developer that designs and manufactures optical MEMS microphones and evaluation platforms for high-performance audio applications. It builds high-SNR, wide-dynamic-range digital microphones using laser interferometry instead of traditional capacitive sensing, targeting professional audio and high-end consumer electronics markets.
1. A sensor developer that designs optical MEMS microphones sold as finished components and packaged with digital ASIC output for integration into customer hardware.
2. The core technology uses laser interferometry to measure the motion of a silicon membrane, replacing legacy capacitive detection to achieve high signal-to-noise ratio and dynamic range.
3. The microphones deliver high-SNR sound acquisition up to 80-84 dBA, dynamic range up to 146 dB, 24-bit digital output, and high acoustic overload point handling up to 146 dB SPL.
4. Customers receive the technology as finished microphone components, microphone modules, and evaluation and recording platforms.
5. The microphones are used in conferencing systems, laptops, automotive systems, professional audio equipment, Ambisonics microphones for spatial audio capture, and road-noise cancellation.
6. The company sells to device makers in professional audio, consumer electronics, and automotive markets, including developers of Ambisonics microphones.
7. Its microphones are designed into hardware products by professional audio equipment brands and consumer electronics manufacturers.
8. The use of laser interferometry and optical subsystems to detect membrane motion replaces legacy capacitive MEMS sensing, enabling studio-quality performance in a microelectromechanical form factor.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Silex manufactures the MEMS element for its microphone platform, Sennheiser has made an investment, Aizip collaborates on edge AI beamforming integration, and the em64d Eigenmike is the first commercially available product using its microphones.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held deep-tech startup.
Business model: The company makes money through sales of optical MEMS microphone components and evaluation platforms.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2016 and approaching commercialization, the company was born out of SINTEF research and is expanding its team.
Geography: The company is based in Norway.

points.name: Starkey

A manufacturer of hearing aids that designs and sells finished wearable devices with embedded proprietary processors, neural-network-based audio processing and integrated health sensors for consumers with hearing loss.
