7. Its earbuds feature a dual-form-factor design with five adjustable wearing positions that allow switching between open-ear and in-ear modes.
points.profile:
Organization type: The organization is a subsidiary brand of a larger consumer electronics company.
Business model: It makes money through direct hardware sales of finished consumer electronics products.
Geography: The company operates globally and showcases products at international consumer electronics trade shows.
Beyond audio: The company operates as a dedicated audio brand within a broader consumer electronics portfolio.

points.name: Edifier
points.description: Chinese audio technology company designing and manufacturing speakers, earbuds, and gaming headsets.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer and professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures speakers, headphones, earbuds, and studio monitors for consumers, gamers, and creators. It builds finished audio hardware across personal, home, premium hi-fi, professional, and gaming categories, incorporating licensed wireless and spatial audio technologies.
1. An equipment maker that designs and manufactures finished audio hardware sold as physical products.
2. Acoustic transducers, planar magnetic drivers, balanced armatures, digital signal processing for room calibration, and integrated wireless chips form the core technology of its audio products.
3. The hardware delivers active noise cancellation, spatial audio with head tracking, room acoustic calibration, voice capture, and high-resolution audio playback.
4. Customers receive its offerings as finished hardware products.
5. The products are used in home listening setups, desktop workspaces, gaming environments, personal listening, and professional studio monitoring.
6. The company sells directly to consumers, creators, and music enthusiasts.
7. Its finished audio products are sold directly to end users through retail channels.
8. Vertically integrated design, engineering, and manufacturing capabilities allow it to produce a broad range of audio hardware spanning from budget studio monitors to premium planar magnetic headphones.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its products incorporate technology and components from THX, Qualcomm, Airoha, Bestechnic, Linkplay, and Knowles, and it operates the HECATE, STAX, and AIRPULSE brands.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held company.
Business model: The company makes money through hardware sales of finished audio products.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 1996, the company employs over 300 people and operates globally across more than 80 countries.
Geography: The company is based in Beijing, China, and operates internationally.
Beyond audio: Audio hardware is the entire focus of the organization.

points.name: JLab
points.description: [b'US consumer electronics company making affordable earbuds and headphones.']
points.bullets:
A consumer electronics company that designs and sells affordable personal audio products, including true wireless earbuds, over-ear headphones, and open-ear sports headsets, as well as over-the-counter hearing aids, for budget-conscious consumers.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished consumer audio hardware sold as packaged earbuds and headphones.
2. The products integrate wireless audio connectivity, active noise cancellation, and rechargeable battery systems into compact acoustic enclosures.
3. The audio capabilities it delivers include active noise cancellation, customizable equalization, and stereo audio for calls.
4. Customers get its audio products as finished hardware sold through retail and online channels.
5. The devices are used in personal listening, workouts, sports, and over-the-counter hearing assistance.
6. The company sells directly to consumers.
7. Its finished hardware is sold through big-box retail partners to end users.
8. The approach is distinguished by offering feature sets like active noise cancellation and open-ear designs at ultra-low-cost, budget-oriented price points.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its products are built using wireless chips from semiconductor suppliers and sold through big-box consumer electronics retailers.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held consumer electronics company.
Business model: The company makes money through hardware sales of finished audio products.
Scale and maturity: The organization was founded in 2005, has approximately 30 employees, and generates an estimated annual revenue of $10.8 million.
Geography: It is based in Carlsbad, California, USA.
Beyond audio: The company's entire focus is on consumer audio products.

points.name: Noise
points.description: Indian consumer electronics brand making wireless earbuds featuring Bose audio technology.
points.bullets:
A consumer electronics brand that designs and sells true wireless earbuds, collaborating with audio technology companies to tune and enhance its products for consumers.
1. A consumer electronics brand that makes finished true wireless earbuds sold as consumer hardware.
2. Tuning and spatial audio technologies developed in collaboration with an audio brand are integrated into the earbuds.
3. The earbuds deliver spatial audio, improved audio depth, high-frequency clarity, and adaptive sound features.
4. The technology is delivered in finished true wireless earbud hardware.
5. The products are used in true wireless earbuds.
6. The company sells to consumers.
7. Its finished earbuds are sold directly to consumers through retail channels.
8. The company combines budget and fashion-forward wearables with premium audio tuning developed in collaboration with an established audio brand.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company develops products in collaboration with Bose and uses technology from Syntiant.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held consumer electronics brand.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of true wireless earbuds.
Scale and maturity: The organization is a market-dominant wearables brand in India that was active in 2025 and introduced products for CES 2026.
Geography: The company is based in India and targets both the Indian market and a global presence for its premium products.
Beyond audio: The company focuses entirely on audio and wearable consumer electronics.

points.name: Universal Audio
points.description: US audio equipment manufacturer producing studio interfaces, software plugins, and recording microphones.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment and software that designs and manufactures audio interfaces, microphones, analog outboard gear, and digital audio workstation software. The company builds DSP-accelerated hardware and native plugins that emulate classic studio outboard processing for musicians, producers, and studios.
1. An equipment maker and software developer whose audio interfaces, microphones, and analog hardware are sold as finished physical products, and whose DSP and native plugins run on its own dedicated hardware and host computers.
2. Digital signal processing algorithms and analog circuit modeling running on embedded DSP chips within audio interfaces, alongside native audio processing algorithms for digital audio workstations.
3. Analog console, compressor, equalizer, microphone, and guitar amplifier emulation, low-latency audio conversion, microphone modeling, and digital audio workstation routing.
4. Finished hardware devices, standalone software plugins, digital audio workstation applications, and subscription services.
5. Recording studios, project studios, live sound reinforcement, and guitar amplification setups.
6. Musicians, audio engineers, producers, and recording studios.
7. Its hardware and software are sold directly to end users for studio and live sound applications.
8. It tightly integrates its DSP-accelerated audio interfaces with its custom analog modeling plugins and digital audio workstation software for low-latency recording.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It collaborated with Soundcraft on a live sound plugin integration, partnered with Sonarworks for monitor correction, and acquired Townsend Labs.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales, software licenses, and software subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: A company founded in 1958, refounded by its original founder's son, employing between 201 and 500 people.
Geography: Based in Scotts Valley, California, United States, operating in the professional audio market.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is on professional audio recording, production, and processing hardware and software.

points.name: Lewitt
points.description: Austrian microphone manufacturer building high-quality studio and live sound microphones.
points.bullets:
A microphone manufacturer that builds studio and live microphones, including true condenser and large-diaphragm condenser models, for home studios and professional users.
1. A maker of finished audio hardware sold as physical microphones and digital wireless microphone systems.
2. Condenser microphone capsules and digital wireless transmission systems with encryption and automatic frequency management.
3. Acoustic sound capture and encrypted wireless audio transmission with automatic frequency coordination.
4. Finished hardware products.
5. Home studios, professional recording studios and live sound stages.
6. Musicians, recording studios and home studio owners.
7. Its finished microphones are sold directly to recording artists and studio engineers.
points.profile:
Organization type: Privately held company.
Geography: Based in Vienna, Austria with manufacturing facilities and an anechoic chamber there.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on audio hardware manufacturing.

points.name: Sterling Audio
points.description: Pro audio manufacturer building studio microphones and accessories for music recording.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of professional studio microphones and accessories that makes ribbon, tube condenser, and large-diaphragm condenser microphones, along with shock mounts and microphone packs, for studio recording.
1. An equipment maker that designs and sells finished studio microphones and accessories as standalone hardware.
2. The core technology consists of ribbon, tube condenser, and solid-state condenser transducer designs incorporating hand-assembled capsules, custom-wound transformers, and selectable polar patterns.
3. The microphones deliver acoustic capture for vocals and instruments with various polar patterns, high SPL handling, switchable highpass filters, and attenuation pads.
4. Customers get the products as finished physical hardware, including microphones bundled with shock mounts and carry cases.
5. The devices are used in studio recording environments.
6. The company sells to musicians, audio engineers, and recording studios.
7. Its finished microphones are sold directly to end users for studio recording setups.
points.profile:
Organization type: The organization is a manufacturer.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of microphones and accessories.
Beyond audio: Audio is the entire focus of the organization.

points.name: Royer Labs
points.description: Burbank, California microphone manufacturer building ribbon microphones for recording studios and live sound.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of professional ribbon microphones for recording studios, broadcast facilities, live sound environments, and film and television production.
1. An equipment maker that builds professional ribbon microphones sold as finished hardware for use with analog and phantom-powered audio interfaces.
2. Ribbon microphone transducers using neodymium magnets, offset ribbon motors, and active phantom-powered or tube electronics.
3. High SPL handling, smooth high-frequency response, warm and realistic tone reproduction, and stereo or mono sound capture.
4. Finished microphone hardware.
5. Recording studios, broadcast facilities, live sound stages, and film and television production.
6. Studios and musicians, broadcast facilities, and live sound engineers.
7. Its finished microphones are used directly by engineers and producers in recording, broadcast, and live sound settings.
8. It hand-builds rugged ribbon microphones and produces phantom-powered active ribbon designs.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Sounds Great Holdings.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: An established manufacturer that has won a Technical Grammy Award.
Geography: Based in Burbank, California, USA, expanding globally.
Beyond audio: The company focuses entirely on ribbon microphones and related audio technologies.

points.name: Peluso Microphone Lab
points.description: Boutique microphone manufacturer hand-crafting replicas of vintage designs and supplying aftermarket parts for audio recording.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of professional microphones and aftermarket components that engineers original condenser and ribbon designs to replicate the acoustic character of vintage recording microphones, selling finished hand-built hardware and replacement capsules to recording studios and audio enthusiasts.
1. An equipment maker that builds microphones and aftermarket capsules sold as finished hardware and physical components.
2. Hand-crafted true condenser, ribbon, vacuum tube, solid-state and transformer-based analog audio transducer designs.
3. Acoustic sound capture, vintage microphone sound replication, and aftermarket capsule replacement for large-diaphragm condenser microphones.
4. Finished microphone hardware, aftermarket condenser capsules, output transformers, and vintage microphone restoration services.
5. Recording studios and audio production environments.
6. Recording studios, musicians, audio enthusiasts, DIY microphone builders, and professional audio dealers.
7. Its finished microphones and components are sold through professional audio dealers to recording engineers and studio owners.
8. It engineers original components to replicate the acoustic resonance of specific vintage microphone designs without directly copying the original manufacturing, avoiding direct competition with legacy brands.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Products are sold through dealers including Thomann, RSPE Audio Solutions, Tidepool Audio, and Rock N Roll Rentals.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished microphones, aftermarket components, and vintage restoration services.
Scale and maturity: An established organization with 25 years of microphone design experience and 50 years of vintage microphone restoration experience.
Geography: Based in the United States with products distributed through a global dealer network.
Beyond audio: Audio hardware manufacturing and restoration is the organization's entire focus.

points.name: Neumann
points.description: Berlin manufacturer building condenser microphones and studio monitors.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that manufactures studio microphones, studio monitors, headphones, audio interfaces, and preamps for recording, broadcast, and live applications.
1. An equipment maker that designs and builds finished microphones, monitor speakers, audio interfaces, and headphones, sold as standalone hardware.
2. Condenser microphone capsules and vacuum tube or solid-state electronics, bi-amplified monitor speakers with analog Class AB amplifiers and digital signal processing, and binaural dummy head recording systems.
3. Sound capture using switchable polar patterns, high sound pressure level handling, low self-noise, binaural 3D audio recording, and DSP-based room correction for nearfield and midfield monitoring.
4. Finished hardware products, including standalone microphones, powered speakers, audio interfaces, and companion calibration software and control applications.
5. Professional recording studios, broadcast studios, post-production facilities, live sound stages, and project studios.
6. Studios and musicians, broadcast engineers, live sound engineers, and audio professionals.
7. Its finished hardware products are used directly by engineers and artists in professional audio production environments.
8. It manufactures iconic studio condenser microphones with a decades-long history and combines modern DSP room correction with hand assembly and rigorous quality control.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It is part of Sennheiser's pro audio division and collaborated with Merging Technologies to develop a premium audio interface.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand of a privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales of professional audio equipment.
Scale and maturity: A long-established brand founded in 1928 with a globally recognized market position.
Geography: Based in Berlin, Germany, with global distribution.
Beyond audio: The organization is a pure-play professional audio company.

points.name: CORSAIR
points.description: US public company manufacturing high-performance gaming headsets and audio gear for PC gamers and content creators.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer and creator hardware that builds gaming headsets and related gear for gamers, content creators, and PC enthusiasts.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished gaming headsets sold as consumer hardware.
2. The headsets deliver balanced sound tuning and user-adjustable, cloud-synced equalizer profiles that stay consistent across devices.
3. Customers receive it as finished hardware products.
4. The devices are used in PC gaming and content creation setups.
5. The company sells to consumers.
6. Its finished hardware is sold direct to consumers through retail channels.
points.profile:
Organization type: It is a publicly traded company that owns subsidiary brands.
Business model: The company makes money through hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: It is an established, large-scale public company.
Geography: It is based in the United States and operates globally.
Beyond audio: The company develops and manufactures a broad range of high-performance computer peripherals, streaming gear, and PC components beyond audio.

points.name: Behringer
points.description: German audio equipment manufacturer building budget-friendly digital mixing consoles and professional microphones.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures a broad range of hardware including analog and digital mixing consoles, audio interfaces, amplifiers, loudspeakers, microphones, synthesizers, and signal processors, targeting budget-conscious consumers and entry-level production markets.
1. An equipment maker that designs finished audio hardware products which are sold as physical units to users.
2. The company utilizes digital signal processing for its digital mixers and acoustic engineering for its loudspeakers, microphones, and analog preamps, manufacturing drivers, cabinets, and internal crossovers in-house.
3. Its products deliver audio mixing, signal routing, recording, amplification, sound reinforcement, equalization, dynamic compression, and feedback suppression.
4. Customers get its technology as finished hardware products, including rack-mounted and console mixers, USB audio interfaces, powered speakers, and outboard gear.
5. Its equipment is used in home studios, live sound venues, small conference rooms, podcasting setups, public address systems, and DJ booths.
6. The company sells to consumers, home studio owners, emerging venues, small production companies, and retail music stores.
7. Its finished audio products are sold directly to end users through musical instrument and pro audio retailers.
8. The company distinguishes itself through aggressive pricing of professional-grade audio gear, leveraging mass production in its own dedicated manufacturing facility to undercut premium competitors.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It operates under the Music Tribe parent company alongside the Midas, Klark Teknik, and Turbosound brands, and integrates networking technology from Waves and reverb algorithms from TC Electronic into its consoles.
Organization type: The organization is a subsidiary brand operating under a privately held parent conglomerate.
Business model: The company makes money through the sale of finished physical audio hardware.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 1989, the company has grown into a high-volume manufacturer, ranking as the fourteenth largest musical instrument manufacturer globally by sales.
Geography: The company is based in Germany and operates a massive manufacturing facility in China.
Beyond audio: Audio hardware manufacturing is its sole focus.

points.name: EASTECH
points.description: Speaker driver manufacturer producing specialized transducers designed to achieve perfect time coherence and superior sound quality.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of loudspeaker transducers that produces a family of point-source speaker drivers designed by a licensor partner, for speaker brands and audio equipment makers.
1. A speaker driver manufacturer that builds loudspeaker transducers, sold as finished hardware components for integration into speaker systems.
2. Pulp cones reinforced with carbon fiber material and point-source transducer designs engineered for time coherence.
3. Sound reproduction with increased stiffness, lower distortion and time coherence.
4. Finished speaker driver components.
5. Speakers and audio systems.
6. Speaker brands and audio equipment makers.
7. Its manufactured transducers are built into speaker systems by audio brands.
8. Its point-source transducers are engineered to achieve time coherence while using pulp cones with patented carbon fiber material for stiffness and low distortion.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The transducer designs are licensed from the speaker driver design company ScanSpeak.
Organization type: Privately held manufacturer.
Business model: Component hardware sales.
Geography: Operates as a manufacturer producing transducer hardware.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on the manufacture of acoustic transducers.

points.name: USound
points.description: Austrian audio component company developing ultra-compact MEMS microspeakers for hearables and wireless earbuds.
points.bullets:
A fabless audio component company that designs and manufactures piezoelectric MEMS microspeakers, audio amplifier ICs and integrated audio modules for consumer electronics brands and contract manufacturers building hearables.
1. A component maker that designs silicon-based MEMS drivers and audio amplifiers, sold as finished components and integrated modules that run inside earbuds and hearing aids.
2. Piezoelectric micro-electromechanical systems using PZT cantilevers to convert electrical signals into acoustic energy, paired with energy recovery amplifiers to reduce power consumption.
3. High-frequency sound reproduction up to ultrasonic bandwidths, spatial audio rendering, ultrasonic gesture sensing, low distortion and miniaturized acoustic output.
4. Finished hardware components, audio amplifier integrated circuits, integrated audio modules and reference designs provided to device manufacturers.
5. True wireless earbuds, over-the-counter hearing aids and premium hearables.
6. Consumer electronics brands, hearing aid manufacturers, original design manufacturers and contract manufacturers.
7. Its MEMS components and audio modules are designed into hearable products by consumer electronics brands and contract manufacturers.
8. It combines piezoelectric MEMS transducers with energy recovery audio amplifiers to achieve radical miniaturization and power reduction compared to conventional electrodynamic drivers.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Named partners and customers include Luxshare-ICT, OBO Pro2, Soranik, QCY, Earweiss, Minami, Nordic Neuro Lab, ASE and Digi-key, with funding from EQventure.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Hardware component sales and integrated module sales to device manufacturers.
Scale and maturity: A Series B company founded in 2014 that has raised $83.8 million and holds over 370 patents.
Geography: Based in Austria and operating globally through international manufacturing and distribution partners.
Beyond audio: It focuses entirely on audio technology, with no operations outside the field.

points.name: Luxshare-ICT
points.description: Chinese manufacturer assembling TWS earbuds and developing compact hybrid audio modules.
points.bullets:
A consumer electronics manufacturer that builds parts, modules and systems for global brands, and assembles finished devices such as earbuds, smart speakers and wearables for device makers.
1. An electronics manufacturer that builds integrated audio modules and finished consumer devices, sold as assembled hardware and components to device brands.
2. Microelectromechanical speakers, microspeakers, amplifiers and MEMS microphones integrated into compact hybrid audio modules for true wireless earbuds.
3. Dual-driver audio output, amplification and microphone capture in miniaturized earbud modules.
4. Components, modules and finished assembled hardware built in manufacturing facilities for consumer electronics brands.
5. True wireless earbuds, headphones, smart speakers, wearables, virtual reality headsets and automotive electronics.
6. Consumer electronics brands, device makers and ODM partners that integrate modules or sell finished assembled devices.
7. Its modules and assembly services are integrated by consumer electronics brands into their earbuds and wearables.
8. It combines high-volume contract manufacturing scale with integrated module development built around strategic MEMS speaker supply partnerships.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Apple for AirPods assembly and USound for MEMS speaker supply in hybrid audio modules.
Organization type: Privately held contract manufacturer and ODM.
Business model: Manufacturing services, component and module sales, and assembled hardware production for consumer electronics brands.
Scale and maturity: One of the largest consumer electronics manufacturers and assemblers, operating multiple facilities across Asia.
Geography: Based in China with manufacturing operations in China and Vietnam.
Beyond audio: It provides integrated intelligent solutions, parts, modules and systems across enterprise infrastructure, consumer electronics and automotive markets.

points.name: Creative
points.description: Singapore consumer audio company making wireless earbuds and Bluetooth accessories with emerging solid-state speaker technology.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer audio equipment that develops and sells finished hardware products, including wireless earbuds, headphones, sound cards, and Bluetooth transmitters, incorporating proprietary spatial audio processing and solid-state MEMS drivers for consumers.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished audio hardware and proprietary spatial audio DSP technology, sold as consumer devices and companion software applications running on mobile platforms and embedded dongles.
2. Computational audio algorithms using head-related transfer function personalization via ear and head photography, running on embedded UltraDSP processors, alongside integrated solid-state MEMS speaker drivers.
3. Personalized holographic spatial audio rendering, simulated room reverberation, active noise cancellation, ambient sound modes, and high-resolution wireless audio transmission.
4. Finished hardware products, including earbuds, headsets, and transmitter dongles, along with a free mobile application for custom sound profile generation.
5. Consumer wireless earbuds, gaming headsets, PC sound cards, home entertainment soundbars, and portable headphone amplifiers.
6. Consumers and gamers.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to consumers, integrating components and licensed technologies from upstream driver and audio personalization providers.
8. It uses ear and head photography to generate custom head-related transfer function profiles for personalized headphone holography.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: xMEMS supplies solid-state MEMS drivers, and Mimi provides sound personalization technology.
Organization type: A publicly traded consumer electronics company.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished consumer audio devices and accessories.
Scale and maturity: A long-established company founded in the 1980s with a historical user base of 400 million.
Geography: Based in Singapore and operating globally.
Beyond audio: The company focuses entirely on digital entertainment and audio products.

points.name: MISCO
points.description: Minnesota speaker manufacturer building microspeakers and audio systems for aerospace, defense, medical, and commercial applications.
points.bullets:
A speaker manufacturer that designs and builds loudspeakers and complete audio systems for original equipment manufacturers. The company produces microspeakers and audio components under two inches in diameter, along with larger speaker systems, for industrial, commercial, and aerospace applications.
1. An equipment maker that builds speaker components and finished audio systems sold as hardware to other manufacturers.
2. The company delivers acoustic transduction and sound reproduction from small-form-factor microspeakers and larger audio systems.
3. Customers receive physical speaker components and audio systems as finished hardware.
4. The products are used in casino gaming systems, mass transit, medical devices, military and defense communication systems, aerospace systems including spacecraft, wearable devices, IoT products, portable communications equipment, and professional audio installations.
5. The company sells to original equipment manufacturers across industrial, commercial, aerospace, and defense markets.
6. Its speaker components are designed into finished products by original equipment manufacturers across various industries.
7. The company maintains over 75 years of operation and ISO 9001:2015 certified manufacturing facilities, with components deployed in aerospace applications including NASA spacecraft.
points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held manufacturer.
Business model: The company makes money through hardware sales of speaker components and audio systems.
Scale and maturity: The organization has operated for over 75 years and maintains certified manufacturing facilities in Minnesota and Asia.
Geography: The company is based in Minnesota, USA, and operates manufacturing facilities in Asia.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on the design and manufacturing of audio components and systems.

points.name: SEAS
points.description: Norwegian loudspeaker manufacturer making audio drivers and tweeters.
points.bullets:
A loudspeaker driver manufacturer that designs and produces audio components for consumer electronics brands and professional audio equipment makers.
1. An audio component maker that designs and manufactures loudspeaker drivers sold as finished components to equipment manufacturers.
2. The company designs acoustic transducers using materials such as carbon composites for tweeters and other driver architectures.
3. The company delivers acoustic transduction components including tweeters, woofers and full-range drivers.
4. Customers get its products as finished loudspeaker drivers built into the customers' speaker systems.
5. Its drivers are used in wireless speaker systems, passive loudspeakers and professional studio monitors.
6. The company sells to consumer electronics brands and professional audio equipment makers.
7. Its drivers are designed into finished speaker systems by consumer audio brands and professional equipment manufacturers.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Named partners include a portable audio electronics brand and a professional audio equipment maker.
Organization type: The organization is a manufacturer.
Business model: It makes money through component sales of loudspeaker drivers.
Scale and maturity: The company was founded in 1948 and has operated for decades as an established driver manufacturer.
Geography: It is based in Norway.
Beyond audio: The company's entire focus is audio component manufacturing.

points.name: Dynaudio
points.description: Danish speaker manufacturer building studio monitors, hi-fi speakers, and premium automotive audio systems.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment and consumer loudspeakers that manufactures passive studio monitors, hi-fi speakers, and individual speaker drivers for recording professionals and audio enthusiasts.
1. A loudspeaker manufacturer that builds finished passive speakers and speaker drivers, sold as physical hardware in studios and homes.
2. Passive loudspeaker designs incorporating cast aluminum baskets and DDC crossover systems for controlled directivity and beam control.
3. Sound reproduction with technical neutrality, controlled directivity, and beam control.
4. Customers get it as finished hardware: studio monitors, hi-fi speakers, and speaker drivers.
5. The devices and products it is used in are mastering studios and home hi-fi setups.
6. The types of customer it sells to are recording professionals, mastering engineers, and audio enthusiasts.
7. Its finished speakers are installed in studios and homes by professionals and consumers.
8. What distinguishes its approach is a focus on technical neutrality and DDC crossover technology for controlled directivity.
points.profile:
Organization type: The organization is a privately held manufacturer.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of finished loudspeakers and drivers.
Geography: It is based in Denmark.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: Audio Engineering Society
points.description: New York-based professional society developing audio standards and publishing engineering research.
points.bullets:
A professional society and standards body that develops technical standards, recommendations and information documents for the audio industry, and organizes conventions and conferences for audio engineers and related professionals.
1. A standards body that develops technical specifications and recommended practices, delivered as published documents and online portals, that engineers and manufacturers adopt in professional broadcast, studio and online audio systems.
2. Technical specifications and recommended practices for digital audio interconnect, audio-over-IP interoperability, loudness measurement, embedded audio metadata, loudspeaker measurement and spatial acoustic data file formats.
3. Standardized digital audio transmission, audio-over-IP network interoperability, streaming and broadcast loudness normalization, dialogue intelligibility, loudspeaker maximum sound level measurement and spatially oriented acoustic data storage.
4. Published technical standards, recommended practices and educational web portals accessed via subscription services and online libraries.
5. Professional and broadcast equipment, online streaming platforms, loudspeaker systems, automotive audio systems, virtual and augmented reality systems and digital microphones.
6. Audio engineers, broadcast professionals, device makers, automakers, software manufacturers and standards contributors.
7. Its standards are adopted and implemented by equipment manufacturers and broadcasters into their professional audio products and workflows.
8. It is the principal international professional society devoted exclusively to audio technology, combining standards development with peer-reviewed publishing and industry conventions.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The European Broadcasting Union, Samsung, Telos Alliance, Yamaha, Genelec and NAB Show.
Organization type: A professional society and standards body.
Business model: Membership dues, convention registrations and subscription services for standards access.
Scale and maturity: A long-established global organization that hosts multiple international conventions annually and publishes the Journal of the Audio Engineering Society.
Geography: Based in New York, USA, and operating internationally.
Beyond audio: It is a pure-play audio organization whose entire focus is audio engineering, standards and education.

points.name: Tymphany
points.description: Taiwanese audio manufacturer designing transducers, amplifiers, and integrated acoustic systems for consumer, professional, and automotive audio applications.
points.bullets:
An original design manufacturer and audio equipment maker that designs and manufactures loudspeakers, audio systems, acoustic transducers, and DSP platforms for consumer, professional, conference, and automotive applications.
1. An equipment maker and original design manufacturer that builds transducers, finished audio systems, and DSP tuning software, sold as manufactured hardware and design services to brands.
2. Acoustic transducers, including coaxially arranged diaphragms and ring radiator designs, paired with integrated DSP software and acoustic system design.
3. It delivers physical sound reproduction, acoustic system integration, audio tuning, and spatial audio deployment through integrated hardware and software.
4. Customers receive finished hardware products, manufactured components, reference designs, and software tuning tools.
5. Its products are used in WiFi and Bluetooth speakers, soundbars, automotive audio systems, in-vehicle headrest speakers, personal computers, and conference room systems.
6. The company sells to consumer electronics brands, PC and peripheral manufacturers, and automotive makers.
7. Its manufactured audio systems and transducers are branded and sold by consumer electronics and automotive companies.
8. It operates a holistic approach that integrates transducer design, amplifier, DSP, acoustic system, and mechanical engineering into a single manufacturing service.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It collaborates with Fraunhofer IIS to integrate upHear spatial audio technologies and licenses technologies from Bluacs, operating under the Primax Tymphany Group.
Organization type: It is an original design manufacturer and subsidiary brand.
Business model: It makes money through hardware manufacturing, component sales, and original design manufacturing services.
Scale and maturity: The organization has over ninety years of experience and employs over eight thousand people globally.
Geography: It is headquartered in Nangang District, Taiwan, and operates globally.
Beyond audio: Audio design, development, and manufacturing is its entire focus.

points.name: B&O
points.description: Danish consumer audio manufacturer designing high-end loudspeakers and truly wireless earbuds.
points.bullets:
A consumer electronics company that manufactures high-end audio products, including truly wireless earbuds and loudspeakers, for consumers.
1. A maker of finished audio hardware that sells loudspeakers and earbuds as completed physical products.
2. Acoustic loudspeaker designs, including long-running models developed with external simulation support.
3. High-end sound reproduction for home listening and personal audio.
4. The company provides finished hardware products sold directly to end users.
5. Its products are used in home audio settings and personal listening environments.
6. The company sells to consumers seeking premium audio equipment.
7. Its finished hardware is sold directly to consumers through its own retail channels and brand presence.
8. It distinguishes itself through long-lived, premium loudspeaker designs developed with specialized external acoustic simulation support.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It engaged acoustic simulation consultant Peter Larsen for speaker design support.
Organization type: It is a consumer electronics brand operating as a subsidiary.
Business model: It makes money through the sale of finished audio hardware.
Geography: The organization is based in Denmark.
Beyond audio: The company focuses entirely on consumer audio and related electronics.

points.name: OBO Pro2
points.location: Taiwan; manufacturing operations in Dongguan, China
points.description: Taiwanese audio manufacturer designing OTC hearing aids and building audio modules using silicone rubber and MEMS technology.
points.bullets:
An audio manufacturer that provides OEM and ODM services for hearing aids, specializing in silicone rubber technology for electrodynamic drivers and integrating components into finished devices for hearing aid brands.
1. A manufacturer of finished audio hardware that designs and assembles OTC hearing aids and electrodynamic drivers for sale as complete devices to brand owners.
2. The company delivers electrodynamic driver design and full hearing aid component integration into user-friendly finished devices.
3. Customers get finished hearing aid hardware manufactured under OEM or ODM arrangements.
4. The devices are used in OTC hearing aids.
5. The company sells to hearing aid brands and audio module developers.
6. Its finished devices and manufactured components are branded and sold by consumer health and audio companies.
7. Its approach combines silicone rubber electrodynamic driver expertise with full-device OTC hearing aid integration under one manufacturing roof.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company has a strategic cooperation with a MEMS technology developer and participates in an OTC hearing aid reference design collaboration.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held manufacturer.
Business model: It makes money through OEM and ODM contract manufacturing of finished hearing aid devices and components.
Geography: The company is headquartered in Taiwan with manufacturing operations in Dongguan, China.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: Singularity Audio
points.description: Audio company designing in-ear monitors using MEMS speaker technology.
points.bullets:
A maker of finished audio equipment that designs in-ear monitors incorporating micro-electromechanical speaker drivers, sold to consumers and audiophiles.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished in-ear monitors sold as physical hardware.
2. Micro-electromechanical system drivers enclosed in a titanium shell.
3. Personal audio monitoring and playback.
4. Finished hardware products.
5. In-ear monitors used for personal listening and professional monitoring.
6. Consumers and audiophiles.
7. Its finished earphones are designed around micro-electromechanical speaker drivers supplied by a component manufacturer.
8. It builds in-ear monitors using twin micro-electromechanical drivers in a titanium shell.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company is a launch partner for xMEMS.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on audio equipment.

points.name: iFi
points.description: English audio equipment manufacturer building portable and desktop DACs and headphone amplifiers.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer and professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures portable and desktop DACs, headphone amplifiers, and streaming components for personal audio enthusiasts.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished digital-to-analog converters, headphone amplifiers, and Bluetooth streamers sold as standalone consumer hardware.
2. Digital-to-analog conversion chips, analogue amplification circuits, and Bluetooth streaming technology paired with bespoke firmware running on input processing microcontrollers.
3. Digital-to-analog conversion, headphone amplification, high-resolution audio decoding, wireless Bluetooth streaming, and phono signal amplification.
4. Finished hardware products, including pocket-sized dongles, transportable devices, and desktop units.
5. Desktop hi-fi systems, headphone listening setups, smartphone and laptop audio enhancement, and two-channel home audio systems.
6. Consumers and personal audio enthusiasts.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold through consumer electronics retailers to end users.
8. It programs input processing chips with bespoke firmware rather than off-the-shelf code and uses internal batteries in dongle converters to avoid draining source devices.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It is an official DAC and headphone amp technology partner for xMEMS and uses components from Burr-Brown, XMOS, Texas Instruments, and TDK.
Organization type: Privately held manufacturer and audio brand.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: An established manufacturer with a broad product portfolio spanning multiple price tiers.
Geography: Based in England.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: Soranik
points.description: Vietnamese in-ear monitor manufacturer building audio products for performers using MEMS drivers.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures in-ear monitors for audio enthusiasts and performers. The organization builds finished earphones that incorporate micro-electromechanical systems drivers sourced from component suppliers. It creates products that combine different driver technologies in hybrid designs.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished in-ear monitor hardware sold to end users.
2. Hybrid micro-electromechanical systems driver configurations combining separate monolithic and tweeter elements within 3D-printed acoustic shells.
3. Personal audio monitoring with combined high-frequency and monolithic driver reproduction.
4. The company delivers finished hardware products retailing directly to consumers.
5. The products are used in in-ear monitors for audio enthusiasts and live performers.
6. The organization sells to consumers, audio enthusiasts and performers.
7. Its finished earphones are built using micro-electromechanical driver components sourced from upstream component suppliers.
8. The approach distinguishes itself by combining two different types of micro-electromechanical systems drivers from separate suppliers within a single hybrid in-ear monitor design.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company uses micro-electromechanical systems drivers from USound and xMEMS and operates as an original design manufacturer collaborating with USound.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held manufacturer.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of finished earphones.
Scale and maturity: The company was established in 2012 and operates as a manufacturer of premium in-ear monitors retailing at over one thousand US dollars.
Geography: It is based in Vietnam.
Beyond audio: Audio is the entire focus of the organization.

points.name: Arioso Systems
points.description: German startup developing miniaturized MEMS microspeakers for in-ear devices.
points.bullets:
A MEMS microspeaker IP developer that designs miniaturized electrostatic transducers for in-ear audio devices. It licenses its patented Nanoscopic Electrostatic Drive principle and MEMS microspeaker technology to audio device manufacturers. The company creates compact acoustic components capable of generating high sound pressure levels from small active areas.
1. An IP licensor that designs MEMS microspeaker transducers and licenses the underlying electrostatic drive technology to chip and device manufacturers for integration into their hardware.
2. Nanoscopic electrostatic drive technology that powers miniaturized MEMS microspeakers, using electrostatic forces to generate sound pressure levels up to 120dB SPL from a 10mm² active area.
3. High sound pressure level audio reproduction from miniaturized MEMS microspeaker components.
4. Patented IP and microspeaker designs licensed to manufacturers for integration into semiconductors and audio hardware.
5. In-ear audio devices requiring miniaturized high-output microspeakers.
6. Audio device manufacturers and semiconductor companies integrating MEMS microspeaker technology into their products.
7. Its transducer IP and designs are integrated by semiconductor and device manufacturers into miniaturized audio hardware.
8. Its nanoscopic electrostatic drive principle enables higher sound pressure levels from smaller active areas than conventional microspeaker approaches.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A Fraunhofer IPMS spin-off acquired by Bosch Sensortec.
Organization type: A startup acquired by a semiconductor and sensor company, originally spun out of a research institute.
Geography: Based in Dresden, Germany.
Beyond audio: It focuses entirely on miniaturized MEMS microspeaker technology.

points.name: SonicEdge
points.description: Audio technology company developing modulated ultrasound MEMS microspeakers for earbuds and hearing aids.
points.bullets:
A MEMS microspeaker IP and component developer that builds modulated ultrasound speakers for hearables, licensing its technology to audio chipsets and collaborating on custom-fit earbuds.
1. A MEMS microspeaker developer whose modulated ultrasound technology is embedded in partners' audio chipsets and sold as packaged evaluation devices.
2. Silicon MEMS technology that generates sound by modulating ultrasound waves.
3. High-performance audio output in microsized speakers and integrated speaker-microphone functionality in a single package.
4. The technology is delivered as licensed IP embedded in audio chipsets, packaged MEMS evaluation devices, and integrated components for true wireless earbuds.
5. The devices are used in true wireless stereo earbuds, headphones, and hearing aids.
6. The organization sells to audio chip companies, hearable manufacturers, and developers of custom-fit earbuds.
7. Its IP is embedded into audio chipsets by semiconductor makers and its components are integrated into earbuds by consumer electronics brands.
8. It replaces conventional speaker technology with a second-generation modulated ultrasound approach to achieve high audio quality in a microsized form factor.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company collaborates with a custom-fit earbuds developer and has a strategic partnership with a major global semiconductor maker.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held startup.
Business model: It makes money through IP licensing and packaged device sales.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2019, the company holds proprietary patents and is seeking investment for expansion.
Geography: It is based in Israel.
Beyond audio: It is a pure-play audio company focused entirely on MEMS microspeaker technology.

points.name: Earweiss
points.description: Shenzhen manufacturer building advanced earbuds and hearables that integrate MEMS speaker technology.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of earbuds and hearables that builds finished personal audio hardware for consumers.
1. An equipment maker that builds earbuds and hearables sold as finished hardware products.
2. The core technology consists of personalization and advanced hearable systems integrating MEMS speaker technology.
3. The organization delivers personalization and advanced hearable capabilities in personal audio devices.
4. Customers receive finished hardware products.
5. The products are used in earbuds and hearables.
6. The company sells to consumers.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to end users.
8. Its approach is distinguished by integrating MEMS speaker technology into hearable products.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The organization has a strategic partnership with USound to explore MEMS speaker integration.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held manufacturer.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: The company is an established manufacturer with R&D operations.
Geography: It is based in Shenzhen, China with R&D in Nanjing, China.
Beyond audio: Audio is the entire focus of the company.

points.name: QCY
points.description: Chinese wireless audio manufacturer producing affordable Bluetooth earbuds and true wireless earbuds.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer audio equipment that designs, manufactures and sells wireless earbuds and headphones, integrating drivers and acoustic systems for consumers.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished wireless earbuds and headphones sold as packaged consumer electronics.
2. Dynamic and MEMS drivers configured in dual-driver acoustic systems, combined with adaptive hybrid active noise cancellation.
3. Active noise cancellation, high-resolution audio playback and dual-driver sound reproduction with bass and treble separation.
4. Finished consumer hardware products.
5. True wireless stereo earbuds and over-ear headphones.
6. Consumers.
7. Its finished earbuds are sold to consumers through retail channels, incorporating MEMS speakers designed by its component suppliers.
8. It targets the low-to-mid-tier price segment with affordable wireless audio solutions built through efficient supply chains.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It collaborates with USound and uses xMEMS drivers.
Organization type: A brand and subsidiary of a privately held electronics manufacturer.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: An established brand with over 16 years of industry experience and millions of users worldwide.
Geography: Based in China and operating globally.
Beyond audio: It focuses entirely on wireless audio products.

points.name: Soundpeats
points.description: Chinese audio brand manufacturing budget-friendly wireless earbuds and headphones.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer audio equipment that builds budget-friendly wireless earbuds and headphones for consumers, integrating components from silicon suppliers into finished products.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished wireless audio hardware sold to consumers.
2. Wireless audio playback systems combining dynamic drivers, silicon-based micro tweeters, multi-driver acoustic architectures, and adaptive hybrid active noise cancellation.
3. Wireless audio playback, active noise cancellation, multi-driver sound reproduction, adaptive equalization, hearing test-based sound personalization, and dual-device connectivity.
4. Finished hardware devices paired with a companion mobile software application.
5. Wireless earbuds and over-ear headphones.
6. Consumers.
7. Its finished hardware products incorporate components designed by semiconductor vendors and are sold directly to end users.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: xMEMS Labs.
Organization type: A privately held company operating as a consumer electronics brand.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished audio devices.
Geography: Based in China and operating in the consumer electronics market.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on audio products.

points.name: Dongguan Rayking Electronics
points.description: Dongguan manufacturer building microphones and turnkey speaker modules for wireless earbuds.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of electret condenser microphones, MEMS microphones and turnkey speaker modules, building intelligent acoustic components and automotive modules for consumer electronics and automotive device makers.
1. An equipment and component maker that builds microphones and integrated speaker modules sold as finished hardware components designed into customers' devices.
2. Electret condenser microphone and MEMS microphone technology combined with integrated speaker module design that packages drivers and all external components into a single covered unit.
3. Acoustic capture through electret and MEMS microphones and audio output through turnkey speaker modules for true wireless earbuds.
4. Finished acoustic hardware components and turnkey speaker modules.
5. True wireless earbuds and automotive electronics.
6. Consumer electronics device makers and automakers.
7. Its acoustic components and speaker modules are designed into true wireless earbuds and automotive modules by consumer electronics brands.
points.profile:
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Hardware component sales.
Scale and maturity: Established in 2011 and operating as a component manufacturer.
Geography: Based in Dongguan, China.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is on acoustic components and modules.

points.name: Noble Audio
points.description: Premium in-ear monitor brand crafting audiophile earbuds featuring hybrid MEMS and dynamic drivers.
points.bullets:
A maker of premium portable audio equipment that designs and sells in-ear monitors and true wireless earbuds for audiophiles.
1. An equipment maker whose finished wireless earbuds and wired in-ear monitors run as consumer electronics devices.
2. Hybrid driver acoustics pairing solid-state MEMS tweeters with dynamic drivers, integrated with Bluetooth codecs and companion software.
3. High-fidelity audio reproduction, active noise cancellation, transparent hearing modes, multi-point Bluetooth connectivity, and voice assistant support.
4. Finished consumer hardware products.
5. True wireless earbuds and wired in-ear monitors.
6. Consumers and audiophiles.
7. Its finished earbuds are sold directly to end users.
8. It combines solid-state silicon tweeters with dynamic drivers in true wireless earbuds targeting the audiophile market.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: xMEMS and Qualcomm.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: An established manufacturer with an award-winning product portfolio and an entry-level tier.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is on audio.

points.name: U.S. Food and Drug Administration
points.description: US government agency regulating over-the-counter hearing aids for adults with mild to moderate hearing loss.
points.bullets:
A government agency that regulates medical devices, including establishing and enforcing the regulatory framework for over-the-counter hearing aids and clearing audio-related software and hardware devices for consumer use.
1. A regulatory body that establishes medical device categories and clears finished audio hardware and software for market entry.
2. Regulatory approval pathways including Traditional 510(k) and De Novo classifications are applied to evaluate the safety and efficacy of audio devices.
3. The agency evaluates and clears audio features such as over-the-counter hearing aid functions and wheeze detection.
4. Manufacturers receive market clearance and regulatory authorization to sell their devices and software features to consumers.
5. Clearances apply to devices including earbuds, hearing aids, cochlear implants, and digital stethoscopes.
6. The organization regulates device manufacturers, consumer electronics brands, and medical device companies.
7. Its regulations govern the market entry of products developed by device manufacturers and consumer electronics brands.
8. The agency creates and enforces the legal categories that allow consumer audio devices to be marketed and sold as medical devices.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Named regulated entities include consumer electronics and medical device manufacturers such as Apple, Samsung, Eko Health, TytoCare, Solventum, Envoy Medical, Sonova, and Knowles.
Organization type: A United States federal government agency.
Business model: The agency is publicly funded through federal appropriations.
Scale and maturity: A federal agency with jurisdiction over the entire United States market.
Geography: Based and operates within the United States.
Beyond audio: The organization regulates a broad range of products beyond audio, including food, veterinary drugs, biological products, and various human medical devices.

points.name: Lucid Hearing
points.description: Illinois parent company selling over-the-counter hearing aids, hearing protection devices, and professional in-ear monitors.
points.bullets:
A maker of hearing health and consumer audio equipment that designs, manufactures, and sells OTC and prescription hearing aids, hearing protection products, and companion apps, and operates hearing clinics for consumers.
1. An equipment maker that designs and sells finished hearing aids and hearing protection hardware, sold as retail devices and worn in the ear or behind the ear, and operates in-store fitting clinics.
2. Digital sound processing platforms running on low-power hearing aid chips, using adaptive dynamic range optimization, multi-channel analysis, and Bluetooth streaming.
3. Adaptive noise reduction, dynamic feedback cancellation, speech enhancement in noisy environments, directional microphones, and multi-channel audio amplification.
4. Finished hardware, companion mobile applications, and in-person clinical hearing evaluations and fittings.
5. Hearing aids, hearing protection, in-the-ear audio devices, and retail hearing health clinics.
6. Consumers, retail pharmacy and wholesale club chains, and hearing aid wearers with mild to moderate hearing loss.
7. Its finished hearing aids are sold through wholesale club hearing centers, big-box retail pharmacies, and direct-to-consumer online storefronts.
8. It operates a vertically integrated direct-to-consumer model that combines in-store audiological evaluations and retail distribution with user-controlled app-based hearing aid tuning.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Knowles, Sam's Club, Walmart, Best Buy, CVS, Walgreens, Amazon, Target, and the University of Texas at Dallas.
Organization type: A privately held subsidiary of Hearing Lab Technology.
Business model: Hardware sales of hearing aids and accessories, direct clinical service revenue, and retail distribution partnerships.
Scale and maturity: A mid-sized company founded in 2009, operating over 500 hearing centers and distributing through major national retail chains.
Geography: Based in Fort Worth, Texas, USA, operating clinics and retail distribution throughout the United States, Latin America, and China.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on hearing health technology, consumer audio equipment, and clinical hearing services.

points.name: Westone Laboratories Inc
points.description: US audio manufacturer making custom in-ear monitors and hearing protection for musicians.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures custom and universal in-ear monitors, earphones, and hearing protection products for professional musicians and audio enthusiasts.
1. A maker of professional audio equipment that sells finished hardware in the form of custom and universal in-ear monitors.
2. The core technology comprises balanced-armature drivers and passive crossovers housed in ergonomic custom or universal shells, supplemented by ambient port designs for environmental awareness.
3. The products deliver high-quality sound reproduction, sound isolation, on-stage ambient awareness, and hearing protection.
4. Customers receive finished hardware, including in-ear monitors, earphones, and related accessories such as cables and connectors.
5. The products are used on live performance stages, in studios, and in hearing protection settings.
6. The company sells to professional musicians, touring professionals, and discerning audio enthusiasts.
7. Its finished hardware is sold directly to consumers and professionals for use in live and studio applications.
8. The approach emphasizes ergonomic custom-fit shells and ambient awareness technology to reduce ear fatigue during extended use.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Lucid Audio (Lucid Hearing) acquired the music division, and the company historically collaborated with Jerry Harvey on early in-ear monitors.
Organization type: The organization is a subsidiary brand operating under a parent hearing health and consumer audio company.
Business model: The company generates revenue through the direct sale of premium audio hardware and related accessories.
Scale and maturity: Operating since 1959, the brand has a long-standing legacy in the professional audio industry and produces custom units domestically and universal units in Asia.
Geography: The company is based and manufactures custom products in the United States, with universal models produced in Asia.
Beyond audio: The company's entire focus is on audio hardware, in-ear monitors, and hearing protection.

points.name: Etymotic Research
points.description: US hearing technology manufacturer creating high-fidelity earplugs, hearing protection products, and hearing aids.
points.bullets:
An equipment maker that develops and manufactures high-fidelity in-ear earphones, hearing aids, hearing protection devices, and audiometric testing instruments based on auditory research.
1. An equipment maker that designs finished audio hardware products sold as complete physical units worn in-ear.
2. The products rely on balanced-armature transducers, tuned acoustic resonators, acoustic resistors, and directional microphones.
3. The products deliver high-isolation audio playback, noise attenuation, speech enhancement, and hearing diagnostic measurement.
4. The products are finished hardware sold directly to consumers and professionals.
5. The products are used in earbuds, hearing aids, personal sound amplifiers, audiometric testing equipment, and communication headsets.
6. The products are sold to consumers, audiophiles, hearing care professionals, and children requiring volume-limited listening.
7. The company sells its finished hardware directly to end users and through distributors.
8. The company originated the first commercial balanced-armature in-ear earphones for music playback and publishes accuracy scores for its designs based on target frequency response curves.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The organization operates as a brand within Lucid Hearing, which acquired it, and its products are distributed by Oaktree Products and Hearing Lab Technologies.
Organization type: The organization is a subsidiary brand operating under a parent company.
Business model: The company makes money through hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: The organization was founded in 1983 and operates as an established brand within its parent portfolio.
Geography: The organization is based in Elk Grove Village, Illinois.
Beyond audio: Audio is the entire focus of the company.

points.name: Knowles Hearing Health Technologies
points.description: Audio component division building transducers and MEMS microphones for hearing aids and premium audio markets.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of foundational audio transducers that designs and produces balanced armatures and MEMS microphones for hearing aid manufacturers, consumer audio brands, and professional audio equipment makers.
1. A hardware component maker that designs and manufactures physical audio transducers sold as finished components integrated into customers' devices.
2. Balanced armatures and micro-electromechanical systems (MEMS) microphones operating within the transducer layer of the audio stack.
3. Physical sound capture through MEMS microphones and sound reproduction through balanced armatures.
4. Finished hardware components supplied in high volume to device manufacturers.
5. Hearing aids, over-the-counter hearing aids, consumer audio devices, and professional audio equipment.
6. Hearing aid manufacturers, consumer audio brands, and professional audio equipment makers.
7. Its transducer components are designed into hearing aids and consumer audio devices by device manufacturers.
8. It is the world's largest producer of transducers for hearing aids, with its technologies incorporated into the top seven over-the-counter hearing aid products rated by a major aging council.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The top seven over-the-counter hearing aid products rated by a major aging council all incorporate its technologies.
Organization type: A specialized division of a publicly traded corporation.
Business model: High-volume hardware sales of audio components to device manufacturers.
Scale and maturity: A well-established and mature business with roots tracing back to the 1954 invention of the balanced armature for the hearing aid industry.
Geography: Strategically positioned to capitalize on the United States market, leveraging regulatory changes like the FDA's authorization of over-the-counter hearing aids.
Beyond audio: Audio technology and hearing health solutions are the sole focus of the organization's mission.

points.name: Alango Technologies
points.description: Israeli software company developing digital signal processing solutions for wireless earbuds and other audio devices.
points.bullets:
An audio DSP IP licensor that develops digital signal processing algorithms and software packages for voice communication, speech recognition, and hearing enhancement, licensing them to device makers in the mobile, automotive, and consumer electronics industries.
1. An audio DSP IP licensor that builds voice processing algorithms and sound acquisition modules, sold as licensed software and hardware modules that run on customers' embedded Bluetooth SoCs.
2. Digital signal processing algorithms, sensor fusion combining acoustic microphones with MEMS vibration sensors, and adaptive filtering.
3. Acoustic echo cancellation, adaptive microphone arrays, noise reduction, dereverberation, acoustic feedback cancellation, beamforming, sound personalization, and speech intelligibility enhancement.
4. Licensed IP, software packages, and surface-mounted hardware modules.
5. Bluetooth earbuds, headsets, conferencing systems, speakerphones, hearing enhancement devices, smart speakers, mobile phones, automotive, and aviation systems.
6. Mobile phone manufacturers, VoIP providers, videoconferencing companies, automotive and aviation industries, and consumer electronics brands.
7. Its algorithms are integrated by chip vendors into their Bluetooth SoC platforms and adopted by device manufacturers into finished products.
8. It combines standard microphone array processing with MEMS vibration sensor technology to capture clear speech through solid barriers.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It partners with Qualcomm, NXP, Knowles, and MIPS.
Organization type: A privately held company and a spin-off of its parent company.
Business model: IP and per-unit software licensing.
Scale and maturity: A 23-year-old established provider of DSP software.
Geography: It is based in Tirat Carmel, Israel.
Beyond audio: It is a pure-play audio company.

points.name: Asahi Kasei Microdevices Corporation
points.description: Japanese semiconductor manufacturer developing high-quality, low-power audio chips and converters for portable and premium audio applications.
points.bullets:
A semiconductor manufacturer that develops analog and mixed-signal audio ICs, including DACs, ADCs, codecs and voice processors, for consumer electronics and portable audio device makers.
1. A semiconductor manufacturer that designs analog and mixed-signal audio chips and sensors sold as packaged integrated circuits for integration into customers' hardware.
2. The core technology comprises analog and digital mixed-signal processes, combining compound semiconductor technology for sensors with silicon-based ASIC and analog circuit technology.
3. The company delivers high-resolution digital-to-analog and analog-to-digital conversion, high signal-to-noise ratio audio processing, motion artifact cancellation and audio voice processing.
4. Customers get its products as packaged semiconductor chips and integrated circuits.
5. The chips are used in portable audio devices, high-end audio amplifiers, DACs and boards requiring audio processing and sensing.
6. The company sells to consumer electronics device makers and component distributors.
7. Its chips are designed into audio equipment by consumer electronics brands.
8. Its approach is distinguished by the Velvet Sound architecture, which targets high sound quality and low power consumption in its premium audio converters.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company operates as a subsidiary of Asahi Kasei and partners with Aizip for AI-enhanced sensing solutions and CODICO for product distribution.
Organization type: The organization is a subsidiary of a publicly traded chemical and materials group.
Business model: The company makes money through semiconductor and electronic component sales.
Scale and maturity: It is an established component manufacturer with a long-standing distribution relationship spanning decades.
Geography: The company is based in Japan and holds trademarks in Japan, Europe and the United States.
Beyond audio: Beyond audio, the company develops magnetic sensors, gas sensors and microdevices for broader electronic and sensing applications.

points.name: Soundec
points.description: Taiwanese technology company developing AI-based audio processors and noise canceling solutions for headphones and communication devices.
points.bullets:
A chip and solutions company that develops AI-based audio processors and bundled turnkey audio solutions for consumer electronics manufacturers.
1. A chip company that designs integrated audio processors and packages them with reference algorithms and turnkey solutions sold to device makers.
2. AI audio processing algorithms and audio codecs running on an integrated processor built around a Tensilica HiFi3 DSP core.
3. Single- and multi-microphone noise cancellation, far-field beamforming, echo cancellation, howling suppression, dynamic bass enhancement, multi-band equalization, dynamic range control, and sleep-friendly sound effects.
4. Chips, turnkey hardware solutions, firmware, and evaluation kits.
5. USB microphones, noise-canceling headphones, walkie-talkies, car audio, call center headsets, esports earphones, smart TVs, vehicle cockpits, enterprise conference systems, live streaming equipment, portable speakers, soundbars, PC speakers, and pillow speakers.
6. Consumer electronics brands and device manufacturers.
7. Its processors and turnkey solutions are designed into finished consumer audio devices by electronics brands.
8. It pairs integrated audio processors based on licensed DSP cores with a broad portfolio of application-specific turnkey audio solutions.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Cadence Tensilica.
Organization type: A privately held technology company.
Business model: Chip sales and turnkey hardware solution sales.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is on audio processing technology and hardware.

points.name: Cadence Design Systems
points.description: US technology company providing Tensilica audio DSP cores and electronic design automation software for audio processing chips.
points.bullets:
An electronic design automation software and IP licensor that develops audio, voice and AI digital signal processor cores, along with design software, used by chip designers and consumer electronics makers.
1. An audio DSP IP licensor whose processor cores and EDA software are sold as licensed IP and software tools that run in customers' silicon designs.
2. Digital signal processor instruction set architectures and neural network acceleration hardware optimized for low-power audio, voice and edge AI compute.
3. Wake-word detection, beamforming, noise reduction, audio and voice codec processing, and object-based audio decoding.
4. Licensed IP cores, EDA software tools, and software development kits.
5. Smartphones, laptops, smartwatches, automotive head units, digital TVs, set-top boxes, AR headsets, smart amplifiers and battery-operated portable devices.
6. Chip companies, semiconductor designers, consumer electronics manufacturers, and automakers.
7. Its DSP IP cores are integrated by semiconductor vendors into system-on-chip platforms for consumer electronics and automotive applications.
8. It develops DSP instruction set architectures in parallel with updated codec basic operators to optimize hardware and software efficiency, and leads audio codec standardization efforts in standards bodies.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Dolby, DTS, Fraunhofer, Google, NXP, Qualcomm, Analog Devices, Airoha, Huawei, Lenovo, Sensory, Silentium, Elevear and Waves.
Organization type: A publicly traded electronic design automation technology company.
Business model: IP licensing, per-unit royalties, and software licenses and subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: A large, established public corporation with a comprehensive audio partner ecosystem of over 180 partners.
Geography: Based in San Jose, California, USA, operating globally.
Beyond audio: It provides software, hardware, IP and services for designing and verifying advanced semiconductors, networking equipment, and computer systems across the electronics industry.

points.name: Topping
points.description: Chinese audio equipment manufacturer building digital-to-analog converters and headphone amplifiers for consumers.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer and desktop audio equipment that designs, builds and sells finished digital-to-analog converters and headphone amplifiers for audiophile consumers.
1. An equipment maker whose finished DAC and headphone amplifier hardware runs as standalone desktop units.
2. Digital-to-analog conversion and amplification circuits built around discrete DAC chips and fully balanced analog architectures.
3. High-resolution digital-to-analog decoding of DSD and PCM audio signals and headphone amplification.
4. Finished hardware products.
5. Desktop audio systems and personal headphone listening setups.
6. Audiophile consumers.
7. Its finished audio hardware is sold directly to consumers.
8. High-performance digital-to-analog conversion and balanced headphone amplification offered at competitive prices.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It uses DAC chips from AKM and ESS.
Organization type: A privately held manufacturer.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Geography: Based and operating in China.

points.name: Allen & Heath
points.description: UK pro audio manufacturer building digital mixing consoles for live sound.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures digital and analog mixing consoles, audio matrix processors, and I/O expanders for live sound, broadcast, installation, and studio applications.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished mixing consoles, matrix processors, and stage boxes sold as standalone hardware units.
2. Embedded digital signal processing cores running at 96 kHz, combined with analog microphone preamps and audio networking protocols.

Organization type: A privately held consumer audio brand and equipment manufacturer.
