A maker of professional audio equipment that builds commentary units, intercoms, networked interfaces, and monitoring loudspeakers integrating Dante, RAVENNA, AES67, and ST 2110-30 audio networking for broadcasters and event productions.
1. An equipment maker that designs finished audio networking hardware and intercom systems sold as standalone units for broadcast and live production environments.
2. Analog and digital audio interfaces built on network audio protocols including Dante, RAVENNA, Milan AVB, AES67, and SMPTE ST 2110-30, with embedded software for routing, monitoring, and remote control.
3. Multi-channel audio networking, commentary and intercom routing, low-latency audio interface bridging, member identification and electronic voting, microphone-loudspeaker delay compensation, and networked monitoring playback.
4. Finished hardware products sold directly for installation in broadcast facilities, legislatures, and live event production setups.
5. Broadcast commentary positions, legislative chambers, intercom systems for production crews, mobile game production feeds, and studio monitoring.
6. Broadcasters, event production companies, legislatures, and professional audio facilities.
7. Its finished hardware products are deployed directly by broadcasters and production facilities in commentary, intercom, and legislative broadcast workflows.
8. It combines multiple network audio standards including Dante, RAVENNA, and ST 2110-30 in dedicated commentary and intercom hardware built specifically for broadcast and parliamentary applications.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It uses Audinate's Dante audio networking technology and participates in standards-based interoperability with AES67 and SMPTE ST 2110-30 ecosystems.
Organization type: A privately held manufacturer of professional broadcast audio equipment.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of finished audio products to broadcasters and production facilities.
Scale and maturity: A long-established manufacturer with over a thousand of its primary commentary boxes deployed in the US alone and operations spanning global broadcast markets.
Geography: Based in the United Kingdom and serving broadcasters and event productions worldwide.
Beyond audio: It focuses entirely on professional audio equipment for broadcast, live event, and legislative applications.

points.name: Genelec
points.description: Finnish pro audio manufacturer building active studio monitors with integrated room correction.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures active loudspeaker systems, networked audio management devices, and personalized spatial audio services for professional studios, audiovisual installations, and residential applications.
1. A professional audio equipment maker that builds active loudspeakers, networked audio management devices, and spatial audio measurement services, sold as finished hardware and cloud-based services.
2. DSP-based room measurement and correction algorithms, directivity control waveguides, Audio-over-IP networking, and photogrammetric head-and-torso modeling for personalized HRTF generation.
3. Room correction and calibration, low-frequency directivity control, networked audio routing and management, and personalized spatial audio rendering.
4. Finished hardware loudspeakers and management devices, alongside a cloud-based service that outputs spatial audio profile files.
5. Professional studios, immersive audio setups, audiovisual installations, residential theaters, and free-field localization tests.
6. Studios, audio professionals, system integrators, and residential consumers.
7. Its finished loudspeakers and management devices are installed directly into studios and residential spaces by system integrators and audio professionals.
8. Its loudspeakers integrate DSP-based room calibration with coaxial designs and Audio-over-IP networking into a unified monitoring ecosystem.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its networking devices support Dante, AES67, Ravenna, and ST2110 protocols, and its spatial audio profiles adhere to AES SOFA standards.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished loudspeakers and network devices, and service fees for personalized spatial audio profile generation.
Scale and maturity: Established in 1978, manufacturing its products sustainably in Iisalmi, Finland.
Geography: Based in Iisalmi, Finland, serving a global market.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is on professional audio reproduction, monitoring, and room calibration.

points.name: Attero Tech
points.description: Fort Wayne, Indiana-based manufacturer building networked audio wall plates and interfaces for commercial sound systems.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of networked audio equipment that designs and builds audio networking interfaces, including wall plates, HDMI audio converters, and rack monitors, for professional audio integration.
1. An equipment maker whose finished hardware products and companion software plugins run in professional AV installations.
2. Digital audio networking interfaces and signal routing hardware based on Dante and AES67 protocols, managed through proprietary configuration software.
3. Analog and digital I/O conversion, networked audio transport, HDMI audio embedding and de-embedding, Bluetooth reception, and confidence monitoring of networked audio signals.
4. Finished hardware products, configuration software, and software plugins.
5. Professional AV installations, networked audio racks, conference rooms, and integrated audio systems.
6. Professional audio integrators and AV system designers.
7. Its hardware products are installed by integrators into professional AV networks and controlled through third-party control platforms.
8. It focuses on audio networking endpoints designed specifically for integration with Q-SYS control platforms.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its products are developed with Q-SYS platform integration and operate on Dante and AES67 networks.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales, software subscriptions for expanded device channels, and free software plugins.
Geography: Based in Fort Wayne, Indiana, USA, operating in the professional audio integration market.
Beyond audio: The company focuses entirely on networked audio hardware and management software for professional installations.

points.name: AuviTran
points.description: French audio networking manufacturer building networked audio interfaces and platforms for professional audio systems.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of professional audio networking equipment that designs and builds networked audio interface cards and host platforms for the professional audio industry.
1. An equipment maker that builds networked audio interface cards and host chassis sold as finished hardware.
2. Embedded asynchronous sample-rate conversion technology and audio networking bridging hardware that routes multichannel AES67 and AVB streams.
3. AES67 and AVB network audio bridging, high-density multichannel audio routing and asynchronous sample-rate conversion.
4. Finished hardware interface cards, host platforms and touch control systems.
5. Professional audio installations and live sound mixing systems.
6. Professional audio integrators, sound engineers and mixing console operators.
7. Its interface cards are installed into host chassis to bridge digital mixing consoles and audio networks in professional environments.
8. It provides high-density channel bridging between AES67 and legacy AVB networks directly compatible with professional mixing consoles.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Yamaha's RIVAGE PM series and Synthax as US distribution partner.
Organization type: Privately held manufacturer.
Business model: Hardware sales of interface cards and platforms.
Scale and maturity: Established manufacturer with a worldwide presence in the professional audio industry.
Geography: Based in France and operates globally.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is on professional audio networking and interface hardware.

points.name: d&b audiotechnik
points.description: German pro audio manufacturer building loudspeaker systems and AVB networking technology for live sound.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that manufactures loudspeakers, subwoofers, amplifiers, signal-processing devices and software for sound reinforcement systems used in live concerts, festivals, theatres, stadiums and corporate installations, and co-develops network-management software for the Milan AVB protocol for audio professionals.
1. A maker of professional audio equipment that builds loudspeaker systems, amplifiers and signal processors sold as finished hardware, alongside sound-system design and control software and immersive-audio signal engines that run on dedicated hardware in live and installed venues.
2. The core technology comprises high-performance transducers, integrated amplification, line-array acoustics, object-based immersive-audio signal processing and AVB-based network audio protocols for synchronized low-latency multichannel audio.
3. The capabilities include high-quality speech and music reproduction, low-frequency sound reinforcement, line-array acoustic coverage control, object-based three-dimensional sound positioning and room emulation.
4. Customers get finished loudspeakers, subwoofers and amplifiers, dedicated signal engines, design and control software applications and network-management software for Milan-AVB networks.
5. The products are used in large-scale outdoor festivals, live concerts, theatres, arenas, corporate events, stadiums and permanent installations.
6. The organization sells to live-sound production professionals, system integrators, audio engineers, installers and venue operators.
7. Its finished audio hardware and software products are deployed by sound-reinforcement integrators and touring professionals into live-event and installed-venue sound systems.
8. A system-oriented approach integrating own loudspeakers, amplifiers, signal engines and control software into unified sound-reinforcement workflows is the distinguishing approach.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It is a founding and Promoter Member of the Avnu Alliance, a co-developer of the Milan protocol and Milan Manager software and a partner integrating its Soundscape DS100 engine with DiGiCo SD7 and SD12 mixing consoles; it acquired the ARVA group.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held company.
Business model: The organization makes money through hardware sales of professional audio equipment, amplifiers and signal-processing devices, alongside software products.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 1981 and based in Backnang near Stuttgart with over 1000 employees worldwide and sales offices in major cities, it is a large established manufacturer.
Geography: It is headquartered in Germany with global operations, subsidiaries and sales offices in major cities internationally.
Beyond audio: Professional sound reinforcement systems are the organization's entire focus.

points.name: AudioScience
points.description: Audio equipment manufacturer building digital sound cards and network interfaces for broadcast and professional audio systems.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures DSP-based digital audio peripherals, including network audio interfaces, broadcast sound cards and tuner cards, for broadcast, installed sound and OEM markets.
1. An equipment maker that designs and manufactures PCIe sound cards and digital audio network peripherals that run in professional servers and workstations.
2. Digital signal processing hardware and audio networking interfaces supporting Dante, AVB, AES67, Livewire and CobraNet protocols.
3. High-density multichannel audio routing, low-latency audio over IP, analog and digital I/O, mic preamplification, broadcast signal monitoring and AM/FM/HD Radio and analog TV tuner functionality.
4. Finished hardware products, primarily PCIe sound cards and tuner cards, along with custom-design services for OEMs and systems integrators.
5. Broadcast production facilities, audio streaming, digital automation systems, distributed installed sound systems and professional AV networks.
6. Broadcasters, OEMs, systems integrators and digital automation system designers.
7. Its finished hardware cards are integrated into broadcast servers and installed sound systems by professional audio engineers and systems integrators.
8. It focuses on standards-based technology across multiple audio networking protocols rather than proprietary designs, ensuring compatibility across diverse professional audio ecosystems.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Co-founder of the Milan protocol under the Avnu Alliance, with products compatible with Dante networks, Livewire+ networks and Broadcasters Warehouse automation systems.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales of sound cards and tuner cards, plus custom-design services for OEMs.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: Axia
points.description: US broadcast equipment manufacturer building IP-based audio mixing consoles for radio networks.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that develops and manufactures Audio-over-IP consoles, console engines, network audio interfaces, and intercom systems for broadcast studios.
1. An equipment maker whose finished broadcast hardware and software run in studio facilities.
2. Audio-over-IP networking systems utilizing proprietary Ethernet protocols and AES67 compliance for low-latency digital audio transport and routing.
3. Digital audio mixing, analog-to-network audio conversion, Ethernet-based intercom communication, and network switching.
4. Finished hardware products, including mixing consoles, rack interfaces, intercom panels, and virtual software drivers.
5. Radio broadcast studios, professional audio production environments, and broadcast intercom networks.
6. Broadcast stations, audio production facilities, and network infrastructure engineers.
7. Its broadcast equipment is deployed directly into radio studios and integrated with third-party hardware through standard audio networking protocols.
8. It developed and operates a proprietary audio-over-Ethernet protocol that forms the basis of a large broadcast equipment ecosystem with no central matrix.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A brand of Telos Alliance with an ecosystem of over 115 broadcast equipment partners.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand of a privately held broadcast equipment company.
Business model: Hardware sales of mixing consoles, network interfaces, and intercom panels.
Scale and maturity: An established brand with over 5,500 radio studios equipped with its networks and 100,000 connected devices.
Geography: Based in Cleveland, Ohio, USA, operating in broadcast markets.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is on audio-over-IP technology and equipment for the broadcast industry.

points.name: Elytone
points.description: Taiwanese audio technology company developing networked audio processing modules and power amplification solutions.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment and modules that develops networked audio processing and amplification solutions for installed audio systems.
1. An equipment maker that designs networked audio processors and amplifier modules, sold as finished hardware components to other equipment manufacturers.
2. Networked audio processors combining ARM and SHARC DSP architectures with GaN-based amplifier circuits and real-time energy storage power management algorithms.
3. Networked audio processing, AoIP networking, Dante support, programmable DSP with web control, and dynamic peak power boosting above PoE limits.
4. Finished hardware modules and networked amplifiers.
5. Networked installed audio systems, PoE-powered loudspeakers and amplifiers.
6. Audio brands and equipment manufacturers.
7. Its modules and finished hardware are integrated by audio brands into installed sound products.
8. Its SoundBoost technology dynamically stores energy to deliver peak audio output exceeding standard PoE power limits.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Analog Devices.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Hardware and module sales.
Scale and maturity: A company with over 45 years of engineering and manufacturing expertise.
Geography: Headquartered in Taiwan with manufacturing across Asia.
Beyond audio: The organization also provides magnetic solutions alongside its audio products.

points.name: DiGiCo
points.location: New York, NY, USA (announcement location, not necessarily HQ)
points.description: Digital mixing console manufacturer building professional audio systems for live sound applications.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of professional audio equipment that designs and builds digital mixing consoles, audio networking systems, and control surfaces for live sound, theatre, broadcast, and postproduction engineers.
1. A maker of professional audio equipment that builds digital mixing consoles, stage I/O racks, and audio networking matrices, sold as finished hardware running dedicated embedded software.
2. Digital signal processing engines built on field-programmable gate arrays, integrated with touch-screen control surfaces and digital audio networking protocols.
3. Digital mixing, audio routing, channel processing, multitrack playback, and object-based immersive mixing control.
4. The company delivers finished hardware consoles, outboard I/O racks, wall controllers, and companion control software to audio engineers and venues.
5. Its consoles and systems are used in live music tours, theatres, megachurches, broadcast studios, and large entertainment venues.
6. The company sells to front-of-house and monitor engineers, audio production companies, theatres, houses of worship, and broadcast networks.
7. Its consoles are operated by audio engineers as the central routing and processing hub in live sound and installed venue signal chains.
8. Its approach centers on high-channel-count FPGA processing engines combined with extensive native integrations for immersive audio and audio-over-IP networking protocols.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company is a subsidiary brand of Audiotonix, operates the KLANG:technologies brand, and partners with L-Acoustics, d&b audiotechnik, Waves Audio, Fourier Audio, and the Avnu Alliance.
Organization type: The company is a corporate subsidiary brand of a larger professional audio manufacturing group.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of consoles, stage racks, and control surfaces, plus associated software and integration products.
Scale and maturity: It is a globally established brand whose consoles are standard equipment on major concert tours and broadcast events.
Geography: It is based in the United Kingdom and distributes its products through exclusive partners such as Group One Ltd. in the United States.
Beyond audio: Professional digital audio mixing and signal processing is its entire focus.

points.name: Neutrik
points.description: Liechtenstein manufacturer building professional audio connectors and certified audio networking modules.
points.bullets:
An equipment maker and component manufacturer that develops and manufactures audio connectors and Milan-certified audio networking modules for professional AV and OEM customers.
1. A manufacturer of finished connectivity hardware and embedded audio modules that OEMs integrate into their professional audio products.
2. Audio networking modules featuring a 100mbit switch and operating in redundant or daisy-chain modes, alongside high-performance analog and fiber optic connectors.
3. Milan-certified audio networking transport, daisy-chaining and redundancy for 2x2 stream audio products, and physical audio and video signal connectivity.
4. Finished hardware sold as connectors and certified modules, alongside evaluation boards, sample modules, and technical support provided through a development kit and online portal.
5. Professional AV systems, live events and entertainment, broadcast, medical, industrial, and audio networking devices.
6. OEM manufacturers, professional AV integrators, and industries requiring mission-critical interconnect solutions.
7. Its connectors and certified modules are designed by OEMs and integrators into professional audio and video networking products.
8. It provides the first Milan Certified audio module, enabling efficient implementation of Milan audio networking with included self-testing support for logo approval.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Avnu Alliance.
Organization type: A subsidiary of a privately held manufacturer.
Business model: Hardware sales of connectors, components, and development kits.
Scale and maturity: A globally established manufacturer operating a regional subsidiary across the Americas.
Geography: Based in Liechtenstein with operations headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina, serving North, Central, and South America.
Beyond audio: The organization develops connectivity solutions for video, lighting, data, and fiber optic networks in addition to audio.

points.name: MOTU
points.description: US audio technology manufacturer developing digital audio workstation software and audio interfaces.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of audio interfaces and digital audio workstation software that builds hardware and software for music production, recording, and studio routing. It sells finished recording hardware with embedded DSP mixing alongside a DAW and virtual instruments for musicians, producers, and studios.
1. A manufacturer of finished professional audio equipment whose audio interfaces and digital audio workstation software run on Mac and Windows computers.
2. A/D and D/A conversion using high-performance DACs, Thunderbolt and USB connectivity, AVB Ethernet audio networking, and software-based digital mixing and DSP effects.
3. Multi-channel audio recording and playback, low-latency mixing, parametric EQ, compression, metering, immersive audio mixing, AI stem separation, MIDI sequencing, and software-based virtual instrumentation.
4. Finished hardware units sold with bundled software, standalone digital audio workstation software, and virtual instrument plugins.
5. Home and project studios, professional recording studios, live tracking, and computer-based music production.
6. Musicians, producers, recording engineers, and home studio owners.
7. Its finished audio interfaces are sold directly to end users through retailers and bundled with partner DAW software.
8. It combines a long-standing digital audio workstation with a broad lineup of AVB-networked and USB audio interfaces at accessible price points.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It uses ESS Sabre32 Ultra DAC technology and bundles Ableton Live Lite software.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales and software licenses.
Scale and maturity: An established manufacturer operating since the 1980s.
Geography: Based in the USA.
Beyond audio: It focuses entirely on audio production hardware and software.

points.name: RME
points.description: German pro audio manufacturer building professional audio interfaces, converters, and preamplifiers for studio and stage use.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of professional audio interfaces, converters, and preamplifiers that implements AVB, MADI, and Dante networking technologies in its products for studio, live, broadcast, and installation applications.
1. An equipment maker that designs and manufactures professional audio hardware, sold as finished devices.
2. High-channel-count digital audio networking routing, analog-to-digital and digital-to-analog conversion stages, and hardware-based DSP mixing engines driven by a jitter-suppressing clock technology.
3. Multichannel audio routing, analog and digital signal conversion, microphone preamplification, standalone hardware mixing, and audio signal analysis.
4. Finished hardware devices, including PCIe interface cards, half-rack routers, and standalone converters, bundled with dedicated mixer and analyzer software.
5. Recording studios, live sound stages, broadcast facilities, permanent audio installations, and acoustic measurement setups.
6. Audio engineers, recording studios, broadcasters, system integrators, and live sound professionals.
7. Its finished hardware devices are distributed through a dedicated audio marketing and distribution division to professional audio end-users.
8. It integrates proprietary clock technology and bundled hardware DSP mixing software across a comprehensive range of high-channel-count interface and converter formats.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Products are marketed and distributed by Synthax and designed to interoperate with Milan-certified AVB networks and optical MADI connections from other hardware manufacturers.
Organization type: A privately held manufacturer.
Business model: Hardware sales of professional audio interfaces, converters, and related network audio equipment.
Scale and maturity: An established manufacturer with a broad portfolio of professional audio products and long-term product support commitments.
Geography: Based in Germany and operating globally through a dedicated distribution network.
Beyond audio: It is a pure-play professional audio company.

points.name: JOYNED
points.description: Global software company building networking tools and hardware for open-standard audio protocols.
points.bullets:
A software and IP provider that develops networking protocol stacks, reference designs and finished hardware for AVB/Milan networked audio, selling to equipment manufacturers and system integrators.
1. A software company that develops protocol libraries and controller software sold as licensed software and reference designs, and also builds finished network switches and USB audio interfaces.
2. Time-sensitive networking protocols, Ethernet stacks and I2S drivers implementing AVB/Milan standards for deterministic audio networking.
3. Milan-compliant networked audio transport, USB class-compliant bridging, AVB switching and system configuration management.
4. Licensed software libraries, reference designs and finished hardware products.
5. Professional audio networks, live sound systems, show laser systems and integrated audio installations.
6. Professional audio equipment manufacturers and system integrators.
7. Its protocol stacks and reference designs are embedded by equipment manufacturers into their networked audio products.
8. Its focus on cost-effective implementation of open Milan standards to lower the barrier to adoption for manufacturers.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Avnu Alliance, Adamson, Kelsey Acoustics, Luminex, Nixer, LaserAnimation Sollinger, Meyer Sound, d&b audiotechnik, Audiotonix, L-Acoustics, PreSonus.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Software licenses and hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: A founder-led company that has grown to Promoter Member status in the Avnu Alliance and demonstrates multi-vendor interoperability with 18 manufacturers.
Geography: Based in Austria and operating globally.
Beyond audio: It is a pure-play audio networking company focused entirely on AVB/Milan protocol implementation.

points.name: Avnu Alliance
points.description: Industry alliance certifying networked audio devices for interoperability using open Milan and AVB standards.
points.bullets:
A standards body and industry alliance that develops and administers networking protocols and certification programs for professional audio and video equipment manufacturers. It defines interoperability standards built on IEEE Audio Video Bridging and Time Sensitive Networking, manages the certification of compliant devices, and provides testing tools for manufacturers.
1. A standards body that develops networking protocols and certification programs delivered as specifications, test plans, and validation tools for manufacturers implementing its standards.
2. Deterministic networking protocols built on IEEE Audio Video Bridging and Time Sensitive Networking standards, extended with added specification requirements for professional media to ensure real-time, low-latency interoperability.
3. Device interoperability certification, conformance testing, and deterministic media networking for professional audio and video end devices and network switches.
4. Networking protocol specifications, certification programs, a comprehensive testing portal, a certified product registry, and a validation test tool bundling software with hardware equipment.
5. Professional audio and video networked systems, including certified end devices and network switches used in professional media environments.
6. Professional audio and video equipment manufacturers, network switch developers, module developers, and authorized test facilities implementing its standards.
7. Its protocol specifications and certification programs are adopted by equipment manufacturers to validate and market interoperable networking devices.
8. It is the defining body for the Milan protocol, adding specific professional media requirements to open IEEE AVB/TSN standards and managing a structured certification ecosystem with authorized test facilities.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Founding and promoter members include Avid, d&b audiotechnik, L-Acoustics, Meyer Sound, Biamp, AudioScience, Luminex, PreSonus, JOYNED, Neutrik, and DiGiCo; authorized test facilities include Allion, Excelfore, and GRL.
Organization type: An industry alliance and standards body composed of professional audio, video, and automotive networking manufacturers.
Business model: Membership fees and certification program administration.
Scale and maturity: An established global industry consortium with a broad membership of leading professional audio, video, and networking manufacturers.
Geography: Operates globally, with authorized test facilities in regions including the European Union and Japan.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses on real-time Ethernet networking for both professional audio/video and automotive applications.

points.name: d&b
points.description: German pro audio manufacturer building loudspeaker systems and software for high-end sound reproduction.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures loudspeaker systems and associated control and simulation software for high-end speech and music reproduction in live venues and installed sound systems.
1. A manufacturer of professional loudspeaker systems and associated control, simulation and verification software sold as finished hardware and software products that run on standard computing devices.
2. Professional loudspeaker transducers and acoustical systems paired with remote control, acoustic simulation and array verification software.
3. High-fidelity speech and music reproduction, loudspeaker array verification and remote system control.
4. Finished loudspeaker hardware, remote control software, simulation software and a companion mobile viewer application.
5. Live venues, tours and installed professional sound reinforcement systems.
6. Audio professionals, sound engineers and system integrators.
7. Its loudspeaker systems and software are deployed as end-user professional audio solutions in live and installed venues.
8. Integrated proprietary array verification that automatically identifies the physical position of a loudspeaker in an array to verify correct cabling within its control software.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A member of the Avnu alliance involved in developing MILAN standards.
Organization type: A privately held manufacturer.
Business model: Hardware sales of professional loudspeakers and associated software products.
Scale and maturity: A mid-sized company with between 501 and 1,000 employees.
Geography: Headquartered in Backnang, Germany.
Beyond audio: The organization is a pure-play professional audio company.

points.name: Adamson
points.description: Canadian pro audio manufacturer building touring-grade loudspeakers and sound reinforcement systems.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures loudspeaker systems, amplifiers, processing, and software for sound reinforcement, providing complete audio solutions for touring professionals, live events, performing arts, and permanent installations.
1. An equipment maker that designs and manufactures professional loudspeakers, subwoofers, amplifiers, and system management platforms sold as finished hardware and accompanying software products.
2. Acoustic engineering, chamber design, and transducer architecture, combined with networked audio protocols and system matrixing software.
3. High-output sound reinforcement, line array dispersion control, low-frequency extension, and audio system management and matrixing.
4. Finished loudspeaker enclosures, amplifiers, racks, and system management software sold as integrated hardware and software products.
5. Global concert tours, music festivals, performing arts centers, theaters, live venues, and permanent architectural installations.
6. Touring sound rental companies, audio integration firms, live event production professionals, and performance venues.
7. Its finished loudspeaker and amplification systems are deployed by audio rental and integration companies into live event venues and touring productions.
8. In-house design and manufacturing of nearly all loudspeaker components, including patented chamber design and transducer architecture, in a vertically integrated facility.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Promoter Member of the Avnu Alliance, adopting JOYNED Milan Software, with installation partnerships with Clair Global Integration.
Organization type: A privately held equipment manufacturing company.
Business model: Hardware sales of professional loudspeaker systems, subwoofers, and amplifiers, bundled with system management software.
Scale and maturity: A long-established manufacturer with over 40 years of operation, over 100 employees, and a large in-house manufacturing facility.
Geography: Based in Port Perry, Ontario, Canada, exporting and operating in global professional audio markets.
Beyond audio: Professional audio and sound reinforcement is its entire focus.

points.name: Nixer
points.description: Pro audio company building network monitoring and routing tools for live sound and broadcast.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures audio monitoring, diagnostics, routing and mixing tools for Audio over IP networks, used in live sound, broadcast and event production environments.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished hardware monitoring units, switches and related accessories sold as rack-mounted products and portable devices.
2. Networked audio processing and routing systems that monitor, mix and switch multichannel Audio over IP streams across Dante, Ravenna, AES67, ST2110 and Milan AVB protocols.
3. Multichannel audio monitoring, mixing, routing, diagnostics, signal change-over switching and remote control with metering and audio streaming.
4. Finished hardware products including rack-mounted units, portable engineering tools, remote control adapters, WiFi adapters and power supplies, alongside an iPad application.
5. Live sound and events, broadcast facilities and network audio engineering environments.
6. Audio engineers, live sound professionals, broadcast technicians and event production teams.
7. Its finished hardware is deployed directly by audio professionals in live sound and broadcast signal chains.
8. Focuses on compact, cost-effective multi-protocol network audio monitoring and mixing hardware spanning up to 256 channels.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Integrates technology from JOYNED into its PD-Milan monitoring solution.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales.

points.name: Audio Precision
points.description: US audio test equipment manufacturer building high-performance audio analyzers for professional testing and measurement.
points.bullets:
An equipment maker that designs and manufactures high-performance audio analyzers and measurement software used by engineers to test, measure and calibrate audio equipment and hearing aids.
1. A manufacturer of finished audio test and measurement equipment and accompanying software suites that run on dedicated hardware analyzers in lab and production environments.
2. High-precision analog and digital signal generation and analysis hardware paired with measurement software for characterizing audio devices.
3. Analog and digital audio analysis, acoustic testing, multitone and continuous sweep measurements, loudspeaker testing and hearing aid production testing.
4. Finished hardware audio analyzers and measurement software.
5. Engineering labs, anechoic chambers, production lines for hearing aids, and acoustic test setups.
6. Audio equipment engineers, hearing aid manufacturers and acoustic test professionals.
7. Its finished test equipment is operated directly by engineers in development labs and on manufacturing lines.
8. Its audio analyzers are considered the gold standard in audio measurement for performance and reliability.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company operates as part of Axiometrix Solutions alongside GRAS Sound & Vibration, integrates with Outline turntables and Interacoustics test boxes, and is owned by Battery Ventures.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand operating within a private equity-owned test and measurement group.
Business model: Hardware sales of audio analyzers and accessories.
Scale and maturity: A globally recognized brand serving engineers for over thirty-five years.
Geography: Based in Beaverton, Oregon, USA and serving engineers worldwide.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on audio test and measurement.

points.name: Siemens
points.description: German manufacturer formerly producing hearing aids and currently using acoustic monitoring for industrial machinery.
points.bullets:
A diversified manufacturing and technology company whose role in audio encompasses historically manufacturing hearing aids and wireless accessories, producing acoustic sound imaging cameras, and licensing its brand to a separate hearing aid company, while also using acoustic monitoring services for industrial machinery.
1. A manufacturer that builds finished hardware including acoustic sound imaging cameras and industrial sensor platforms, while its former hearing aid hardware division is now sold by a separate brand licensee.
2. Acoustic imaging cameras and edge-based machine learning platforms that analyze sensor data from factory equipment to detect anomalies in real time.
3. Industrial machinery acoustic monitoring, acoustic sound imaging, and anomaly detection, alongside historical hearing aid sound processing.
4. Finished hardware, industrial IoT platforms, and historically finished hearing aid devices and smartphone companion applications.
5. Industrial factories, production lines, and historically audiology clinics and hearing healthcare settings.
6. Industrial enterprises, factory operators, and historically hearing aid patients and audiology clinics.
7. Its industrial IoT platforms and acoustic cameras are deployed directly by industrial enterprises, while its hearing aid brand is licensed to a separate manufacturer that produces and sells the devices.
8. It applies industrial-scale engineering and edge-based machine learning to acoustic monitoring for factories while maintaining a legacy brand presence in hearing healthcare through a licensing model.
points.profile:

points.name: 3GPP
points.description: Global standards organization developing voice and audio codec specifications for mobile telecommunications.
points.bullets:
A standards organization that develops and publishes technical specifications for mobile telecommunications, including speech and audio codecs. It defines protocols for encoding, decoding, and rendering voice and audio services, such as narrowband, wideband, and immersive spatial formats, for cellular networks. These specifications are used by device makers, network operators, and chipset vendors to ensure interoperability in communication systems.
1. A standards body that develops audio and speech codec specifications, distributed as published technical standards and reference software, which run on mobile network infrastructure and consumer devices.
2. Audio and speech coding algorithms, including low-delay immersive voice codecs, adaptive multi-rate codecs, and metadata-assisted spatial audio formats, standardized for cellular telephony.
3. Speech and audio compression, spatial audio rendering, binaural and ambisonic decoding, multi-stream teleconferencing, and real-time immersive voice communication.
4. Technical specifications, reference software code, and conformance testing frameworks published as standardized documents for implementation by industry stakeholders.
5. Mobile telephony, 5G Advanced networks, real-time voice and video calls, teleconferencing systems, AR/MR content streaming, and packet-switched streaming services.
6. Telecommunications equipment manufacturers, mobile network operators, chipset companies, handset developers, and telecommunications standards bodies.
7. Its specifications are implemented by codec developers and chipset vendors into DSPs and processors that are integrated into smartphones and network infrastructure by telecommunications brands.
8. It operates as a collaborative consortium of telecommunications industry players to establish globally interoperable cellular standards, moving proprietary technologies into open specifications.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Nokia, Ericsson, Fraunhofer IIS, Huawei, Qualcomm, Samsung, ETSI, NTT DOCOMO, Orange, Panasonic, ZTE, VoiceAge, Cadence.
Organization type: A collaborative standards organization and ETSI partnership project.

Scale and maturity: A global standards initiative responsible for multiple generations of cellular network specifications including 4G LTE and 5G Advanced.
Geography: A global project operating worldwide with standards published in collaboration with regional standards organizations like ETSI.
Beyond audio: The organization develops complete system specifications for cellular telecommunications network technologies, including radio access, core network architecture, and multimedia services.

points.name: Samsung Research
points.description: South Korean research division developing spatial audio formats and immersive audio codecs for consumer devices.
points.bullets:
A corporate research division that develops spatial audio metadata, encoding systems, playback architecture, and efficient room simulators for immersive audio formats.
1. A research and development organization whose audio processing algorithms and format architectures are integrated into consumer electronics hardware.
2. Immersive audio codecs, spatial rendering algorithms, and room simulation implementations form the core technology.
3. The organization delivers spatial audio rendering, format encoding, and device-compatible playback.
4. Customers and internal product groups receive the technology as licensed IP and algorithms integrated into hardware.
5. The technology is used in over-the-top streaming environments, live venues, and consumer electronics devices.
6. The organization primarily supports internal hardware divisions and collaborates with industry standards bodies.
7. Its research and architectures are standardized and integrated into consumer electronics by device manufacturers.
8. The organization co-develops open immersive audio standards rather than proprietary closed ecosystems.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The organization is affiliated with a major consumer electronics parent company and collaborates with industry standards bodies.
Organization type: The organization is a corporate research division of a publicly traded company.
Business model: The entity is funded internally as a corporate research division.
Scale and maturity: The organization is a large-scale advanced research hub within a global electronics manufacturer.
Geography: The organization is based in Seoul, South Korea.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses on advanced research and development across visual technology and broader consumer electronics product improvement.

points.name: Sonus faber
points.description: Italian manufacturer handcrafting high-end loudspeakers and in-car audio systems.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional and consumer audio equipment that designs and handcrafts high-end passive and active loudspeakers, subwoofers and all-in-one audio systems for audiophiles, home theater enthusiasts and luxury automotive brands.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished passive and active loudspeakers and all-in-one audio systems sold as consumer hardware.
2. Acoustic design and cabinet construction using silk dome tweeters, paper fiber bass and midrange drivers, bipole and dipole bass drivers and class-D amplification.
3. High-fidelity sound reproduction, room acoustics correction, multi-room wireless audio streaming and multi-channel home theater playback.
4. Customers get it as finished hardware products including floorstanding speakers, bookshelf speakers, subwoofers and integrated wireless systems.
5. The products are used in home listening rooms, home theaters and luxury cars.
6. The company sells to consumers through retail distributors and to luxury automakers.
7. Its finished loudspeakers are sold directly to end users through retail channels and are integrated into luxury vehicles by automakers.
8. Its approach is distinguished by Italian craftsmanship, handbuilt cabinets and a design heritage focused on aesthetic excellence and premium materials.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Notable partners include Bose, McIntosh, Maserati, Lamborghini and Pagani.
Organization type: The organization is a subsidiary brand under the McIntosh Group, which is owned by Bose.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of finished loudspeakers and audio systems.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 1983, the company has a global distribution presence spanning Australia, New Zealand, Singapore, the UK and the US, with flagship products priced up to $700,000.
Geography: It is based in Italy and operates globally through a network of distributors.
Beyond audio: High-end audio is its entire focus.

points.name: Orka
points.description: Chinese hearing technology company making AI-powered hearing aids that track health metrics and stream audio.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer healthcare wearables and finished hearing aid hardware that embeds proprietary AI audio processing and biometric sensors, targeting consumers with hearing loss.
1. A finished hardware maker whose hearing aids are sold as FDA-cleared Class II medical devices that run on-device in the ear.
2. Embedded AI and machine learning algorithms process audio and sensor data on the hearing aid hardware.
3. The devices deliver adaptive noise suppression, speech enhancement, health metric monitoring, Bluetooth audio streaming and hands-free calling.
4. Customers get the technology in finished, rechargeable wireless earbud-style hardware.
5. The products are used in hearing aids and consumer health wearables.
6. The organization sells directly to consumers.
7. Its finished hearing aids are sold to consumers through a technology partnership with an audio brand.
8. The core differentiator is the combination of FDA-cleared hearing aid functionality, active noise cancellation and biometric health monitoring in a single consumer wearable.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A notable partner is Bose, with which it co-developed and launched a noise-canceling hearing aid.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held startup.
Business model: The company makes money through finished hardware sales of its medical devices.
Scale and maturity: Founded in Silicon Valley in 2018, the organization is an award-winning consumer technology company.
Geography: The company was founded in Silicon Valley and operates globally, including in China.
Beyond audio: Beyond audio, the company builds healthcare wearables that use sensors to monitor health metrics like heart rate and step count.

points.name: Alliance for Open Media (AOM)
points.description: US standards organization developing royalty-free open-source audio and video codecs, including formats for 3D sound.
points.bullets:
A standards body that develops royalty-free, open-source audio and video codec formats, including a 3D audio format, for the broader technology ecosystem.
1. A standards body that develops open codec specifications that are implemented by others in their software and hardware products.
2. Open-standard codec specifications that define how compressed audio and video data is structured, decoded and rendered.
3. 3D spatial audio rendering, immersive sound playback, and general video compression.
4. Royalty-free open-source specifications and codec formats released to the industry.
5. Media streaming services, video platforms, and consumer electronic devices.
6. Semiconductor companies, device manufacturers, software developers, and media platforms.
7. Its open codec specifications are implemented by hardware and software vendors into their encoders, decoders, and media players.
8. Its formats are developed and released under a royalty-free license to remove licensing barriers for broad industry adoption.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Founded by Google and Samsung.
Organization type: A consortium and standards body.
Business model: Operating as an industry consortium, it does not sell products but provides royalty-free open standards.
Scale and maturity: An established industry alliance founded by major technology companies.
Geography: Based in Wakefield, Massachusetts, USA.
Beyond audio: It develops both audio and video codec specifications, with video codecs forming a central part of its work alongside its audio formats.

points.name: International Telecommunication Union
points.description: Geneva-based UN agency setting broadcast audio standards for loudness measurement and immersive sound.
points.bullets:
A United Nations specialized agency that develops and publishes international standards and recommendations for telecommunications and broadcasting, including audio programme exchange formats, loudness measurement algorithms, speech quality assessment metrics, and immersive audio systems.
1. A standards organization that develops recommendations for broadcast and telecommunications audio technologies, adopted by industries worldwide.
2. Open standards for object-based spatial audio, loudness measurement algorithms, wideband speech quality assessment, and digital telephony speech coding specifications including A-law and µ-law.
3. Defines loudness measurement algorithms, immersive audio file formats, wideband speech quality assessment metrics, and digital telephony speech coding specifications.
4. Published recommendations and standards documents adopted by broadcasters, telecom operators, and equipment manufacturers.
5. TV and broadcast audio, digital telephony, speech quality assessment, international audio programme exchange, and immersive audio systems.
6. Broadcasters, telecommunications operators, equipment manufacturers, and regulatory bodies that adopt ITU standards.
7. Its recommendations are implemented by broadcasters and equipment manufacturers into their products and broadcast workflows.
8. It is a UN specialized agency with global authority over telecommunications and broadcasting standards, providing recommendations adopted as international norms.
points.profile:
Organization type: A United Nations specialized agency for information and communication technologies.
Business model: Standards development and publication as an intergovernmental organization.
Scale and maturity: A long-established global UN agency operating since 1865 with 193 member states.
Geography: Headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland, operating worldwide.
Beyond audio: It coordinates global telecommunication standards and development across all ICT domains, with audio being one area among many.

points.name: Emotion Systems
points.description: Software company automating audio processing and mastering workflows.
points.bullets:
A software company that builds automated audio post-production and mastering systems for content creators and distributors.
1. A developer tools company whose software products run as standalone applications in broadcast and post-production facilities.
2. Audio processing algorithms and built-in machine learning models for rendering, encoding, quality control and language detection.
3. Object-based audio rendering, automated mixing, audio format conversion, metadata embedding, up-mixing, dialogue extraction and language detection.
4. Licensed software products and modular software applications.
5. Broadcast facilities, post-production pipelines and content distribution workflows.
6. Content creators and distributors.
7. Its software is used by content creators and distributors to automate audio post-production workflows.
points.profile:
Organization type: Privately held technology company.
Business model: Software licenses.

points.name: USL Inc.
points.description: Nevada audio equipment manufacturer building automated sound testing and signal processing tools for cinemas.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment and test-and-measurement products that designs and manufactures audio-visual test devices, audio signal processors, and digital cinema processors for motion picture exhibition venues.
1. A professional audio equipment maker that designs and manufactures finished hardware sensors, digital cinema processors, and accompanying diagnostic software for installation in cinemas.
2. Automated light and sound sensors with optical detection and Power over Ethernet, digital cinema processors, and diagnostic software for speaker and amplifier fault identification.
3. Automated daily testing of cinema projection and sound equipment, audio signal processing, B-chain processing, and diagnostic measurement of speaker and amplifier problems.
4. Finished hardware sensors, digital cinema processors, digital-to-analog converters, and specialized diagnostic software options.
5. Cinema auditoriums and motion picture exhibition venues.
6. Global cinema operators and exhibitors.
7. Its finished test-and-measurement equipment and cinema processors are installed directly in cinema auditoriums by exhibition operators.
8. Six-time winner of the International Cinema Technology Association Manufacturer of the Year award, recognized for engineering quality and customer support in the cinema exhibition sector.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Acquired by and operates as a subsidiary brand of QSC, complementing its portfolio of cinema power amplifiers, signal processing, and loudspeakers.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand of a privately held professional audio company.
Business model: Hardware and equipment sales, including the direct design, manufacture, and sale of specialized test devices, processors, and accompanying software to cinema operators.
Scale and maturity: An established equipment manufacturer with products installed in over 5,000 cinema auditoriums, operating since its acquisition in 2016.
Geography: Based in the United States and serving global cinema operators.
Beyond audio: Its focus is entirely on professional audio and audio-visual test-and-measurement equipment for the cinema exhibition industry.

points.name: Auro Technologies
points.description: Belgian audio technology company developing immersive 3D audio formats with a focus on vertical sound.
points.bullets:
An audio technology company that develops immersive audio formats, providing spatial audio technology for consumer electronics and entertainment applications.
1. An audio format developer whose immersive audio format is licensed for implementation in consumer devices and media content.
2. The core technology is an immersive audio format that adds vertical sound dimensions to surround sound configurations.
3. It delivers immersive spatial audio rendering with height-based sound reproduction for surround sound systems.
4. The technology is delivered as licensed audio formats and IP integrated into consumer electronics and media production.
5. It is used in home theater systems, consumer electronics, and entertainment media content.
6. The company sells to consumer electronics manufacturers and media content producers.
7. Its audio formats are licensed to device manufacturers and integrated into consumer playback products.
8. Its approach distinguishes itself from other immersive audio formats by emphasizing vertical sound reproduction as a core design principle.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It contributed to the open-source MDA format alongside other industry participants.
Organization type: The organization is an audio technology company based in Belgium.
Geography: The company is based in Belgium and operates in the global immersive audio market.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on audio technology and immersive sound format development.

points.name: Final
points.description: Japanese headphone manufacturer building personalized true wireless earbuds using 3D ear scanning.
points.bullets:
A maker of finished audio hardware that designs and sells premium headphones, earphones, and in-ear monitors, combining experimental materials and acoustic technologies for consumers.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished wireless earbuds and sells them as physical consumer hardware.
2. Three-dimensional head and ear scanning technology for personalized earbud fitting, alongside active noise cancelling and ambient sound processing.
3. Active noise cancellation, ambient sound modes, and high-resolution Bluetooth audio streaming.
4. Finished hardware sold as consumer-ready wireless earbuds.
5. True wireless earbuds and in-ear monitors.
6. Consumers and audiophiles.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to consumers through crowdfunding platforms and retail channels.
8. It uses three-dimensional head and ear scanning to personalize the physical fit of true wireless earbuds.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It supports the LDAC codec developed by a consumer electronics brand and launched its product on a crowdfunding platform.
Organization type: A privately held manufacturing company.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: A high-end audio brand that recently launched a product via crowdfunding.
Geography: Based in Japan.
Beyond audio: Its focus is entirely on audio hardware.

points.name: Embody
points.description: California startup creating AI-based personalized spatial audio profiles from ear scans for games, music, and virtual reality.
points.bullets:
An AI model and software developer that creates personalized spatial audio applications using individual ear profiles. It builds consumer and professional software products that generate personalized head-related transfer function profiles from smartphone images and render binaural audio. The organization provides these tools for gamers, musicians, audio professionals, and extended reality users.
1. An AI model and software developer whose spatial audio personalization and binaural rendering applications run in the cloud behind a mobile application and locally as plugins in digital audio workstations.
2. Artificial intelligence models that generate personalized head-related transfer function profiles from smartphone ear images, coupled with binaural rendering and spatial audio algorithms.
3. Personalized head-related transfer function generation, binaural rendering, virtual spatial audio mixing, and enhanced spatial awareness for headphones.
4. Software products, mobile applications, and VST plugins delivered to end users and audio professionals.
5. Video games, extended reality, professional studio mixing, digital audio workstations, and consumer headphones.
6. Consumers, PC gamers, musicians, audio professionals, and headset manufacturers.
7. Its software and plugins are bundled with consumer gaming headsets by hardware brands and integrated into digital audio workstation software by audio technology companies.
8. It generates personalized head-related transfer functions using artificial intelligence to analyze images of a user's ear captured by a smartphone.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It has partnered with Audeze, Steinberg, Logitech G, and Astro, and integrates with Apple Music and Dolby Atmos binaural renderers.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: It makes money through software sales, application purchases, and plugin licenses.
Scale and maturity: A startup based in San Mateo, California.
Geography: Based in San Mateo, California, USA, operating in the global consumer and professional audio markets.
Beyond audio: Audio and immersive sound technology is the entire focus of the organization.

points.name: Mimi Hearing Technologies
points.description: Berlin technology company personalizing sound based on individual hearing profiles.
points.bullets:
A software and AI model developer that builds sound personalization, hearing test, and neural audio codec technologies for consumer electronics brands and AI speech model developers. It licenses algorithms and models that adapt audio output to individual hearing profiles, and it develops a low-latency neural audio codec used by cloud-based voice AI. The organization has collected a large database of digital hearing profiles to power its personalization engines.
1. A software and AI model developer whose sound personalization algorithms run on-device in consumer electronics products and whose neural audio codec runs in the cloud behind speech models.
2. Digital hearing test algorithms, hearing-profile-based audio processing, and a transformer-based neural audio codec that distills self-supervised speech representations for low-bitrate audio streaming.
3. Sound personalization, hearing assessment, dialogue and voice clarity enhancement, background noise reduction, and neural audio compression.
4. SDKs, APIs, cloud models, and licensed algorithms integrated into consumer devices, plus mobile hearing test applications.
5. Earbuds, headphones, smartphones, televisions, soundbars, automotive sound systems, smart glasses, in-flight entertainment systems, browser extensions, and cloud-based conversational voice models.
6. Consumer electronics brands, headphone and earbud makers, television manufacturers, automakers, telehealth and health-tech providers, and AI speech model developers.
7. Its algorithms and codecs are integrated by device makers into their hardware and by AI developers into their voice models.
8. It leverages a massive proprietary database of digital hearing profiles to drive its personalized sound adaptation, and its neural codec achieves low-latency, low-bitrate streaming through transformer-based architecture and self-supervised representation distillation.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Nothing, Bragi, Breggz, Creative, Cleer, Montblanc, Apple Health, 3D Sound Labs, Kyutai, WavLM, EnCodec, and SoundStream.
Organization type: A privately held technology company.
Business model: Software licensing, per-unit royalties, API usage fees, and acquired intellectual property.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2014, with over one million hearing test app downloads across 180 countries and a database of over four million hearing tests.
Geography: Based in Berlin, Germany, and operating globally through consumer electronics integrations.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on audio, spanning hearing assessment, sound personalization, and neural audio codecs.

points.name: 3D Sound Labs
points.description: French VR audio startup developing 3D binaural software, smart headphones, and licensing SDKs to third parties.
points.bullets:
A VR audio technology company that develops 3D spatial audio software and hardware, including HRTF-based binaural engines and smart headphones. It licenses its spatial audio technology to third parties and builds finished consumer hardware for immersive listening.
1. An audio software developer whose spatial rendering engines are sold as SDKs and licensed technology, alongside finished consumer hardware devices.
2. HRTF-based Ambisonics binaural rendering engines combined with motion tracking modules for dynamic spatial audio.
3. 3D and VR audio spatial rendering, binaural sound, and motion-tracked head-related transfer function processing.
4. Software development kits, technology licensing programs, and finished smart headphones.
5. Virtual reality experiences and smart headphones.
6. Third-party hardware and software developers, and consumers.
7. Its spatial audio engines are integrated into third-party products while it also sells finished consumer hardware directly.
8. Its combination of HRTF-based Ambisonics binaural rendering with integrated motion tracking modules in both software and hardware.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Acquired by Mimi Hearing Technologies to enhance sound personalization technology with HRTF expertise.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Software licensing, freemium technology licensing programs, and hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: A startup founded in 2014 and acquired by a hearing technology company.
Geography: Based in Paris, France.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on audio technology.

points.name: SteelSeries
points.description: US gaming peripherals manufacturer making wireless headsets and audio software for esports.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer and gaming audio equipment that builds wireless and wired gaming headsets, audio DACs, and companion audio software for gamers.
1. A consumer electronics brand that designs gaming headsets and peripherals sold as finished hardware alongside companion configuration and equalization software.
2. Audio hardware including high-fidelity drivers, wireless transmission protocols, and integrated digital-to-analog converters paired with parametric equalization software.
3. Active noise cancellation, AI-powered noise-canceling microphones, surround sound, multi-system audio switching, and parametric audio equalization.
4. Finished hardware headsets and accessories, plus companion software applications for audio management and device configuration.
5. Gaming headsets used for console and PC gaming, esports, and competitive gaming.
6. Consumers and gamers.
7. Its finished hardware and software are sold directly to consumers through retail channels.
8. Hot-swappable dual-battery systems for continuous wireless power and auto-tuning software profiles optimized for specific game titles.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Owned by GN Group as part of its gaming division, with KontrolFreek and Nahimic as family brands.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand of a publicly traded company.
Business model: Hardware sales of gaming peripherals and headsets.
Scale and maturity: A global gaming peripherals brand established in 2001 and acquired by GN Group in 2022.
Geography: Based in Chicago, Illinois, USA, operating worldwide.
Beyond audio: A gaming and esports peripherals manufacturer that also makes keyboards, mice, and performance thumb grips.

points.name: AudioControl
points.description: Seattle audio electronics manufacturer building amplifiers, processors, and speakers for home, car, and professional sound systems.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of audio equipment that designs and engineers high-performance home theater processors, distributed audio amplifiers, car audio products, and signal processors for consumers and installers.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished audio hardware products including amplifiers, speakers, subwoofers, and signal processors.
2. High-current Class D amplifier designs, digital signal processing for signal summing and equalization, and analog bass restoration circuits.
3. Multi-zone amplification, on-board DSP with graphic and parametric equalization, OEM integration with factory radios, bass restoration, and Dante audio networking.
4. Finished hardware products including amplifiers, speakers, subwoofers, line output converters, and networked multi-zone controllers.
5. Home theaters, distributed home audio systems, car audio systems, and outdoor speaker installations.
6. Consumers, home audio installers, and automotive audio integrators.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold through regional distributors and sales representatives to custom installers and consumers.
8. It leverages a professional audio engineering heritage to build consumer and automotive audio tools designed to overcome listening environment barriers.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: AVPro Global owns the home audio division, AAMP Holdings retains the vehicle technology business, Dirac provides ART technology, Origin Acoustics integrates its amplifiers, and Oceanic Distribution and Sales And Marketing, Inc. handle regional sales.
Organization type: A brand operating under AVPro Global for home audio and AAMP Holdings for vehicle technology.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished audio equipment and electronic devices.
Scale and maturity: A company with a forty-five-year history and U.S.-based research, development, manufacturing, and training facilities.
Geography: Based in Seattle, Washington, USA, with distribution in Australia and the United States Midwest.
Beyond audio: It is a pure-play audio equipment manufacturer.

points.name: Marantz
points.description: Japanese audio brand making amplifiers and A/V receivers.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer and home audio equipment that designs and sells A/V receivers, A/V preamplifiers and amplifiers for home theater and hi-fi consumers.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished audio components sold as hardware products running in home installations.
2. The core technology consists of multi-channel A/V receivers and preamplifiers incorporating amplification, audio decoding and digital signal processing platforms.
3. The components deliver multi-channel audio amplification, surround sound decoding including MPEG-H, and room correction through Dirac Live integration.
4. Customers get the products as finished hardware components with capabilities delivered via firmware updates.
5. The products are used in home theaters and home audio installations.
6. The company sells to consumers and home audio installers.
7. Its finished components are paired with third-party loudspeakers and used directly in consumer home installations.
8. The brand distinguishes itself through artisanal craftsmanship and design in its premium home audio components.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The brand is under Sound United and is being acquired by Harman International from Masimo, with integration support from Dirac and MPEG-H.
Organization type: The organization is a subsidiary brand.
Business model: It makes money through sales of finished hardware components.
Scale and maturity: The brand has been established for nearly 70 years.
Geography: The brand is based in Japan and operates internationally.
Beyond audio: Beyond audio the company has no other focus, as audio is its entire business.

points.name: miniDSP
points.description: Hong Kong audio electronics company making digital signal processors, room correction devices, and measurement microphones for audiophiles and home theater enthusiasts.
points.bullets:
A maker of digital audio processing equipment and measurement tools that develops digital signal processors, USB measurement microphones, and room correction software for audiophiles, engineers, and DIY enthusiasts.
1. An equipment maker that builds digital signal processors, measurement microphones, and audio calibration software, sold as finished hardware and accompanying software products running in home and professional audio systems.
2. Digital signal processing hardware combined with licensed room correction algorithms and USB measurement microphone technology.
3. Room correction, equalization, multichannel acoustic measurement, and subwoofer integration.
4. Finished hardware devices, USB measurement microphones, and licensed software integrated into digital audio processors.
5. Home theater systems, hi-fi setups, headphones, and automotive audio environments.
6. Audiophiles, engineers, and DIY enthusiasts.
7. Its hardware products are used directly by consumers and enthusiasts to process and calibrate audio in their own systems.
8. It bundles licensed third-party room correction software into its own digital signal processor hardware alongside its own USB measurement microphones.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Dirac, whose room correction and ART technology is licensed and integrated into its processors.
Organization type: A privately held audio equipment manufacturer.
Business model: Hardware sales of processors and measurement microphones, combined with licensed software features.
Scale and maturity: An established manufacturer with a broad product portfolio across home, headphone, and automotive audio markets.
Geography: Based in Kowloon Bay, Hong Kong, operating in global consumer and enthusiast markets.
Beyond audio: The organization is a pure-play audio company focused entirely on digital signal processing and acoustic measurement.

points.name: StormAudio
points.description: US-based manufacturer building immersive audio processors and amplifiers for high-end home theaters.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures immersive audio processors, receivers and amplifiers for high-end home theaters, media rooms and private cinemas.
1. An equipment maker that builds high-end audio processors, receivers and amplifiers, sold as finished hardware installed in custom home cinema environments.
2. Digital signal processing for immersive audio decoding and bass management, integrated with digital-to-analog converters and room correction software.
3. Immersive surround sound decoding, multichannel amplification, digital-to-analog conversion and active room treatment.
4. Finished hardware processors, receivers and amplifiers.
5. High-end home theaters, media rooms and private cinemas.
6. Custom installers, audiophiles and home cinema owners.
7. Its processors and amplifiers are sold through custom installation brands and integrators into private home theaters.
8. It builds future-proof, modular and upgradeable processors with flexible digital input and output options and integrated active room treatment.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It integrates Dirac Live Active Room Treatment, uses ESS Sabre DACs, is carried by Pulse Cinemas and partners with ASCENDO and Alcons Audio.
Organization type: A privately held manufacturer with a United States subsidiary and a Hong Kong office.
Business model: Hardware sales of processors, receivers and amplifiers.
Scale and maturity: An established manufacturer with a worldwide presence serving the high-end custom installation market.
Geography: Headquartered in France with a United States subsidiary and a Hong Kong office, operating worldwide.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on high-performance audio electronics for home theaters.

points.name: IK Multimedia
points.description: Italian pro audio company making music software, hardware, and amp modelers for musicians.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of professional audio software and hardware that develops and sells studio monitoring, room correction, amp modeling, and music production tools for musicians and engineers.
1. A maker of professional audio equipment and software whose products run as standalone hardware, software plugins, and finished studio monitors.
2. DSP algorithms for acoustic room correction, machine-modeled guitar amp simulation, and digital audio processing for mixing and mastering.
3. Room correction, acoustic measurement, loudspeaker calibration, guitar amp modeling, MIDI control, and mixing and mastering.
4. Software plugins, standalone hardware processors, finished studio monitors, MIDI controllers, and measurement microphones.
5. Studios, live performance rigs, and desktop music production environments.
6. Musicians, audio engineers, and producers.
7. Its hardware and software products are sold to end users through musical instrument and audio retailers.
8. It provides tightly integrated software and hardware ecosystems for guitar amp modeling and room correction paired with companion measurement microphones.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Retailers include Thomann GmbH and Plugin Boutique.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales and software licenses.
Scale and maturity: A well-established manufacturer with a broad portfolio of multiple product lines sold worldwide.
Geography: Based in Italy with worldwide distribution.
Beyond audio: The company's entire focus is on audio and music production tools.

points.name: Sonarworks
points.description: US audio software company developing calibration tools that personalize sound for headphones and speakers.
points.bullets:
An audio software developer that builds calibration and personalization software for studio monitoring, headphones and consumer audio, as well as voice processing tools for creators, sold to studios, musicians and consumers.
1. An audio software developer whose calibration and personalization products run as standalone applications and plugins on desktop and mobile platforms, and whose voice processing tool runs locally on users' machines.
2. Digital signal processing algorithms for room and headphone correction and machine learning models for audio personalization based on hearing tests and preference data.
3. Room correction, headphone calibration, virtual monitoring, audio personalization and voice processing.
4. Software products sold as standalone applications, plugins and mobile apps, accompanied by individually calibrated measurement microphones as finished hardware.
5. Professional recording studios, post-production facilities, personal listening on mobile devices and creator workflows for voice processing.
6. Recording studios, musicians, creators, consumers and consumer electronics brands.
7. Its software is used directly by creators and consumers for monitoring and listening, and its personalization technology is integrated by headphone manufacturers into their products.
8. It combines individually calibrated measurement microphones with software that applies correction profiles across entire system audio or within specific plugins.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Universal Audio, 1MORE and Thomann.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Software licenses, perpetual licenses, pay-as-you-go usage fees and hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: Established company whose software is used in over 45,000 professional recording studios and by close to 100 Grammy-winning creators.
