8. It operates a model-agnostic architecture with a bring-your-own-key model that separates platform usage costs from underlying model and carrier expenses.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Integrates with OpenAI, Deepgram, ElevenLabs, AssemblyAI, Twilio, Telnyx, and Plivo.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Platform usage subscriptions and connected duration fees, with pass-through billing for model providers, carrier services, and add-ons.
Scale and maturity: An established platform in the voice AI orchestration market.
Geography: Based in the USA and operates in the cloud.
Beyond audio: Its focus is entirely on voice AI infrastructure and orchestration.

points.name: Synthflow AI
points.description: German startup providing a no-code platform for building AI voice agents that automate phone calls.
points.bullets:
A cloud software and AI model developer that provides a no-code platform for enterprises to build and deploy AI voice agents that automate real-world phone conversations. The platform enables the creation of natural-sounding voice agents for inbound and outbound calling without requiring technical expertise. It supports multilingual conversational workflows, CRM integration, and telephony connectivity.
1. An AI model and software developer whose conversational voice agents and no-code platform run in the cloud behind a telephony infrastructure and API.

5. Enterprise contact centres and live voice agent deployments.
6. Enterprises deploying voice agents in customer service environments.
7. Its models are integrated by enterprises into their contact centre and customer service applications.
8. Its audio-native speech-to-speech model is built for live interaction with native handling of interruptions, turn-taking, and proactive anticipation of user needs.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Deployed in a global insurance company's contact centre.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Scale and maturity: An early-stage startup co-founded by Alex Smola.
Beyond audio: The company also develops multimodal interaction tools including avatars and benchmarks for evaluating voice agent behavior.

points.name: Moises
points.location: Salt Lake City, Utah, United States
points.description: US AI music software company providing tools for musicians to separate tracks, practice, and create.
points.bullets:
An AI software developer that builds AI-based music production and practice tools, including stem separation, chord detection, pitch and tempo shifting, AI mastering, and voice modeling, for musicians and audio creatives.
1. An AI model developer whose audio separation, mastering, and voice transformation models run in the cloud behind an API and as applications on mobile, desktop, and web clients.
2. Generative and discriminative neural networks for audio source separation, chord estimation, pitch shifting, and voice transformation running in the cloud.
3. Stem separation, chord detection, pitch and tempo shifting, audio mastering, and AI-powered voice modeling.
4. Mobile and desktop applications, a browser-based digital audio workstation, and a cloud service accessed through subscription tiers with a free plan.
5. Mobile and desktop music production and practice environments, digital audio workstations, and online music creation platforms.
6. Musicians, songwriters, producers, and music enthusiasts, from beginners to professionals.
7. Its applications are used directly by musicians and integrated with music distribution and creation platforms.
8. Its AI models are trained exclusively on licensed material, with royalties paid to rights holders, and it combines stem separation with practice-oriented features like chord detection.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its platform integrates with SoundCloud, runs on Apple iOS and Google Play, and is backed by investors including Monashees, Kickstart Fund, Norwest, Toba Capital, Alumni Ventures, Goodwater, and Valutia.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Software subscriptions with a free tier and paid plans.
Scale and maturity: It has over 30 million registered users and over 80 million musicians working with its platform.
Geography: It is based in Salt Lake City, Utah, United States.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is on AI-based audio tools for music creation and practice.

points.name: Runway
points.description: New York AI company providing generative video, voice, sound effect, and music tools for creative production workflows.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer and platform company that builds generative video and audio models for media creation. It provides cloud-based generative audio tools for voice, sound effects and music, alongside video generation models that produce synchronized dialogue and ambient sound. It serves creators and developers through its own workspace, a unified API and integrations with creative software platforms.
1. An AI model developer whose video and audio models run in the cloud behind an API and a web workspace.
2. Large generative video and audio models, including cinematic video generation workflows and world models, running in the cloud.
3. Generative audio for voice, sound effects and music, alongside text-to-video generation, native synchronized audio generation, video editing and interactive simulation.
4. Cloud APIs, a web-based workspace, a unified API with a model router and third-party model integrations.
5. Creative workflows for video production, cinematic generation, media editing and interactive simulation.
6. Creators, developers and enterprises using generative media in production.
7. Its models are integrated by creative software platforms into their generative media tools and accessed by developers through its API.
8. It consolidates multiple third-party generative video, image and audio models alongside its own into a single unified API with a model router.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Adobe integrates its models into Firefly, Shutterstock supplies training data and its API consolidates models from ElevenLabs.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Software subscriptions, API usage and free tiers.
Scale and maturity: A global brand and startup offering multiple generations of video and world models.
Geography: Based in New York, USA and operating globally.
Beyond audio: It develops general video generation, world simulation and robotics training models beyond audio.

points.name: Gemini
points.description: New Jersey audio equipment manufacturer building portable PA systems and DJ gear.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio and mobile DJ equipment that designs and manufactures finished hardware including DJ controllers, mixers, turntables, portable PA systems, powered loudspeakers, wireless microphones, and compact USB mixers for performers, DJs, and sound contractors.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished professional audio hardware and consumer electronics sold as physical products.
2. Analog and digital audio electronics, integrated mixers, Bluetooth connectivity, and amplifier designs packaged into road-ready physical enclosures.
3. Audio mixing, DJ playback control, wireless microphone transmission, sound reinforcement, and Bluetooth audio streaming with TWS stereo linking.
4. Customers get it as finished hardware products and physical devices, alongside genuine replacement parts and accessories.
5. DJ performances, live sound events, mobile entertainment, podcasting setups, houses of worship, and home audio environments.
6. DJs, musicians, sound contractors, mobile entertainers, and consumers.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to performers, consumers, and sound installers for live and recorded audio applications.
8. A fifty-year DJ equipment heritage focuses on balancing performance and value across a complete range of mobile entertainment and sound reinforcement hardware.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A third-generation, family-owned audio equipment manufacturer operating under the parent company GCI Technologies.
Organization type: A privately held company and subsidiary brand.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished audio equipment and physical replacement parts.
Scale and maturity: A well-established company founded in 1974 with over fifty years in the audio equipment manufacturing industry.
Geography: Headquartered in New Jersey, USA, with products supplied to markets worldwide.
Beyond audio: Audio equipment manufacturing is its entire focus.

points.name: Moises.AI
points.description: Software company building AI apps that separate music tracks into individual instruments and vocals.
points.bullets:
An AI software developer that builds cloud-based and desktop audio processing applications for musicians, providing stem separation, lyric transcription, and chord identification from recorded tracks.
1. An AI software developer whose audio models run in the cloud behind a web and mobile application, with additional desktop plugin forms.
2. Deep learning models that analyze mixed audio recordings to isolate individual instrument and vocal components and recognize musical structure.
3. Audio stem separation, lyric transcription, and chord identification.
4. Finished software products delivered as web, desktop, and mobile applications, with Pro Plan features offered as plugins.
5. Digital audio workstations, music production studios, and practice environments for musicians.
6. Musicians and music producers.
7. Its AI models are embedded into third-party digital audio workstations and studio software as a core feature.
8. Separates tracks into a high count of specific instruments and two distinct vocal tracks alongside lyric and chord recognition.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Ableton Live and Fender Studio DAW integrate its stem separation technology.
Organization type: A privately held technology company.
Business model: Software subscriptions and application sales.
Geography: Operates online globally.
Beyond audio: Its focus is entirely on audio processing for music applications.

points.name: LANDR
points.description: Canadian music technology startup providing automated audio mastering, stem separation, and digital distribution for independent artists.
points.bullets:
An audio software and service company that provides an AI-powered platform for music creation, production, mastering, and distribution for independent musicians and producers.
1. A software and service company that builds AI mastering engines, stem separation plugins, and digital distribution tools, sold as cloud services, DAW plugins, and subscription bundles running on desktop and mobile platforms.
2. Machine learning algorithms that analyze track styles and enhance audio parameters based on a reference library, and AI stem separation algorithms licensed from a third party.
3. Automated audio mastering, stem separation, vocal removal, digital music distribution, sample library access, and remote collaboration.
4. Cloud APIs, DAW plugins in VST3, AU, and AAX formats, desktop and mobile applications, and subscription bundles.
5. Digital audio workstations, music production studios, mobile music creation, and streaming platforms.
6. Independent musicians, producers, content creators, and software developers.
7. Its plugins and services are used directly by independent artists for music production and its mastering API is integrated by developers into their own software.
8. It combines AI mastering, stem separation, samples, plugins, collaboration tools, and digital distribution under a single subscription bundle.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its stem separation is powered by AudioShake, and it acquired Reason Studios.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Software subscriptions, API usage, and music distribution fees.
Scale and maturity: A startup in the portfolio of a venture firm.
Geography: Operates online globally.
Beyond audio: It also offers digital music distribution to streaming platforms and promotional tools for independent artists.

points.name: Omnisale
points.description: Swiss technology company developing AI-powered audio stem separation and voice cleaning tools.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer that builds and operates an AI-powered audio stem separation and voice cleaning platform for musicians, producers, and audio engineers.
1. An AI model developer whose audio stem separation models run in the cloud behind an API and are packaged into consumer software applications and plugins.
2. Neural networks for audio source separation that isolate individual instrument and vocal stems from mixed audio recordings.
3. The platform delivers audio stem separation, vocal isolation, and voice cleaning.
4. Customers access it through web, desktop, and mobile applications, as well as audio plugin formats.
5. The technology is used in studios, music production workflows, and post-production environments.
6. The company sells to consumers, musicians, producers, and audio engineers.
7. Its models are delivered directly to end-users through its own software applications and plugins.
8. Its approach centers on a proprietary neural network designed specifically for high-fidelity audio stem separation.
points.profile:
Organization type: The organization is a privately held company.
Business model: It makes money through software subscriptions and usage fees for its stem separation platform.
Scale and maturity: The company has been active and launching neural network models since 2020.
Geography: It is based in Zug, Switzerland, and operates its platform globally online.
Beyond audio: The company focuses entirely on AI-powered audio processing.

points.name: Gaudio Lab
points.description: South Korean AI audio company separating and remastering sound for content.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer and software provider that builds cloud-based and on-device AI models for audio source separation, content localization, spatial upmixing, and loudness management for global content partners.
1. An AI model developer whose audio models run in the cloud behind web applications and APIs, and on-device in mobile apps, with a primary business in software products and SaaS.
2. Neural networks for audio source separation, multimodal generative AI for sound effects synthesis, and spatial rendering algorithms.
3. Audio source separation into individual stems, vocal removal, noise reduction, sound effects generation, multi-lingual AI dubbing, spatial upmixing, and broadcast-standard loudness normalization.
4. Cloud-based web SaaS applications, mobile apps, and licensed SDKs.
5. Content localization workflows, broadcast production, audio post-production, and mobile voice recording.
6. Global content partners, broadcast studios, audio engineers, and consumers.
7. Its models and SDKs are integrated by content creators and studios into their localization and production workflows.
8. Its source separation model isolates audio into discrete instrument stems and it licenses a binaural renderer that is an ISO/IEC international standard.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Strategic investors include SBVA, Samsung Venture Investment, and Naver Corp, with a subsidiary named Wavelab.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Software licenses, SaaS subscriptions, and licensed SDKs.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2015, award-winning, and backed by major corporate venture investors.
Geography: Headquartered in Seoul, South Korea with a subsidiary in Berkeley, California.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on audio technology.

points.name: zplane
points.description: Berlin software company developing and licensing audio processing algorithms and plugins for the music industry.
points.bullets:
An audio software company that develops and licenses DSP algorithms, SDKs, and consumer plugins for the music industry, providing intelligent signal processing for music analysis, pitch and time manipulation, and audio separation.
1. An audio software developer whose algorithms and SDKs are licensed to music software companies and whose consumer plugins run inside DAWs.
2. Digital signal processing algorithms for time-stretching, pitch detection, tempo and beat tracking, convolution reverb, and real-time stem separation.
3. Time-stretching, pitch shifting and detection, tempo and beat tracking, harmonization, audio metering, real-time stem separation, and convolution reverb.
4. Licensed algorithms, SDKs, APIs, and consumer software plugins.
5. Digital audio workstations, music production software, and audio processing pipelines.
6. Music software developers, audio technology companies, and musicians.
7. Its DSP algorithms and SDKs are integrated by music software companies into their DAWs and production platforms.
8. It supplies foundational music analysis and time-stretching algorithms to major audio software companies while also selling its own consumer plugins.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Ableton, Dolby, Native Instruments, Sweetwater, Plugin Boutique, and Gemini.
Organization type: An independent, privately held audio software company.
Business model: Software licensing for SDKs and algorithms, and direct sales of consumer plugins.
Scale and maturity: A company founded in 2000 with over 25 years of experience in the audio industry.
Geography: Based in Berlin, Germany, and operating internationally.
Beyond audio: The organization's entire focus is audio technology.

points.name: LALAL.AI
points.description: Swiss software company developing AI tools for separating vocals and instruments from audio tracks.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer and software company that builds neural network models for audio stem separation and voice processing, offering web services, APIs, plugins, and desktop and mobile apps for musicians, content creators, and enterprises.
1. An AI model developer whose audio separation and voice models run in the cloud behind an API and on-device inside desktop, mobile, and plugin software.
2. Transformer-based neural networks that analyze audio time, frequency, and tone to isolate discrete sound sources.
3. Stem separation, vocal isolation, lead and backing vocal splitting, echo and reverb removal, voice cleaning, voice changing, and voice cloning.
4. Cloud APIs, native desktop and mobile applications, a VST3 plugin, and enterprise integrations.
5. Digital audio workstations, audio production workflows, sports broadcasting platforms, and mobile content creation.
6. Musicians, content creators, third-party developers, and enterprises.
7. Its models and APIs are integrated into third-party content platforms to automate audio processing workflows.
8. Its proprietary neural network models support extraction of up to ten distinct stem types with a focus on high separation quality and offline plugin processing.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Slate integrates its API to remove copyrighted music from sports footage, and the platform operates under OmniSale GmbH.
Organization type: A privately held software company and subsidiary brand.
Business model: Software subscriptions, API usage fees, and enterprise service contracts.
Scale and maturity: An established service launched in 2020 with multiple iterations of proprietary neural network models.
Geography: Based in Zug, Switzerland, and operating online globally.
Beyond audio: Audio processing is its entire focus.

points.name: Audo
points.description: Software company providing AI-powered tools for cleaning up audio and enhancing speech recordings.
points.bullets:
An AI software developer that builds cloud-based models and tools for audio and video enhancement, providing speech cleanup, stem separation, and transcription services through a web platform and API for developers, creators, and AI assistants.
1. An AI software developer whose models and tools run in the cloud behind a web platform and API.
2. Cloud-based neural networks process uploaded media to suppress noise, separate audio stems, transcribe speech, and isolate vocal tracks.
3. Noise removal, echo removal, voice isolation, dereverberation, vocal and stem separation, speech-to-text transcription, pitch and tempo shifting, and audio format conversion.
4. Cloud APIs, a web-based platform, and free links that AI assistants use to process and return enhanced files.
5. Recorded speech, music tracks, video soundtracks, and media files for transcription, content creation, and AI agent workflows.
6. Developers, content creators, and AI assistant platforms.
7. Its models and tools are accessed directly by end users and integrated by developers and AI assistants via API.
8. It provides a broad suite of targeted audio tools that either reconstruct or isolate voice while keeping the original signal untouched, alongside format conversion and transcription in a single platform.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: AI assistant platforms ChatGPT and Claude.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: API usage with pay-as-you-go pricing and a free tier.
Scale and maturity: An early-stage company offering a free tier and pay-as-you-go products.
Geography: Operates as a cloud platform serving users globally.

points.name: Widex
points.description: Danish hearing aid manufacturer producing devices that use natural signal processing to preserve sound quality and reduce noise.
points.bullets:
A hearing aid manufacturer that designs and sells prescription hearing aids, fitting software, and companion accessories for hearing care professionals and end users.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished hearing aids, accessories, and cloud-based fitting software.
2. Digital signal processing with ultra-low-latency time-domain filter banks, adaptive directional systems, and machine learning algorithms for sound personalization.
3. Noise reduction, speech intelligibility enhancement, feedback cancellation, directional beamforming, tinnitus sound therapy, and on-demand deep neural network processing.
4. Finished hardware devices, smartphone apps, and cloud-based fitting software.
5. Prescription hearing aids, tinnitus management devices, and remote hearing care services.
6. Hearing care professionals, audiology clinics, and end-use consumers.
7. Its finished hearing aids are sold to and dispensed by hearing care professionals to end users.
8. A design philosophy focused on preserving natural auditory cues through ultra-low-latency processing, complemented by user-controlled, on-demand neural network processing.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A brand operating under WS Audiology, integrating with Apple Watch, distributed by Hearing Dynamics and TruDensity, and a member of BIHIMA.
Organization type: A hearing aid brand and subsidiary of WS Audiology.
Business model: Hardware sales of hearing aids and accessories, plus software services for professionals.
Scale and maturity: A historically top-six global hearing aid brand operating in over 100 countries with thousands of employees, now folded into a larger parent company.
Geography: Based in Lynge, Denmark, with an American subsidiary and global distribution.
Beyond audio: The organization is a pure-play audio and hearing healthcare company.

points.name: Audio Analytic
points.description: Technology company developing sound recognition software for consumer devices.
points.bullets:
An AI model and software developer that builds sound recognition systems and datasets for consumer device makers. It develops inference platforms for embedding acoustic event and scene recognition into low-power consumer hardware, and provides large labeled audio datasets for training sound recognition models.
1. An AI model developer whose sound recognition models and datasets run on-device in consumer electronics hardware.
2. Deep neural networks trained on large labeled audio datasets run as compact inference engines on low-memory, low-power devices.
3. Acoustic event recognition, acoustic scene recognition, and sound tagging across a wide range of sound classes.
4. Software development kits, inference platforms, and datasets licensed to device manufacturers.
5. Smartphones, smart speakers, and hearables.
6. Consumer device makers.
7. Its models and datasets are integrated into consumer electronic devices by device manufacturers.
8. It pairs a proprietary large-scale labeled sound dataset with compact inference engines optimized for low-power edge devices.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its technology is pre-validated to run on Qualcomm's Snapdragon 888 Sensing Hub.
Organization type: Privately held technology company.
Business model: Software licenses and dataset licensing.
Geography: Based and operates in markets serving global consumer electronics manufacturers.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is on sound recognition technology for consumer devices.

points.name: Reality Defender
points.description: New York cybersecurity startup detecting synthetic audio deepfakes for enterprises and governments.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer whose deepfake detection models run in the cloud behind APIs and SDKs, analyzing media for enterprises, governments, and media organizations.
1. An AI model developer whose detection models run in the cloud behind APIs and SDKs.
2. Specialized neural networks for audio, image, and video detection combined through ensemble fusion.
3. Real-time detection of AI-generated synthetic voice and manipulated media with low-latency risk scoring and forensics review.
4. Cloud APIs, SDKs, a web application, video meeting plugins, and private deployment options.
5. Call centers, telephony systems, video meetings, media upload workflows, banks, and marketplaces.
6. Enterprises, governments, media organizations, and developers.
7. Its detection APIs and SDKs are integrated by enterprises into their content management systems, communication platforms, and incident response workflows.
8. Its platform is stateless by design, meaning nothing is enrolled or stored, and it uses continuous model retraining on diverse datasets covering multiple languages and real-world distortion conditions.
points.profile:
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Software licenses, subscriptions, and API usage fees.
Scale and maturity: A startup that has released a free API and multiple dataset iterations and was recognized by a major bank for innovation.
Geography: Based in New York, USA.
Beyond audio: It is an AI and cybersecurity company that secures communication channels against deepfake impersonations across audio, video, images, and text.

points.name: Pindrop
points.description: US startup detecting deepfakes and analyzing voice interactions to secure customer service calls.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer whose voice security models run in the cloud behind an API, providing voice authentication, liveness detection and deepfake detection for enterprises and contact centers.
1. An AI model developer whose voice security models run in the cloud behind a SaaS API.
2. Machine learning and audio analysis algorithms that evaluate call audio, background signals, voice biometrics and acoustic features to distinguish human voices from synthetic speech.
3. Passive voice authentication, voice liveness detection, synthetic voice and deepfake detection, and fraud risk assessment.
4. Cloud SaaS APIs and software products.
5. Contact centers, telephony environments, live meeting audio and customer service operations.
6. Financial institutions, insurers, healthcare organizations, retailers and large enterprises.
7. Its models are integrated by cloud telephony platforms into customer service operations.
8. It continuously analyzes call audio background signals to authenticate callers passively while detecting synthetic audio in seconds.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It integrates with Amazon Connect, is an AWS Partner, and partnered with SK Telecom.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Software licenses, API usage and cloud subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: Over 15 years of enterprise-scale experience with over 300 patents.
Geography: Based in the United States with operations extending to South Korea.
Beyond audio: It is a pure-play audio security company focused entirely on voice fraud prevention and authentication.

points.name: Modulate
points.description: US technology company developing AI voice moderation for online gaming and audio deepfake detection.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer that builds voice analysis models for detecting audio deepfakes and moderating online voice chat, providing security and moderation services for gaming platforms and enterprises.
1. An AI model developer whose detection and moderation models run in the cloud behind an API.
2. Deep neural networks and explainable AI algorithms process voice chat streams to classify harmful content and synthesized speech.
3. Audio deepfake detection, toxic behavior detection, hate speech recognition, harassment detection, and fraud prevention.
4. Cloud APIs and voice-native moderation services.
5. Online gaming voice chats, gig platform communications, and enterprise voice agent supervision.
6. Game publishers and developers, gig economy platforms, and enterprises.
7. Its moderation services are integrated by gaming platforms into their voice chat systems to monitor user behavior.
8. It focuses on explainable, configurable AI architectures rather than single massive models, achieving low false positive rates while analyzing millions of hours of audio.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Future Ventures, AWS, Nintendo, and integration with games like Call of Duty.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: API usage and service subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: Raised $25 million in funding.
Geography: Based in the United States.
Beyond audio: Its technology extends to general content moderation and fraud prevention in non-audio online interactions.

points.name: IngenID
points.description: US software startup providing AI-driven voice biometric platforms for identity verification and deepfake detection.
points.bullets:
A SaaS startup that provides AI-driven voice biometrics and deepfake detection platforms for identity verification and voice security, serving small to mid-sized businesses in sectors such as law enforcement, online education, healthcare, and banking.
1. An AI model developer whose voice biometric and deepfake detection models run in the cloud behind an API, delivered as a software-as-a-service platform.
2. Neural networks for speaker verification and adaptive deepfake detection, with acoustic watermarking techniques under development to trace and protect original audio sources.
3. Speaker verification, deepfake detection, identity verification, and acoustic watermarking for audio source tracing.
4. Cloud-based software-as-a-service platforms and APIs.
5. Identity verification and voice security systems in law enforcement, online education, healthcare, banking, and multi-factor authentication.
6. Small to mid-sized businesses in law enforcement, online education, healthcare, and banking.
7. Its cloud-based voice biometric platforms are integrated by enterprises into their identity verification and multi-factor authentication systems.
8. Adaptive deepfake detection models paired with voice biometrics, with acoustic watermarking under development to trace and protect original audio sources against AI-generated manipulation.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: CyberloQ for multi-factor authentication integration, and academic or regional partners for research and entrepreneurial support.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Software-as-a-service subscriptions and API usage.
Scale and maturity: Launched in 2021, operating as an early-stage startup.
Geography: Based in Rochester, New York, USA, serving businesses across multiple sectors.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on AI-driven voice biometrics and audio security, with no activity outside audio.

points.name: Edge Impulse
points.description: Software platform building and deploying TinyML machine learning models for audio recognition on edge devices.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company whose platform engineers use to build, train, and deploy machine learning models on edge devices, providing data collection, optimization, and firmware generation for embedded audio and sensor applications.

2. Cloud-based development environment and optimization tools that generate small-footprint neural networks and DSP blocks for tinyML hardware.
3. On-device audio classification, wake-word detection, voice command recognition, and cough detection.
4. Cloud-based platform access, SDKs, exported TensorFlow Lite model libraries, WebAssembly libraries, and generated firmware.
5. Hearables, tinyML boards, and microcontroller-based edge devices.
6. Developers and engineers building embedded machine learning applications.
7. Its development platform is used by engineers to design and deploy models onto third-party edge hardware.
8. Provides an automated development pipeline and optimization tools specifically for high-performance, small-footprint machine learning models constrained by tinyML memory and power limits.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Partners with Ambiq, Arduino, Syntiant, and POLYN Technology, with leadership experience at Qualcomm.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Subscription and usage-based platform access for model development and deployment.

points.name: Picovoice

3. Wake word detection, speech-to-intent recognition, speech-to-text transcription, noise suppression, speaker recognition, and voice activity detection.
4. Software development kits, on-device edge AI models, and a web-based console for training custom voice models.
5. Custom voice products, smart hardware, and microphone arrays.
6. Developers and product builders creating custom voice interfaces.
7. Its edge models and design platform are used by developers to build voice interfaces integrated into third-party hardware.
8. Its platform processes voice entirely on-device, providing low latency and privacy compliance without relying on cloud connectivity.

Key partners and customers: Its platform is integrated with hardware from Seeed Studio.

Business model: Software licenses and platform subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2018.
Geography: Based in Vancouver, Canada.

points.name: Cleer

A maker of consumer audio equipment that designs and markets true wireless open-ear earbuds, over-ear headphones, and smart speakers, incorporating spatial audio, active noise cancellation, and high-resolution wireless audio technologies for consumers.

5. Consumer earbuds, over-ear headphones, and smart speakers.

points.name: Doppler Labs

points.description: US hearing aid manufacturer building affordable AI-powered over-the-counter hearing aids with real-time translation and tinnitus relief.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of over-the-counter hearing aids that designs proprietary audio processing algorithms and integrates them into finished wearable devices for consumers.
1. A hearing aid maker that builds proprietary DSP algorithms and embeds them in finished wearable hardware sold to consumers.
2. Deep neural network algorithms running on a proprietary audio processing chip within the hearing aid.
3. The devices deliver AI-driven noise reduction, speech separation, feedback cancellation, directional microphones, real-time language translation, and tinnitus masking.
4. The company provides its audio technology embedded in finished hearing aid hardware, accompanied by a mobile application for user configuration.
5. The technology is used in over-the-counter, completely-in-canal hearing aids.
6. The company sells finished hearing devices directly to consumers.
7. The company is a vertically integrated brand that develops its own algorithms and chips, manufactures finished devices, and sells them directly to end users.
8. The company pairs medical-grade over-the-counter hearing aids with proprietary deep neural network chips and algorithms for real-time speech isolation and translation.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The organization collaborates with global tech leaders, professional audiology teams, and research institutes.
Organization type: The company is an integrated, privately held brand encompassing research, manufacturing, and global sales operations.
Business model: The company generates revenue through the direct sale of finished hearing aid hardware to consumers.
Scale and maturity: The company offers multiple FDA-registered products and operates global sales operations for its devices.
Geography: The organization is based in Las Vegas, Nevada, USA, and conducts global sales operations.
Beyond audio: The company's entire focus is on hearing aids and auditory technology.

points.name: Oticon
points.description: Danish hearing aid manufacturer developing hearing aids with deep neural networks and BrainHearing technology.
points.bullets:
A maker of finished hearing aid hardware that designs its own DSP chipsets and embeds on-device deep neural networks to provide adaptive sound processing for hearing-impaired end users.
1. An equipment maker that designs and manufactures finished hearing aids containing custom DSP chips, sold as wearable medical devices running on-device.
2. Deep neural networks and custom digital signal processors run on-device inside the hearing aids to process sound.
3. The organization delivers AI-driven noise reduction, speech enhancement, feedback cancellation, wind noise handling, beamforming, and wireless audio streaming.
4. Customers get the technology as finished hearing aids and companion wireless accessories, supported by professional fitting software.
5. The devices are used in hearing aids, including behind-the-ear and in-the-ear models, for adults and children with hearing loss.
6. The organization sells to hearing care professionals, audiology clinics, and public health systems, which fit the devices for end users.
7. Its finished hearing aids are distributed through audiology clinics and hearing care providers to consumers.
8. The approach is distinguished by integrating purpose-built DSP chipsets with on-device deep neural networks trained on millions of sound scenes to preserve environmental context rather than just suppressing noise.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The organization operates as a brand under Demant A/S and uses Bluetooth LE Audio, Apple Made for iPhone, and Android ASHA connectivity.
Organization type: It is a subsidiary brand of a publicly traded company.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of hearing aids and accessories.
Scale and maturity: It is a large, long-established manufacturer with over a century of history, over 20,000 employees, and revenues around DKK 18 billion.
Geography: It is based in Copenhagen, Denmark, and operates globally.
Beyond audio: Beyond audio, the organization incorporates digital health features such as activity tracking and tinnitus relief into its wearable devices.

points.name: Signia
points.description: German hearing aid manufacturer building AI-powered hearing platforms for dynamic sound environments.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of finished hearing aid hardware that designs proprietary audio processing chips and deep neural network platforms to deliver adaptive sound processing for hearing-impaired consumers.
1. An equipment maker that designs and sells finished wearable hearing aid hardware with embedded proprietary chips and companion mobile software to consumers through hearing clinics.
2. Deep neural networks and acoustic processing algorithms running on proprietary dual-core audio chips embedded in hearing aids.
3. Speech detection and enhancement, own-voice processing, ambient scene adaptation, dynamic noise control, beamforming and Bluetooth audio streaming.
4. Prescription and over-the-counter finished hearing aids, behind-the-ear and in-the-ear hardware, companion mobile apps and remote care platforms.
5. Hearing aids, in-the-ear hearables and remote audiology appointments.
6. Hearing clinics, audiology practices, retail hearing networks and end-use consumers.
7. Its finished hearing aids and proprietary audio processing chips are sold through audiology practices and retail hearing networks to end-use consumers.
8. It runs four task-specific deep neural networks simultaneously on a proprietary chip to continuously share information and adapt processing in dynamic, multi-talker environments.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It is a brand under WS Audiology and co-developed hearing aids with hear.com.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand under WS Audiology.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished hearing aids and companion accessories through audiology channels.
Scale and maturity: A global hearing aid brand with technology originating from Siemens and operating under WS Audiology.
Geography: Based in Germany with a global commercial presence.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is hearing aids and audiology support services.

points.name: EssilorLuxottica
points.description: French eyewear manufacturer producing smart glasses and over-the-counter hearing aid glasses.
points.bullets:
A maker of finished audio hardware and wearable devices that designs, manufactures and sells smart glasses with embedded audio and over-the-counter hearing aid capabilities for consumers.
1. An equipment maker that builds smart glasses and companion software, sold as finished consumer hardware running on integrated silicon.
2. Beamforming technology and software as a medical device running on the glasses, calibrated through a companion mobile application.
3. Conversation focus, directional amplification, noise reduction and open-ear audio playback.
4. Finished hardware devices and a companion mobile application sold through owned retail chains and authorized optical retailers.
5. Wearable smart glasses and over-the-counter hearing aids for adults with mild to moderate hearing loss.
6. Consumers seeking eyewear, vision care products and hearing enhancement.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to consumers through owned retail stores and licensed optical chains.
8. Integrating over-the-counter hearing aid technology and software as a medical device directly into consumer eyewear.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Co-develops smart glasses with Meta, powered by Qualcomm silicon, using Transitions lenses under license.
Organization type: Publicly traded company traded on Euronext Paris.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished devices and eyewear through retail channels.
Scale and maturity: A global corporation with over 200,000 employees, 600 operations facilities and 18,000 stores that generated €26.5 billion in revenue in 2024.
Geography: Based in Paris, France, with global retail and manufacturing operations.
Beyond audio: A global leader in the design, manufacture and distribution of advanced vision care products, eyewear and med-tech solutions.

points.name: Nuance Audio
points.description: Israeli smart glasses brand developing audio eyewear with directional microphones and open-ear speakers for OTC hearing assistance.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer hardware that builds over-the-counter hearing assistance smart glasses for people with hearing loss.
1. An equipment maker that designs and sells finished smart glasses hardware that runs its own embedded audio processing.
2. Directional beamforming algorithms running on an embedded array of six microphones paired with open-ear speakers.
3. Sound amplification, directional beamforming and speech clarity in noisy environments.
4. Finished hardware smart glasses with embedded microphones, speakers and physical volume controls.
5. Over-the-counter hearing aids and wearable assistive listening devices.
6. Consumers with hearing loss.
7. Its finished assistive hardware is sold directly to consumers as an alternative to traditional in-ear hearing aids.
8. It integrates hearing assistance directional microphone arrays and open-ear speakers into eyewear frames without in-ear devices.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: EssilorLuxottica.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand of a publicly traded eyewear conglomerate.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: A brand with a shipping second-generation consumer product starting at $829.
Geography: Based in Israel and operating under a global eyewear parent company.
Beyond audio: It operates entirely within audio and vision-integrated hearing assistance.

points.name: Cearvol
points.description: Las Vegas startup building AI-powered hearing wearables and smart glasses for mild to moderate hearing loss.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer hearing wearables that designs and sells AI-powered smart hearing glasses and hearing aids for individuals with mild to moderate hearing loss.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished hearing wearables and smart glasses sold as consumer hardware devices worn on the head.
2. An AI platform performing real-time environmental analysis integrated into wearable open-ear hardware.
3. The devices deliver hearing assistance and environmental sound analysis for mild to moderate hearing loss.
4. Customers get the technology as finished hardware devices, including smart hearing glasses and open-ear hearing aids.
5. The wearables are used by individuals with mild to moderate hearing loss in everyday environments.
6. The company sells directly to consumers with hearing loss.
7. Its finished hardware devices are sold directly to end users as complete wearable products.
8. The company combines hearing aids with smart glasses form factors, including models with open-ear designs and touchscreen charging cases.
points.profile:
Organization type: The organization is a privately held startup.
Geography: The company is based in Las Vegas, Nevada, USA and presented its products at CES.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on audio hearing wearables and does not operate outside of this domain.

points.name: Ceretone
points.description: US hearing aid manufacturer building tiny, FDA-cleared OTC hearing aids.
points.bullets:
A maker of finished audio hardware that designs and sells over-the-counter invisible-in-canal hearing aids for consumers with mild to moderate hearing loss.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished hearing aids which run as standalone wearable devices.
2. The hearing aids use audio processing chips integrated into a one-gram in-ear form factor with a charging case.
3. The devices deliver hearing amplification, tinnitus masking, and selectable listening presets for different environments.
4. The organization provides finished wearable hardware paired with a charging case.
5. The products are used as invisible-in-canal hearing aids.
6. The company sells directly to consumers.
7. Its finished hearing aids are purchased directly by end users.
points.profile:
Organization type: The organization is a privately held company.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales.
Geography: The company is based in Las Vegas, Nevada, USA.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on hearing aids.

points.name: Kardome
points.description: Israeli technology company developing spatial hearing AI for voice recognition in smart devices and vehicles.
points.bullets:
An AI model and software developer whose on-device voice AI models and algorithms run on edge devices in cars and smart devices. It builds a spatial hearing and voice processing layer that localizes speakers, suppresses noise and processes intent on-device for consumer electronics, automotive and enterprise hardware developers.
1. An AI model developer whose on-device voice AI models and algorithms are sold as a development suite or licensed to device manufacturers and run on-device at the edge.
2. Neural networks and spatial sound analysis algorithms that infer room impulse responses to determine relative sound source locations and run on edge devices.
3. Sound source localization, speaker separation, beamforming, noise suppression, spatial audio capture for IVAS transmission and contextual intent processing.
4. Software development kits, licensed algorithms and on-device AI models integrated into hardware developers' products.
5. Car infotainment and voice recognition systems, smart home devices and smart televisions.
6. Device manufacturers, automakers and consumer electronics brands.
7. Its software and models are integrated by device manufacturers into their finished products.
8. It uses acoustic clustering to infer room impulse responses and spatially separate speakers into distinct streams rather than relying on standard noise suppression alone.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: LG Electronics, NVIDIA and KT.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Software licenses and per-unit royalties.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2019.
Geography: Based in Tel Aviv, Israel.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is on-device voice AI technology.

points.name: GN Hearing
points.description: Danish hearing aid manufacturer developing intelligent hearing solutions with wireless connectivity and AI integration.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of hearing aids and related audio accessories that designs, produces, and sells finished hearing instruments under multiple proprietary brands, integrating traditional signal processing with deep neural networks for hearing healthcare professionals and consumers.
1. A finished hardware equipment maker whose hearing aids and audio accessories run as self-contained wearable devices on users.
2. Deep neural networks for denoising and environment classification run alongside traditional digital signal processing, beamforming algorithms, and 2.4 GHz wireless connectivity on low-power hearing aid chips.
3. Environmental sound classification, binaural directional beamforming, DNN-based noise suppression, own-voice detection, digital feedback suppression, spatial audio rendering, and Bluetooth LE Audio streaming.
4. The company provides finished hearing aid hardware, wireless accessory devices, and companion mobile and fitting software products.
5. The products are used in hearing aids, CROS systems for single-sided deafness, over-the-counter hearing devices, TV streaming, and broadcast audio reception in public venues.
6. The company sells to hearing care professionals, audiology clinics, consumers with hearing loss, and venues seeking accessible audio broadcasting.
7. Its finished hearing instruments are fitted and distributed to patients through audiology clinics and retail hearing care networks.
8. The approach uses an extra microphone placed inside the ear canal to leverage natural pinna acoustics for improved sound localization alongside deep neural network denoising.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The organization is a subsidiary of GN Store Nord, operates the ReSound, Beltone, Jabra, and Interton brands, collaborates with Cochlear, and is a member of the Bluetooth SIG.
Organization type: The organization is a subsidiary business division of a publicly traded parent company.
Business model: The company generates revenue through the wholesale and retail sale of finished hearing aid hardware, accessories, and related fitting software to clinical networks.
Scale and maturity: The parent company employs approximately 7,000 people and was founded in 1869, placing the organization among the five largest global hearing aid manufacturers.
Geography: The company is based in Ballerup, Denmark, and operates globally with a strong presence in North America and Europe.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on hearing healthcare and intelligent hearing instrument technology.

points.name: Seeed Studio
points.description: Chinese hardware manufacturer making open-source microcontroller boards and microphone arrays for audio prototyping.
points.bullets:
A hardware manufacturer that produces microphone arrays, edge computing gateways, and microcontroller boards for voice capture, IoT, and embedded machine learning applications. It manufactures the ReSpeaker line of USB and Raspberry Pi HAT microphone arrays with onboard DSP processing, as well as reComputer edge gateways for local AI inference.
1. A hardware manufacturer that builds finished microphone array products, Raspberry Pi HATs, edge computing gateways, and microcontroller boards, sold as physical hardware through its Bazaar store.
2. microphone arrays using XMOS DSP chips for hardware-level acoustic processing, combined with edge computing gateways powered by NVIDIA Orin or Rockchip NPUs for on-device speech recognition and LLM inference.
3. far-field voice capture with beamforming, direction of arrival detection, acoustic echo cancellation, noise suppression, dereverberation, and multi-channel concurrent speech recognition on edge gateways.
4. finished hardware products including USB microphone arrays, Raspberry Pi HATs, wearable recording devices, edge computing gateways, and microcontroller boards, along with open-source Linux drivers and software libraries.
5. smart speakers, interactive kiosks, robots, desktop transcription, near-field recording, ceiling and wall-mounted microphones, voice assistant integration, and edge AI voice processing.
6. makers, developers, enterprises building voice-enabled products, and hobbyists integrating voice interfaces into Raspberry Pi and IoT projects.
7. its microphone array hardware is integrated into voice-enabled products by developers and makers, and its edge gateways are used to run on-device speech recognition models for local AI processing.
8. combines open-source hardware manufacturing with integrated XMOS DSP-based acoustic processing and edge computing gateways designed for on-device AI inference.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: XMOS supplies DSP processors, STMicroelectronics supplies microphones, NVIDIA supplies Orin NX modules, and Picovoice provides voice software integrated with its hardware.
Organization type: a privately held hardware company based in Shenzhen, China.
Business model: hardware sales through its online Bazaar store, with customization and manufacturing services for IoT and maker applications.
Scale and maturity: an established company with a broad product catalog spanning microcontrollers, microphone arrays, and edge computing gateways.
Geography: headquartered in Shenzhen, Guangdong, China, serving global maker and developer markets.
Beyond audio: an open-source hardware company serving the broader IoT and embedded electronics ecosystem, with audio products as one segment of its offerings.

points.name: Nexa AI
points.description: AI company developing multimodal audio-language models and edge inference engines for on-device sound recognition.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer that builds an audio-language multimodal model and an edge inference engine for on-device deployment. It combines speech recognition with large language model capabilities in a single model, and provides a software development kit for running that model locally, for developers building edge AI applications.
1. An AI model developer whose speech and language models run on-device in an edge inference engine provided as an SDK for developers.
2. A multimodal neural network architecture combining an audio transcription model with a text-based large language model via a custom projector module.
3. Audio speech recognition and large language model reasoning.
4. AI models and an inference SDK delivered as downloadable software to developers.
5. Edge AI applications running speech recognition and language reasoning on local hardware.
6. Developers building on-device AI applications.
7. It unifies audio speech recognition and large language model reasoning into a single multimodal model optimized for edge inference.
points.profile:
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Beyond audio: The organization's focus extends to broader on-device AI inference and multimodal models beyond audio alone.

points.name: AONDevices
points.description: California technology company making ultra-low-power edge AI chips for on-device voice and sound recognition in battery-powered devices.
points.bullets:
A fabless chip company that designs and markets ultra-low-power edge AI processors for on-device voice, sound, and motion recognition, alongside a software platform for model training and deployment, for battery-powered devices.
1. A fabless semiconductor company that designs application-specific edge AI processors and sells them as finished chips alongside a software platform for edge deployment.
2. The organization builds neural network processors and proprietary cores for on-device inference, including specific hardware intellectual property for speech enhancement.
3. It delivers voice recognition, sound event detection, motion pattern detection, single-microphone speech denoising, and always-on multi-modal sensing.
4. Customers get it through finished semiconductor chips, software development platforms, hardware intellectual property, and evaluation kits.
5. Its processors are used in hearing aids, wireless earbuds, smartphones, wearables, and battery-powered remote controls.
6. It sells to consumer electronics device makers and developers of battery-powered edge hardware.
7. Its chips are designed into battery-powered consumer devices by hardware manufacturers.
8. It focuses on ultra-low-power consumption, with its voice core drawing less than 150µW in constant speech conditions and its denoising technology using only 50K parameters.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It is a partner of the tinyML Foundation and has collaborated with Atmosic Technologies and P-Logic Consulting.
Organization type: It is a privately held fabless semiconductor company.
Business model: It makes money through chip sales and associated software platforms.
Scale and maturity: It is an established company offering multiple generations of processors and evaluation kits.
Geography: It is based in Irvine, California, USA.
Beyond audio: It focuses entirely on edge AI processing and sensing solutions.

points.name: Liquid AI
points.description: Foundation-model startup building efficient, low-memory on-device AI models for agentic behavior and data extraction.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer whose foundation models run on-device in customers' hardware. It builds compact, open-weight multimodal models that process text, vision, and audio natively on edge processors for automakers and enterprises, avoiding cloud latency.
1. An AI model developer whose foundation models run on-device in customers' hardware and are accessed via open weights, local deployment platforms, or hosted cloud APIs.
2. Efficiency-first foundation models built on a non-transformer liquid neural network architecture combining short convolutions, sliding-window attention, and global attention to minimize memory and compute overhead.
3. Real-time speech-to-speech conversation, automatic speech recognition, live captions, text-to-speech, and structured decision routing from audio inputs.
4. Open-weight models for local deployment, a developer platform for fine-tuning and deployment, hosted API services, and custom edge-deployed models.
5. Automotive in-car assistants, smartphones, laptops, and edge devices requiring low-latency conversational AI.
6. Automakers, consumer electronics brands, enterprises, and developers.
7. Its models are integrated by hardware vendors and automakers into their edge platforms and vehicles.
8. It uses a biologically inspired non-transformer architecture designed from first principles with hardware co-design to achieve low memory and power usage on edge processors.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: AMD, Qualcomm, Mercedes-Benz, Samsung, Shopify, Intel, NVIDIA, Arm, Ambarella, and DARPA.
Organization type: Privately held startup and MIT CSAIL spin-out.
Business model: Hosted API usage, custom enterprise model development, and revenue-limited open-weight model licensing.
Scale and maturity: An AI unicorn founded in 2023 with around 120 employees and a 250 million US dollar Series A funding round.
Geography: Based in the United States, operating globally with partners in Germany and other markets.
Beyond audio: It develops general-purpose foundation models spanning text, vision, audio, and decision tasks for enterprise and edge deployment.

points.name: Smallest.ai
points.description: San Francisco AI startup building real-time conversational voice agents.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer whose cloud-based speech and audio models run behind an API, providing a full-stack, real-time conversational voice agent platform for enterprises and developers.
1. An AI model developer whose suite of streaming speech-to-text, text-to-speech, conversational language and full-duplex speech-to-speech models runs in the cloud behind an API.
2. Large generative voice models, streaming speech recognition engines and full-duplex speech-to-speech models operating in a continuous latent space over cloud WebSockets.
3. Streaming speech recognition, text-to-speech synthesis, voice cloning, multi-turn conversational state management, overlapping speech handling and full-duplex speech-to-speech conversion.
4. Cloud APIs and a cloud orchestration platform accessible via code-first interfaces and no-code deployment paths.
5. Real-time customer support voice bots, telephony infrastructure and enterprise voice agents.
6. Enterprises and software developers.
7. Its cloud APIs and models are integrated by enterprises and developers into their telephony and support infrastructure.
8. It provides a vertically integrated, full-stack conversational loop that replaces cascaded pipelines with a unified, speech-native architecture engineered for sub-300ms latency.
points.profile:
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Usage-based API pricing with volume sales tiers.
Scale and maturity: A San Francisco-based early-stage startup.
Geography: Based in San Francisco and operating in the cloud.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on the speech and audio AI layer.

points.name: Fluent.ai
points.description: Canadian AI technology company building offline speech recognition software that lets devices understand voice commands without internet.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer that builds offline, low-latency speech-to-intent voice interface software for original equipment manufacturers and service providers.
1. An AI model developer whose offline speech recognition models run on-device at the edge in customers' embedded hardware.
2. Deep neural network algorithms map speech directly to user intent without internet connectivity.
3. Offline speech recognition, multi-wake word detection, multilingual voice command execution and noise-robust speech-to-intent.
4. Software development kits and embedded voice control engines integrated into customers' hardware.
5. Smart home control devices, industrial factory machinery operated via connected headsets and various embedded consumer devices.
6. Original equipment manufacturers, smart home device makers and industrial service providers.
7. Fully offline, privacy-protective speech-to-intent models with small footprints engineered for loud environments and accent-agnostic understanding.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Investors include 500 Global, BDC Capital, Danhua Capital, Startup Autobahn and the Canadian Technology Accelerator Digital — Silicon Valley.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Software licensing of its embedded voice control engines to original equipment manufacturers.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2016 and backed by venture capital investors.
Geography: Based in Montreal, Quebec, Canada.

points.name: Arduino
points.description: Open-source hardware technology company building microcontroller boards for audio sensing and voice recognition.
points.bullets:
A maker of open-source hardware and software platforms that develops microcontroller boards with onboard sensors and microphones for embedded audio and sensing applications, providing development boards, software libraries and documentation for developers.
1. A hardware maker that builds microcontroller development boards with integrated microphones and sensors, sold as finished boards running embedded software programmed by users.
2. Microcontrollers with integrated analog and digital sensors, paired with software libraries and firmware running on-device.
3. Audio capture via onboard microphones and motion, environmental and gesture sensing through integrated sensor arrays.
4. Finished hardware development boards with associated software libraries, documentation and tutorials.
5. Embedded edge devices, TinyML systems and prototype audio sensing projects such as cough detection.
6. Developers, hobbyists and engineers building embedded and IoT systems.
7. Its development boards are used directly by developers to build embedded prototypes and edge machine learning systems.
8. An open-source hardware and software platform with onboard sensors and microphones designed for accessible embedded development.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Collaborated with Edge Impulse on a cough detection system and uses the RP2040 microcontroller from a semiconductor partner.
Organization type: A privately held technology company.
Business model: Hardware sales of development boards.
Scale and maturity: An established organization known for open-source hardware.
Geography: Based and operates globally as an open-source hardware provider.
Beyond audio: The company provides broad hardware and software platforms for embedded systems, IoT and electronics prototyping beyond audio.

points.name: Cerence
points.description: US software company building voice assistant technology for cars.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer whose conversational AI, speech processing and large language models run across cloud and edge environments for automakers and tier 1 suppliers.
1. An AI model developer whose automotive voice assistant and audio AI software runs in the cloud and on-device in automotive hardware.
2. Large and small automotive-grade language models, generative AI and digital signal processing algorithms running across cloud servers and partner chipsets.
3. Natural language processing, multi-step conversational threads, multimodal interaction, speech signal enhancement, noise reduction, emergency vehicle detection and in-car communication.
4. Cloud APIs, software development kits and edge language models running on customers' devices.
5. Cars, automotive dealerships and in-vehicle ecosystems.
6. Automakers, tier 1 suppliers, automotive dealerships and technology companies.
7. Its software and models are integrated by automakers and tier 1 suppliers into their in-vehicle platforms.
8. It delivers hybrid, agentic AI platforms that combine cloud and edge language models for reliable in-car interaction without connectivity.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It runs on Microsoft Azure and NVIDIA AI Enterprise, its Audio AI suite is integrated into DSP Concepts' Audio Weaver platform, and it partners with Microsoft, Ford and SiMa.ai.
Organization type: A publicly traded company that is a spinoff of Nuance.
Business model: Software licenses, subscriptions and API usage.
Scale and maturity: It generates around $300 million annually in revenue and has shipped technology in over 525 million cars.
Geography: It is based in Burlington, Massachusetts, USA and operates globally.
Beyond audio: It focuses entirely on conversational AI and mobility-based software solutions.

points.name: Unitron
points.description: Canadian hearing aid manufacturer producing digital hearing aids with DNN sound processing, owned by the Sonova Group.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of hearing aids and related accessories that builds and sells finished digital hearing instruments incorporating deep neural network sound processing, spatial processing, and wireless connectivity, for hearing care professionals and end users.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished hearing aid hardware and companion apps, sold as finished consumer medical devices worn on or in the ear.
2. Deep neural network sound processing, binaural spatial processing algorithms, feedback management, and Bluetooth wireless connectivity running on the devices.
3. Noise suppression, speech separation from background noise, spatial audio localization, feedback management, wireless audio streaming, and remote hearing aid adjustment.
4. Finished hearing aid hardware, Bluetooth accessories, and mobile apps.
5. Hearing aids, behind-the-ear and in-the-canal hearing instruments, wireless TV listening, and remote audiology services.
6. Hearing care professionals, audiology clinics, and end users with hearing loss.
7. Its hearing instruments are fitted and dispensed to patients by hearing care professionals.
8. Combines deep neural network sound processing with remote adjustment capabilities and a focus on the end-to-end hearing care experience.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Sonova Group, which owns the company and shares production facilities and components.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand of a publicly traded parent company.
Business model: Hardware sales of hearing aids and accessories.
Scale and maturity: A brand founded in 1964 with 16 offices worldwide, operating under a global parent company.
Geography: Based in Canada with research and development there, production in Switzerland, and global operations.
Beyond audio: A hearing care technology company focused entirely on hearing aids, diagnostic equipment, and tools for hearing care professionals.

points.name: Sonova/Phonak

A maker of finished hearing-aid hardware that builds and sells hearing aids for consumers with hearing loss.

2. Digital signal processing and wireless audio streaming are embedded in wearable medical devices.
3. The devices deliver hearing amplification and Auracast broadcast audio reception.
4. Customers get it as finished hardware.
5. The technology is used in hearing aids.

7. Its finished hearing aids are dispensed directly to end users through hearing care professionals.

Organization type: The organization is a publicly traded medical device company.

points.name: Demant/Oticon

A maker of hearing-aid hardware that designs and sells finished medical audio devices for hearing loss, embedding proprietary sound processing and AI capabilities directly into the wearable products it manufactures.
1. A medical device manufacturer that builds finished hearing aids containing embedded sound processing and AI systems, sold as complete wearable hardware.
2. Embedded audio processing and dual AI systems integrated into the firmware of wearable hearing aids.
3. Hearing compensation and sound processing driven by dual AI models.
4. Finished hearing-aid hardware.
5. Hearing aids.
6. Consumers with hearing loss.
7. Its finished hearing aids are dispensed to consumers through clinical audiology channels.
8. It operates as one of the four major European hearing-aid manufacturers with in-house device design.

Key partners and customers: Operating under the parent brand Demant alongside the Oticon brand.
Organization type: A publicly traded medical device manufacturer.
Business model: Finished hearing-aid hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: One of the four major European hearing-aid manufacturers.
Geography: Based in Europe.
Beyond audio: The organization's focus is entirely on hearing healthcare and audiological devices.

points.name: WS Audiology/Signia
points.description: European hearing aid manufacturer building hearing aid platforms that use coordinated neural networks.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of hearing aids that builds advanced audio processing platforms for hearing-impaired users, embedding coordinated deep-neural networks into its finished wearable devices.
1. A maker of finished hardware that builds hearing aid platforms sold as wearable devices worn by end users.
2. Deep-neural networks divide the workload among four coordinated networks running on-device in hearing aids.
3. Audio processing for hearing aids.
4. Finished hearing aid hardware.
5. Hearing aids.
6. Consumers with hearing loss.
7. Its hearing aids are fitted and dispensed to end users by hearing care professionals.

points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held manufacturer.
