points.description: UK audio equipment manufacturer building networked audio interfaces and intercoms for broadcast and live events.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures networked audio systems, including audio interfaces, intercoms, monitoring units, and announcer interfaces, for broadcast, live events, esports, and commercial audio environments.
1. An equipment maker that builds networked audio interfaces, intercoms, and monitoring units sold as finished hardware.
2. Networked audio systems supporting Dante, Ravenna, Milan (AVB), AES67, and SMPTE ST-2110-30 protocols with integrated connectivity, remote setup, and control.
3. Audio interfacing, intercom communication, signal monitoring, and remote setup and control for networked audio routing.
4. Finished hardware products including audio interfaces, intercoms, monitoring units, announcer interfaces, and debating chamber systems.
5. Broadcast environments, live events, esports, and commercial audio installations such as debating chambers.
6. Broadcasters, live event production companies, esports organizations, and commercial audio installations.
7. Its finished hardware products are deployed directly by end users in broadcast, live event, and commercial audio environments.
8. It responds to bespoke design requests and solves complex audio challenges for specialized broadcast and live event applications.
points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held company founded in 1966.
Geography: Based in Maidstone, UK, and operating worldwide.
Beyond audio: It is a pure-play audio equipment company.

points.name: Hitomi Ltd
points.description: British broadcast technology company measuring audio-video synchronization and latency for professional productions.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional broadcast equipment that develops precision timing measurement solutions for broadcast and professional AV environments, producing hardware and software tools that measure audio-video synchronisation for production companies and broadcasters.
1. An equipment maker that builds precision timing measurement instruments, sold as finished hardware and software products that run in broadcast infrastructure and cloud-based workflows.
2. Precision timing measurement technology that analyses latency, audio coherence and lip synchronisation across traditional hardware infrastructure and modern cloud-based workflows.
3. Audio-video synchronisation measurement, lip synchronisation verification, latency measurement, audio coherence analysis and channel identification.
4. Finished hardware and software products integrated into broadcast and production systems.
5. Broadcast control rooms, live event productions, professional AV environments and cloud-based broadcast workflows.
6. Broadcasters, production companies and professional AV operators.
7. Its measurement instruments are used by broadcasters and production teams to verify timing in their broadcast and live event workflows.
8. Its focus on precision timing verification across both traditional hardware infrastructure and cloud-based broadcast workflows distinguishes it from general-purpose audio or video equipment makers.
points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales and software products.
Geography: It operates globally, serving broadcast and professional AV customers worldwide.

points.name: Inovonics, Inc.
points.description: US broadcast equipment company making audio processors and signal monitors for radio stations.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional broadcast equipment that designs, manufactures, and sells audio processors, modulation monitors, and RDS encoders for radio broadcast facilities.
1. An equipment maker that builds professional broadcast hardware products sold as finished units deployed in radio stations and transmitter sites.
2. Analog and digital signal processing hardware and Radio Data System encoding circuits integrated into standalone rack-mounted units.
3. Audio processing, AM/FM modulation monitoring, RDS signal encoding, and off-air signal monitoring for analog and digital radio broadcasts.
4. Finished hardware products manufactured and assembled in the USA.
5. Radio broadcast studios, transmitter sites, and broadcast signal monitoring facilities.
6. Radio broadcasters and broadcast facilities.
7. Its finished hardware products are installed directly by radio broadcasters in their studios and transmitter sites.
8. It focuses on cost-effective broadcast products backed by a three-year factory warranty and after-sales support.
points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: Established in 1972 with a long-standing presence in the broadcast equipment market.
Geography: Based in the USA and serving international radio broadcast markets.
Beyond audio: The company focuses entirely on radio broadcast equipment and does not operate outside the audio field.

points.name: MaxxKonnect Group
points.description: Global broadcast technology group providing wireless connectivity, audio consoles, and signal processing software for radio and streaming.
points.bullets:
A broadcast technology group that provides wireless connectivity solutions, engineering and integration services, physical and virtual audio consoles, and software-based audio processing and repair tools for broadcasters.
1. A broadcast equipment and software maker that sells physical and virtual mixing consoles alongside standalone broadcast processing software and integration services.
2. Digital signal processing algorithms for audio enhancement and restoration run in software, integrated into broadcast hardware consoles and connectivity infrastructure.
3. Audio broadcast processing for AM, FM, HD and streaming, alongside audio repair functions including declipping and delossifying.
4. Software products, physical and virtual audio consoles, engineering services and finished broadcast hardware devices.
5. Radio studios, broadcast facilities, AM, FM, HD and streaming transmission chains.
6. Broadcasters and radio station operators.
7. Its software and hardware products are integrated by broadcast engineers into radio and streaming transmission facilities.
8. Combines heritage console manufacturing, broadcast integration services and advanced software-based audio restoration utilities within a single portfolio.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: MaxxKonnect Wireless, MK Technical Services, Logitek Audio and Thimeo.
Organization type: Privately held group of companies.
Business model: Hardware sales, software licenses and professional engineering services.
Scale and maturity: A portfolio of established heritage and operating brands serving the broadcast industry.
Geography: Serves the broadcast industry.
Beyond audio: Its broader activities include wireless connectivity solutions and technical engineering services for broadcast infrastructure.

points.name: Nemal Electronics Intl. Inc.
points.description: US cable manufacturer building fiber optic, copper, and hybrid cable assemblies for broadcast, pro audio, and A/V.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio and video cable, connector, and assembly products that manufactures fiber optic, copper, and hybrid cable, connectors, cable assemblies, panels, and reeler systems for A/V, HD broadcast, RF, data, and electronic control.
1. An equipment maker that builds physical cables, connectors, cable assemblies, panels, and reeler systems sold as finished hardware.
2. Analog and digital signal transport over copper, fiber optic, and hybrid physical media using specialized connectors and cable assemblies.
3. Physical routing and signal integrity for multi-channel audio, HD video, RF, data, and electronic control signals.
4. Finished hardware, including bulk cable, terminated cable assemblies, adapters, panels, and reelers.
5. HD broadcast facilities, stadiums, live venues, studios, and multi-camera installations.
6. Major broadcast networks,系统集成商, and large A/V facility operators.
7. Its finished cables and assemblies are deployed directly in broadcast and live event facilities and mobile units.
8. Manufacturing high-flexibility, rugged, and specialized cable assemblies with patented connectors and approved opticalCON termination capabilities.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Authorized Neutrik opticalCON COCA facility with LEMO and Neutrik approved products.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales of cables, connectors, assemblies, and panels, plus onsite support and system design services.
Scale and maturity: Established US manufacturer and Emmy Award winner.
Geography: Based in the United States.
Beyond audio: Manufactures cabling and connectivity products for A/V, HD broadcast, RF, data, and electronic control markets.

points.name: NTP Technology
points.description: Danish audio equipment manufacturer building digital audio interfaces and mixing systems for live sound.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that develops and manufactures digital audio interfaces, converters, routers, and control systems for broadcast, post-production, live sound, and studio applications.
1. A professional audio equipment maker that builds digital audio converters, routing interfaces, and control software sold as finished hardware units and accompanying software applications.
2. The core technology comprises modular A/D and D/A conversion stages, multichannel digital audio routing matrices, and signal processing engines running embedded within standalone hardware units.
3. The equipment delivers high-channel-count analog and digital audio conversion, MADI and Dante network audio routing, SDI embedding and de-embedding, internal summing, equalization, and sample rate conversion.
4. Customers get the technology through finished hardware units, expansion cards, and downloadable control software applications.
5. The products are used in broadcast facilities, post-production studios, live sound reinforcement setups, houses of worship, and installed audio infrastructures.
6. The company sells to professional recording studios, broadcast networks, live sound engineers, and audio post-production facilities.
7. Its finished hardware interfaces and routers are integrated into larger professional audio workflows and control surfaces by system integrators and end users.
8. The approach is distinguished by highly modular, card-based hardware architectures that allow extensive customization of I/O formats and deep integration with network audio protocols.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company builds I/O units for Avid, uses Dante networking protocols, and integrates with Dolby Atmos rendering software.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held manufacturing company that operates the Digital Audio Denmark brand as a wholly-owned business unit.
Business model: It makes money through the sale of professional audio hardware, expansion cards, and associated software.
Scale and maturity: It is an established manufacturer with a broad portfolio of multiple product generations serving professional audio markets.
Geography: The company is based in Denmark and operates in the global professional audio market.
Beyond audio: The organization is entirely focused on professional audio equipment manufacturing.

points.name: Point Source Audio
points.description: US pro audio company building subminiature microphones and headsets for live sound, broadcasting, and theatre.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs, engineers and manufactures wearable microphones and communication headsets, selling finished hardware under its own brand and as an OEM provider for other brands in live production, broadcast and theatre.
1. An equipment maker that builds wearable microphones and headsets sold as finished hardware used by talent and crews on stage and on location.
2. Microphone transducers and headset hardware using mechanical designs for modular mounting, bendable booms, waterproofing and custom-fitting ear mounts.
3. Vocal capture for live sound and broadcast, high-SPL audio pickup, built-in dual-element redundancy for microphone backup, and wearable headset communication.
4. Finished hardware products sold exclusively through a network of resellers, contractors and distributors.
5. Theatre, broadcasting, live events, worship, corporate AV, theme parks and recording studios.
6. Production companies, Broadway shows, theme parks, performing arts organizations and other audio equipment brands.
7. Its finished microphones and headsets are deployed directly by production crews and talent in live sound and broadcast environments.
8. It focuses on purpose-driven, wearable form factors that combine concealability and durability with practical production solutions like custom-fitting ear mounts and dual-element backup.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The San Francisco Opera uses its microphones, and it acts as a distributor for Digigram in the Americas.
Organization type: A privately held audio equipment design, engineering and manufacturing company.
Business model: Hardware sales through resellers, contractors, distributors and OEM transducer manufacturing agreements.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2004, holding eight patents and operating with offices in California and Ireland.
Geography: Based in Petaluma, California, USA with an additional office in Dublin, Ireland.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: Q5X
points.description: Global pro audio company making rugged wireless bodypack transmitters for sports and broadcast.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs, manufactures and sells ruggedized wireless bodypack transmitters and remote control systems for professional sports, broadcast television, live theatre and reality productions.
1. A professional audio equipment maker whose specialized wireless transmitters are sold as finished hardware worn by athletes, coaches and performers.
2. Wireless RF transmission systems paired with specialized ruggedized industrial designs and remote control and monitoring software.
3. Broadcast-quality wireless audio capture, RF signal encryption, remote parameter control, remote muting and waterproof audio transmission.
4. Finished hardware transmitters and remote control units sold directly to audio engineers and broadcast productions.
5. Professional sports fields and arenas, water sports, broadcast television productions, live theatre and reality shows.
6. Major TV networks, sports leagues, live entertainment venues and broadcast productions.
7. Its finished transmitters are deployed directly by audio engineers and broadcast networks in live sports and entertainment productions.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Shure, NBA, TNT Sports, MLB.
Organization type: A privately held corporation.
Business model: Hardware sales of specialized wireless transmitters priced in the premium professional range.
Scale and maturity: A mature company founded in 2002 with a small, agile structure focused on research and development.
Geography: Based in London, Ontario, operating across professional sports and broadcast productions.
Beyond audio: The company's entire focus is professional wireless audio hardware.

points.name: Salsa Sound
points.description: UK startup making AI software for automated mixing and audio quality control in live sports broadcasts.
points.bullets:
A software developer that builds AI-driven assistive mixing and audio quality control products for live sports and entertainment broadcasters.
1. An AI software developer whose assistive mixing and audio quality control applications run in the cloud or on standard operating systems behind an API.
2. Machine learning models analyze live multi-channel audio signal paths to automate mixing and perform algorithmic quality monitoring.
3. Automated sub-mix creation, multi-format and multi-language mixing, loudness compliance, speech intelligibility analysis, audio fidelity monitoring, phase and level analysis, profanity filtering and language detection.
4. Software products accessible through browser-based interfaces and API backends that run on Windows, Mac and Linux or in virtualized cloud environments.
5. Live sports broadcasts, entertainment productions and professional broadcast facilities.
6. Broadcasters and live production companies.
7. Its software products are deployed by broadcasters into their live production signal chains.
8. Its software automates the configuration of multiple simultaneous mixes across multiple immersive formats and loudness standards.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Integrates with VST plugins and standard broadcast transport and audio routing protocols including Dante, SDI, SRT, NDI, SMPTE 2110, MPEG-H and Dolby ATMOS.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Software licenses or subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: A UK-based startup.
Geography: Based in the United Kingdom.
Beyond audio: Its focus is entirely on audio technology for broadcast production.

points.name: Sanken Microphones
points.description: Japanese microphone manufacturer building professional mics for broadcast and live sound.
points.bullets:
A professional audio equipment manufacturer that builds high-quality microphones including shotgun, lavalier, head-worn, and boundary mics for broadcast, film, production, and live sound professionals.
1. An equipment maker that designs and builds professional microphones sold as finished hardware used on location and in studios.
2. Condenser and electret microphone capsules with directional polar patterns and mid-side stereo configurations.
3. Directional audio capture, dialogue recording, stereo width adjustment, and ultra-miniature body-worn sound pickup.
4. Finished microphone hardware and accessories.
5. Film and television production sets, broadcast studios, live sound venues, and professional recording environments.
6. Production sound mixers, broadcast engineers, and live sound professionals.
7. Its finished microphones are distributed to audio professionals through regional pro audio distributors.
8. Its ultra-miniature lavalier microphone technology earned a Scientific and Engineering Award from the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its microphones are distributed in the US, Canada, and Latin America by plus24.
Organization type: A microphone manufacturing brand.
Business model: Hardware sales of professional microphones.
Scale and maturity: An established manufacturer with a worldwide presence and an Academy Award for technical achievement.
Geography: Based internationally with distribution across North America and Latin America.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is professional audio microphone manufacturing.

points.name: SAS Sierra Automated Systems & Eng. Corp.
points.description: Broadcast technology company building audio routing systems, IP consoles, and intercoms for radio and live sound.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional broadcast audio equipment that builds hardware and software for audio routing, mixing, intercom and signal processing, sold to broadcast, live production and institutional facilities.
1. An equipment maker that builds integrated audio consoles, routers and intercom systems sold as finished hardware with embedded software that runs in broadcast and production facilities.
2. Digital audio routing and mixing systems using audio-over-IP networking combined with embedded digital signal processing for equalization, dynamics and intercom control.
3. Audio routing of thousands of channels over wide area networks, IP console mixing, intercom and IFB communication, equalization and dynamics processing.
4. Finished hardware products with embedded software and companion software tools.
5. Radio broadcast studios, visual radio, podcast facilities, theater audio management, front-of-house live sound, government facilities, professional athletics venues and higher education institutions.
6. Broadcast stations and networks, live production venues and operators, government facilities, professional sports organizations and higher education institutions.
7. Its hardware and software products are installed as the core routing and mixing infrastructure in broadcast and live production facilities.
8. It routes thousands of audio channels intelligently over wide area networks with integrated control, mixing and intercom in a single chassis.
points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales and associated software products.
Scale and maturity: A long-established company founded in 1986.
Geography: Based and operates in the United States.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: SoundNodes
points.description: Company developing AI-based audio recognition technology that identifies original content for music rights compensation, advertisement certification, and broadcast monitoring.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer and equipment maker that builds audio recognition systems and specialized capture hardware for identifying music, voices and ads, providing audience measurement and content discovery data for broadcasters, collective management organizations, advertisers and authorities.
1. An AI model developer whose recognition models run on-device at the edge in proprietary capture hardware and on-premises, and an equipment maker that sells finished audio capture devices.
2. Neural network models for audio recognition and mood detection running on edge hardware and in on-premises or cloud deployments.
3. Music recognition, voice recognition, advertisement certification, mood detection and audience measurement in noisy environments.
4. Finished hardware devices and software building blocks for audio content processing and discovery.
5. Radios, television, night clubs, festivals, shops, restaurants and live media broadcasting.
6. Collective management organizations, advertisers, authorities and media broadcasters.
7. Its finished capture hardware and recognition software are deployed directly by media broadcasters and organizations for content monitoring and audience measurement.
8. Near-real-time identification of music and voices combined with proprietary edge AI capture hardware designed for challenging acoustic environments.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Awarded at NAB and presenting at NAB 2026.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales and software solutions.
Scale and maturity: Hundreds of systems deployed across Europe and Latin America.
Geography: Based in and operates across Europe and Latin America.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is audio content processing, recognition and discovery.

points.name: Syndicate of Sounds Powered by Telos Alliance
points.description: Audio technology company converting stereo broadcasts into 5.1 surround sound and natural 3D headphone listening.
points.bullets:
An audio software developer that creates spatial audio processing technologies for broadcast and streaming. It licenses algorithms that upmix stereo to 5.1 surround sound and render natural 3D audio for headphones. Its tools serve broadcast and streaming platforms seeking immersive sound without remixing.
1. An audio software developer whose spatial audio algorithms run as licensed SDKs, plugins, and hardware solutions integrated into existing workflows.
2. Linear algorithmic processing that synthesizes 5.1 surround sound from stereo sources and recreates room acoustics and spatial positioning for headphone listening.
3. Stereo-to-5.1 upmixing and headphone 3D audio rendering that eliminates in-head localization.
4. SDKs, plugins, and hardware solutions integrated into existing production workflows.
5. Broadcast, streaming platforms, live streams, archived content, podcasts, gaming, and virtual reality applications.
6. Broadcast and streaming platforms seeking to deliver immersive audio.
7. Its algorithms are integrated by platforms into existing broadcast and streaming workflows.
8. It creates discrete surround sound from stereo sources through linear algorithmic processing without phase tricks, artificial reverb, or artifacts, preserving original production integrity.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Powered by Telos Alliance, endorsed by Grammy Award-winning producers, and tested at Abbey Road Studios.
Organization type: A brand or subsidiary operating under Telos Alliance.
Business model: Software licenses and hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: An established brand with patented technologies backed by a major broadcast equipment company.
Geography: Operates within the broadcast and streaming markets.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: Tieline, The Codec Company
points.description: Broadcast technology company manufacturing audio codecs for live remote broadcasting and audio distribution.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional broadcast audio equipment that builds digital audio codecs for live remote broadcasts, studio-to-transmitter links and audio distribution, for radio and television broadcasters.
1. A professional equipment maker that builds digital audio codecs sold as finished hardware units and smartphone apps that run over IP, SIP, ISDN and cellular networks.
2. Audio codecs transport audio simultaneously over any combination of IP, SIP, ISDN or cellular networks, supporting AES67, SMPTE 2110-30, SMPTE 2022-7, RAVENNA, Livewire+, NMOS, Ember+, AES3 and analog I/O.
3. The codecs deliver multichannel IP audio streaming, composite FM multiplex network distribution and live smartphone reporting.
4. Customers get the technology as finished hardware codecs, a smartphone app and a cloud-based remote controller.
5. The equipment is used in radio and television broadcast studios, remote broadcast locations and transmitter sites.
6. The company sells to radio and television broadcasters.
7. Its codecs are deployed by broadcasters to transport live audio over public internet and private IP networks.
8. The codecs transport audio simultaneously over any combination of IP, SIP, ISDN or cellular networks.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The codecs support interoperability with AES67, SMPTE, RAVENNA, Livewire+, NMOS, Ember+, Dante and WheatNet-IP.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held company.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: The company has been manufacturing audio codecs for over two decades.
Geography: The company serves thousands of radio and television broadcasters internationally.
Beyond audio: The company is a pure-play audio organization.

points.name: Venera Technologies
points.description: Software company building AI-powered automated quality control tools for digital media production.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that provides AI/ML-enabled file-based quality control software for the digital media industry, inspecting audio, video, captions and subtitles for post-production houses, broadcasters and streaming platforms.
1. A developer tools company whose automated quality control and captioning software runs as cloud platforms and on-premise deployments used by media engineers and QC operators.
2. AI and machine learning models applied to file-based media analysis for detecting errors, verifying compliance and generating captions within audio-video workflows.
3. The platform delivers automated audio and video quality control, caption and subtitle verification, synchronization detection, profanity detection and burnt-in text overlap detection.
4. Customers get it as cloud software platforms and on-premise software deployments.
5. The software is used in digital media workflows, post-production houses, production companies and broadcasting facilities.
6. The company sells to large media companies, smaller boutique post houses and production companies.
7. Its software is used by media companies and post-production houses to inspect and validate finished media files before distribution.
8. The approach is distinguished by native cloud architectures with dynamic scalability and usage-based pricing alongside robust content security for premium media.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The organization holds SOC-2 certification and AWS FTR certification for its cloud solutions.
Organization type: The company is a privately held technology company.
Business model: It makes money through software platforms offered with usage-based pricing models for cloud deployments and licenses for on-premise deployments.
Scale and maturity: The organization is an established provider serving some of the largest media companies in the world.
Geography: The company operates globally with a focus on the digital media industry.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on digital media quality control and captioning software with no interests beyond media file analysis.

points.name: Ashly
points.description: US pro audio manufacturer building amplifiers, processors, and mixers for commercial sound installations.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and builds amplifiers, matrix processors, digital mixers and analog signal processors for commercial installed sound applications.
1. An equipment maker that builds power amplifiers, matrix processors and digital mixers sold as finished hardware.
2. Digital signal processing, analog signal processing and Dante audio networking integrated into standalone hardware.
3. Multi-mode audio processing, signal routing, mixing and amplification for installed sound systems.
4. Finished hardware products and companion control software.
5. Commercial installed sound systems in churches, restaurants, hotels, schools, courtrooms, health clubs and council chambers.
6. Commercial facility integrators, audio contractors and institutional buyers.
7. Its finished hardware and control software are installed in commercial venues by integrators.
8. It emphasizes long-term hardware durability and ongoing service for legacy products alongside its DSP and networking advancement.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its products incorporate Dante audio networking technology.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: An established manufacturer founded in 1974 with a fifty-year operating history.
Geography: Based in Webster, New York, USA, serving the commercial installed audio market.
Beyond audio: The organization is a pure-play audio equipment manufacturer.

points.name: CAD Audio
points.description: US microphone and audio equipment maker producing recording, broadcast, live sound, and wireless microphone products.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that builds microphones, headphones and audio interfaces for performers, engineers and audio professionals. It provides wired and wireless microphone systems, including handheld, head-worn, ear-worn and gooseneck models, for recording, broadcast, live performance, production, commercial and consumer markets.
1. An equipment maker that builds wired and wireless microphones and audio interfaces sold as finished hardware.
2. Analog and wireless microphone systems operating in the 2.4 GHz band with onboard phantom power and variable pickup patterns.
3. Voice and instrument capture with hands-free operation, background noise reduction and controlled directionality.
4. Finished hardware products.
5. Recording studios, broadcast facilities, live performance stages, presentations and production environments.
6. Performers, engineers, audio professionals and consumers.
7. Its finished hardware is sold to end users and audio professionals for direct use in performance and production environments.
8. A 90-year legacy and a multifaceted family of sub-brands spanning diverse professional and consumer audio markets.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Musical artists including The Kid Brothers perform at its NAMM booth.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: An established company with over 90 years of operation.
Geography: Based in Bloomfield, CT, USA, serving professionals worldwide.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is audio.

points.name: DirectOut GmbH
points.description: German pro audio company building networking and bridging solutions for broadcast and live sound environments.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that develops audio connectivity, networking, and bridging solutions, providing mission-critical infrastructure for broadcast, studio, live, and installed sound markets.
1. An equipment maker that builds professional audio networking hardware and signal distribution solutions, sold as finished hardware devices and expansion cards.
2. The core technology comprises digital audio networking, format conversion, and signal distribution processing, utilizing onboard DSP capabilities to route and bridge signals across established audio network protocols.
3. The specific audio capabilities it delivers are audio format conversion, network bridging, multichannel signal routing, and audio interface I/O.
4. Customers get it as finished hardware products, including format converters, audio interfaces, and expansion cards.
5. The devices and products are used in broadcast facilities, recording studios, live sound venues, and installed sound environments.
6. The organization sells to professional audio facilities,系统集成商, broadcasters, and live event production companies.
7. Its finished hardware products are integrated into professional audio networks and routing systems by system integrators and broadcasters.
8. Its approach is distinguished by supporting emerging high-channel-count audio network standards, such as SMPTE ST 2110, to enable interoperability in demanding broadcast environments.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It is a partner of Stage Tec, collaborating on an AES67 audio networking module, and produces devices compatible with the Waves SoundGrid networking platform.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held company.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of its professional audio networking and format conversion products.
Scale and maturity: The company was founded in 2008 and operates globally.
Geography: It is based in Mittweida, Germany, and operates worldwide.
Beyond audio: Audio connectivity, networking, and bridging is its entire focus.

points.name: Fostex
points.description: Japanese pro audio manufacturer building studio monitors, headphones, and recording equipment.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional and consumer audio equipment that designs and builds acoustic equipment for music lovers, audio engineers and musicians.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished audio hardware products sold to end users.
2. Acoustic transducer and speaker hardware designs.
3. Sound creation and listening reproduction.
4. Finished hardware and software products.
5. Studios and personal listening environments.
6. Consumers, audio engineers and musicians.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to end users.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A member of the WiSA Association and a division of Foster.
Organization type: A division of a publicly traded company.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 1973.
Beyond audio: The company focuses entirely on audio equipment.

points.name: HK Audio
points.description: German pro audio company building PA systems and speakers for portable, live, and installed sound applications.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of professional audio equipment that builds and sells sound reinforcement systems, including PA speakers, subwoofers, monitors, and integrated PA packages for live, portable, and installed sound applications.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished active and passive loudspeakers and PA systems sold as physical hardware for live sound reproduction.
2. Amplified and unamplified loudspeaker enclosures incorporating full-range drivers, subwoofers, stage monitors, modular stackable arrays, power amplifiers, and integrated onboard mixers with Bluetooth connectivity.
3. Sound reinforcement, low-frequency bass reproduction, stage monitoring, and modular audio array configuration for live events.
4. Finished hardware products, including powered PA speaker cabinets, active subwoofers, portable PA packages, and rack-mountable power amplifiers.
5. Live concerts, open-air festivals, corporate events, weddings, mid-sized outdoor shows, and permanent sound installations.
6. Audio professionals, live sound engineers, event production companies, and performance venues.
7. Its finished loudspeaker systems are sold directly to sound engineers and event production companies for deployment at live events and installations.
8. It focuses on modular, portable PA architectures that combine powered subwoofers and satellite speakers with integrated mixers and Bluetooth for simplified live sound setup.
points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held manufacturing company.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished professional audio equipment.
Scale and maturity: An established company in business for over 35 years operating advanced production facilities.
Geography: Based in Germany, operating as a sound systems manufacturer across Europe.
Beyond audio: Professional audio equipment manufacturing is its entire focus.

points.name: Alcons Audio
points.description: Dutch professional sound system manufacturer developing pro-ribbon speaker technology for studio and live event audio.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of professional sound systems that develops and builds loudspeakers, subwoofers, amplified controllers, and stage monitors utilizing proprietary pro-ribbon transducer technology for the studio, cinema, installation, and touring industries.
1. An equipment maker that designs and manufactures finished loudspeakers, amplifiers, and controllers, sold as complete hardware systems.
2. The core technology is a patented pro-ribbon transducer design combined with Class-D amplification and DSP engines, providing high-output mid and high frequencies with fast-transient response and low distortion.
3. The systems deliver high SPL sound reinforcement, extended low-frequency reproduction, accurate sound monitoring, and spatial audio rendering for immersive environments.
4. Customers receive finished hardware products, including passive and self-powered loudspeakers, subwoofers, and amplified loudspeaker controllers with integrated DSP.
5. The products are used in cinemas, houses of worship, live sound touring, studios, corporate installations, residential home theaters, and immersive experience rooms.
6. The company sells to system designers, consultants, AV integrators, production companies, and premium residential distributors.
7. Its finished hardware systems are designed into venues and touring rigs by integrators and distributed to residential channels by cinema equipment providers.
8. The organization applies the exact same proprietary transducer, amplification, and processing technologies from studio reference monitors to large-scale sound reinforcement, maintaining a single cross-application audio reference.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its products are distributed to cinema customers by Pulse Cinemas and are integrated with StormAudio processors.
Organization type: A privately held manufacturer.
Business model: The organization generates revenue through the sale of finished professional audio hardware, loudspeakers, and associated electronic controllers.
Scale and maturity: A European manufacturer founded in 2002 that develops and produces all products in-house.
Geography: Based in the Netherlands with a North American sales operation, operating in global professional audio markets.

2. The core technology comprises audio over IP networking for LAN and WAN distribution, combined with amplification and loudspeaker driver systems built to EN54 and UL2572 compliance standards.
3. It delivers paging, voice alarm, mass notification, and general audio distribution across networked facilities.
4. Customers receive finished hardware products including speakers, amplifiers, and networked audio distribution equipment.
5. Its equipment is deployed in commercial buildings, K-12 schools, and facilities requiring voice alarm and mass notification.
6. The company sells to facility operators, system integrators, and institutions requiring public address and life safety communication.
7. Its finished hardware is installed in buildings by system integrators and facility managers for public address and emergency communication.

points.name: PlexusAV
points.description: Networked AV company delivering standards-based AV-over-IP networking solutions.
points.bullets:
An equipment maker that builds standards-based AV-over-IP endpoints and management solutions for networked audio and video distribution, selling through open-architecture products to integrators and engineers.
1. An equipment maker that designs encoders, decoders, gateways, and networked audio endpoints sold as finished hardware products running on standard IP networks.
2. The core technology comprises ultra low-latency video codecs and networked audio protocols built on open standards for AV-over-IP convergence.
3. The equipment delivers ultra low-latency audio and video encoding and decoding, USB-C connectivity, and network transport over standard 1GbE infrastructure.
4. Customers receive finished hardware products and network management solutions built on open standards.
5. The hardware is used in networked AV installations, IT environments, and scalable AV-over-IP deployments.
6. The company sells to systems integrators and engineers.
7. Its finished hardware products are installed by systems integrators into enterprise IT and AV networks.
8. The company differentiates by building open-architecture products on open standards to avoid proprietary lock-in.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Products are built on standards including IPMX, NMOS, Dante, and JPEG-XS, with select products officially IPMX Certified.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held company.
Business model: The company makes money through hardware sales of encoders, decoders, and network endpoints.
Scale and maturity: The organization is an established company exhibiting at trade shows.
Geography: The company is based in and operates in markets serviced by professional AV distribution.
Beyond audio: The organization builds products for combined audio and video over IP distribution.

points.name: Rational Acoustics
points.description: Audio software company building sound system analysis and measurement tools.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that builds audio analysis and optimization software, hardware and training for sound system measurement, alignment and equalization, used by live sound engineers and system integrators.
1. A developer tools company whose dual-channel FFT-based audio measurement and analysis software runs on standard computers and integrated hardware mixers.
2. Dual-channel FFT-based real-time audio analysis and measurement software with response and locator modules.
3. Real-time audio spectrum analysis, sound system measurement, optimization, and alignment.
4. Software products, training courses, hardware products, and professional consulting.
5. Live sound engineering and sound system optimization in venues and events.
6. Live sound engineers, system integrators, audio professionals, and equipment manufacturers.
7. Its real-time analyzer technology is integrated by mixer manufacturers into their hardware products.
8. It combines its measurement software platform with dedicated training courses and professional consulting focused specifically on sound system optimization.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its software platform is integrated into StudioLive SeriesIII mixers by PreSonus.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Software product sales, training courses, hardware products, and professional consulting fees.
Beyond audio: It is a pure-play audio company focused entirely on acoustic test and measurement and sound system alignment.

points.name: Renkus-Heinz, Inc.
points.description: US pro audio company building digitally steerable loudspeaker arrays for large venues.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of professional audio equipment that designs and builds digitally steerable loudspeaker arrays and passive column loudspeakers for installed sound reinforcement in large venues.
1. An equipment maker that designs professional loudspeakers sold as finished hardware.
2. Acoustic transducers combined with digital beam steering and point source design to provide vertical pattern control and high SPL performance.
3. The products deliver digital beam steering, vertical pattern control and generation of multiple individually controllable acoustic beams.
4. Customers get the technology as finished hardware loudspeakers.
5. The loudspeakers are used in performing arts venues, transportation hubs, houses of worship and corporate, educational and governmental facilities.
6. The company sells to audio integrators and facility operators.
7. Its finished loudspeakers are installed in venues by professional audio integrators.
8. It integrates digital beam steering into a point source design.
points.profile:
Organization type: The organization is a privately held company.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: The company was founded in 1979 and maintains a global office footprint.
Geography: It is headquartered in Foothill Ranch, California, USA and operates globally.
Beyond audio: The company is a pure-play audio manufacturer.

points.name: Revolution Acoustics
points.description: US audio company making invisible surface-mounted speakers for immersive room sound.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment and finished hardware that designs and sells invisible surface-excitation transducers for installed audio, and handcrafted studio monitoring systems for recording professionals.
1. An equipment maker that builds surface-excitation transducers and studio monitor loudspeakers sold as finished physical hardware.
2. The transducers use planar wave physics to excite adhered surfaces into acoustic planar radiating sources, while the monitors use passive crossovers, high-excursion ceramic matrix drivers, and AMT tweeters paired with Class A/B amplification.
3. The transducers deliver invisible room-wide spatial audio with even frequency response and sound pressure levels across large surfaces, and the monitors deliver full-range frequency response and dynamic accuracy for mix translation.
4. The products are sold as finished hardware components and complete stereo monitoring systems.
5. The transducers are used in commercial and residential built-in installations, and the monitors are used in recording, mixing, and mastering studios.
6. The company sells to custom integrators, residential and commercial installers, and recording professionals.
7. Its finished hardware is distributed through authorized dealers and installed directly into architectural surfaces or studio environments.
8. The transducer approach turns standard building materials like drywall and glass into acoustic radiating surfaces to achieve a completely invisible form factor without high-frequency beaming.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Studio monitor development and voicing was handled in collaboration with mastering engineer Brian Lucey and loudspeaker designer Kevin Malmgren.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held company.
Business model: It makes money through the sale of finished hardware.
Scale and maturity: The company has over two decades of operation in its market.
Geography: It is based in the USA and operates globally.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on audio hardware and monitoring technology.

points.name: Beyma
points.description: Spanish manufacturer building loudspeaker drivers for professional and car audio systems.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of professional loudspeaker drivers that designs and builds low-frequency, high-frequency, midrange, and coaxial transducer components for professional audio system manufacturers and car audio integrators.
1. A speaker component manufacturer whose raw drivers and tweeters are sold as physical components integrated into other companies' finished speaker cabinets.
2. Electromagnetic transducers utilizing neodymium magnets, compression tweeter diaphragms, and coaxial driver architectures to convert electrical audio signals into acoustic sound waves.
3. High-efficiency sound reproduction, high-power audio handling, and customized low-frequency and high-frequency acoustic transduction.
4. The components are delivered as finished physical hardware parts sold to equipment manufacturers and through retail channels.
5. Professional loudspeaker enclosures, stage monitors, live sound reinforcement systems, and car audio systems.
6. Professional audio equipment brands and car audio system manufacturers.
7. Its transducers are designed into finished loudspeaker cabinets and stage monitors by professional audio equipment brands.
8. The company maintains an in-house research and development department capable of creating custom driver designs to attend specific customer needs.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its drivers are used in stage monitors by Wharfedale Pro and in loudspeakers by Audiocenter.
Organization type: A privately held manufacturing company.
Business model: The company makes money through the sale of physical speaker components and custom driver hardware.
Scale and maturity: The organization has been operating and manufacturing from its factory in Valencia since 1969.
Geography: The company is based and manufactures its products in Valencia, Spain.
Beyond audio: Audio transducer manufacturing is the organization's sole focus.

points.name: ACX Europe and NewHank
points.description: European audio engineering company designing and manufacturing DSP-based AV equipment and accessories.
points.bullets:
An equipment maker that designs and manufactures professional audio-video hardware and accessories, building products based on digital signal processing, amplification, and source technologies for professional users.
1. An equipment maker whose finished hardware and software products run in professional installations and live environments.
2. The core technology is digital signal processing, extended to loudspeaker amplification and audio-video source technologies.
3. The equipment delivers loudspeaker amplification and audio-video source processing.
4. Customers get the products as finished hardware and software products.
5. The products are used in professional audio-video environments.
6. The company sells to a European network of dealers and professional audio distributors.
7. Its finished hardware is distributed through professional audio and video dealers to end users.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: NewHank is the brand name for AV gear by Netherlands based Interstate Audio.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held equipment manufacturer.
Business model: The company makes money through hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: The company was founded in 2013 and operates with its own manufacturing facilities in China.
Geography: The organization is based in Europe with a head office in the Netherlands and manufacturing facilities in China.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on audio-video equipment.

points.name: AEROMATE SPEAKER
points.description: Taiwanese speaker manufacturer producing PA, ceiling, and horn speakers alongside custom audio components.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment and speaker components that manufactures PA speakers, ceiling speakers, wall-mounted speakers, driver units, tweeters, and horn speakers, providing OEM and ODM manufacturing services for customers worldwide.
1. A manufacturer that builds finished loudspeakers and raw speaker components, sold as finished hardware to equipment brands and installers.
2. Electromagnetic transducer designs and acoustic enclosures manufactured for public address and architectural sound reinforcement.
3. Sound reproduction for public address, architectural ceiling installations, and wall-mounted spatial coverage.
4. Finished hardware components and complete speaker systems.
5. Public address systems, architectural ceiling speaker installations, and wall-mounted sound reinforcement setups.
6. Equipment brands seeking OEM and ODM manufacturing partnerships, audio system installers, and distribution channels.
7. Its finished speakers and components are integrated into commercial sound installations and distributed under other brands.
8. Over forty-five years of ISO 9001-certified manufacturing experience based entirely in Taiwan with flexible customization services.
points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held manufacturing company.
Business model: Hardware sales and contract manufacturing.
Scale and maturity: An established manufacturer founded in 1980 with over forty-five years of operating history.
Geography: Based in Taiwan, manufacturing products locally and serving customers worldwide.
Beyond audio: The organization manufactures audio transducers and loudspeakers as its entire focus.

points.name: ALLDSP
points.description: German pro audio company manufacturing DSP modules for professional amplifiers.
points.bullets:
An equipment maker that develops and manufactures DSP modules and related audio networking products for professional audio applications, selling to demanding companies worldwide.
1. An equipment maker that builds DSP modules and finished audio networking products, sold as hardware components integrated into third-party professional audio equipment.
2. Digital signal processing hardware and Dante and MILAN audio networking technology form the core of its modules.
3. The modules deliver digital signal processing and audio networking for professional audio systems.
4. Customers receive its products as physical DSP modules manufactured on an in-house production line.
5. The modules are used in professional audio amplifiers.
6. The company sells its hardware modules to professional audio equipment manufacturers.
7. Its DSP modules are designed into professional amplifiers by audio electronics brands.
8. The company maintains full control over production quality by manufacturing its DSP modules on an in-house Siplace production line.
points.profile:
Organization type: The organization is a privately held equipment manufacturer.
Business model: The company makes money through hardware sales of its DSP modules.
Scale and maturity: The company has been developing and manufacturing its products for over twenty-three years.
Geography: The company is based in Germany and manufactures its products there while supplying companies worldwide.
Beyond audio: Audio is the entire focus of the company.

points.name: Amadeus Acoustics
points.description: French pro audio company building active acoustics and immersive sound systems for performance venues.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures loudspeakers, spatial sound processors, and active acoustics systems for high-end venues, studios, and cultural institutions.
1. A professional audio equipment maker whose spatial audio processors, active acoustics systems, and custom loudspeakers run as finished hardware and software products in installed venues.
2. Spatial rendering algorithms including Wave Field Synthesis, High-Order Ambisonics, and Distance-Based Amplitude Panning running on dedicated rack-mounted servers and portable hardware units.
3. Spatial sound rendering, 3D sound source localization and envelopment, active acoustic enhancement, and voice lift.
4. Finished hardware products including spatial sound processors, rack-mounted servers, and portable units, alongside custom loudspeakers and software-based audio platforms.
5. Theatres, opera houses, concert halls, museums, recording studios, research centers, and exhibition spaces.
6. Cultural institutions, theaters, museums, research centers, and recording studios.
7. Its finished audio systems and loudspeakers are installed directly into venues and integrated with third-party mixing desks, DAWs, and show control platforms.
8. It integrates research-grade spatialization algorithms developed with institutional research labs into fully redundant, Dante-compatible hardware processors.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: IRCAM, STMS Lab, Kling & Freitag, and Amber Technology.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales, system integration, and custom electro-acoustic design services.
Scale and maturity: A company operating for over thirty years with a portfolio of custom installations across major cultural institutions.
Geography: Based in France and operating globally through distributors.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: Ambient System
points.description: European manufacturer building public address, voice evacuation, and IP intercom systems for critical safety communications.
points.bullets:
An equipment maker and systems provider that builds public address, voice evacuation, and IP intercom systems for large-scale, mission-critical facilities. It designs and implements integrated audio communication technologies that protect people and infrastructure in demanding environments. The organization delivers reliable safety and communication systems to facility operators and owners worldwide.
1. An equipment maker and systems provider whose finished hardware and software products run as installed communication infrastructure in facilities.
2. The core technology comprises networked IP audio routing, voice evacuation processing, and public address amplification integrated into installed communication infrastructure.
3. The specific audio capabilities delivered are public address broadcasting, voice evacuation alerts, and IP intercom communication.
4. Customers get the systems as finished hardware, software products, and large-scale implemented installations.
5. The systems are used in airports, refineries, stadiums, tunnels, shopping centres, hospitals, railway stations, industrial plants, and office buildings.
6. The organization sells to facility operators, infrastructure owners, and enterprises managing mission-critical environments.
7. Its finished systems are installed as communication infrastructure in large-scale facilities by systems integrators.
points.profile:
Business model: The organization makes money through hardware sales, systems implementation, and equipment provision.
Geography: The organization is based in Europe and operates worldwide.

points.name: AMC Baltic
points.description: Lithuanian audio manufacturer making loudspeakers and electronics for public address and voice evacuation systems.
points.bullets:
An equipment maker that designs and manufactures loudspeakers and electronics for voice evacuation, public address, paging, and background music for the contractor market.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished loudspeakers, amplifiers, music players, and microphones sold as physical hardware in commercial installations.
2. Conventional and horn loudspeakers, ceiling loudspeakers, sound projectors, and mixing amplifiers built to EN54 certification standards for voice evacuation.
3. Sound reinforcement, voice evacuation, paging, and background music playback for commercial sound systems.
4. The company provides finished hardware products stocked in a European warehouse and sold worldwide through a distributor network.
5. Public address systems, voice evacuation systems, paging systems, and commercial background music installations.
6. Contractors who install commercial sound and voice evacuation systems.
7. Its finished hardware products are distributed by international distributors to installation contractors for commercial building projects.
8. It focuses on simple, reliable, competitively priced products backed by large European warehouse stock to ensure short delivery times.
points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held company established in 2008.
Business model: Hardware sales through distribution.
Scale and maturity: A mid-sized company established in 2008 with an international distributor network and a conveniently located European warehouse.
Geography: Based in Lithuania and operating worldwide through its distributor network.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is on commercial and public address audio equipment.

points.name: Amina Technologies
points.description: UK company making invisible panel loudspeakers that hide inside walls and ceilings while turning surfaces into sound sources.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures invisible architectural loudspeakers using Distributed Mode Loudspeaker (DML) panel technology, producing flat-panel speakers that install flush into walls and ceilings to be hidden beneath plaster, paint or architectural finishes for custom install and commercial markets.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished architectural loudspeakers sold as physical hardware installed in building surfaces.
2. The core technology is Distributed Mode Loudspeaker (DML) architecture, where distributed-mode vibrations across a composite panel excite a surface to radiate diffuse sound, using a proprietary resin-impregnated cellulose pulp core panel with an anti-warp composite skin.
3. The speakers deliver wide audio dispersion at 150 degrees across a 60Hz to 20KHz frequency response, radiating from flat surfaces while remaining visually hidden beneath architectural finishes.
4. Finished hardware speakers in ceiling-grid and in-wall formats, available with custom vinyl or paint finishes.
5. Luxury residences, superyachts, commercial venues, hospitality spaces, premium architecturally designed homes and commercial ceiling installations.
6. Architects, designers, custom installers and commercial integration firms.
7. Its finished speakers are specified by architects and installed by custom integrators into architectural surfaces in residential and commercial building projects.
8. Its proprietary composite panel material and DML technology transform entire architectural surfaces into hidden high-fidelity sound sources finishable with stone, veneer, plaster, wood, leather or paint.
points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held manufacturing company.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished loudspeaker products with custom-finish options.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 1999 with over 25 years of operation, UK-based research and manufacturing facilities and a global project footprint.
Geography: Headquartered in the United Kingdom with research and manufacturing facilities in the UK and Europe and installations worldwide.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is architectural audio technology.

points.name: AMPLITUDE AUDIO
points.description: Commercial audio company designing synchronized multiroom audio distribution and amplification systems for professional installations.
points.bullets:
An equipment and systems provider that builds multiroom audio distribution platforms combining amplification, synchronized audio routing, and zone control for professional and commercial installations.
1. An equipment maker that builds integrated multiroom audio systems sold as finished hardware and software products running on dedicated networked devices.
2. The core technology combines multi-channel amplification with networked audio distribution, sample-synchronous streaming, and DSP processing for zone, volume, delay, and equalization control.
3. The platform delivers synchronized multiroom audio distribution, multi-source streaming, and precise zone, volume, delay, equalization, and sound scene control.
4. Customers receive the system as finished hardware and software products managed through a web-based interface.
5. The systems are deployed in hospitality, retail, corporate spaces, and cultural venues.
6. The organization sells to systems integrators and end users in commercial markets.
7. Its finished hardware and software products are installed by systems integrators into commercial AV ecosystems.
8. The platform emphasizes ease of deployment through a web-based interface while combining high-quality amplification and synchronized distribution in a scalable architecture.
points.profile:
Organization type: The organization is a privately held company.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales and software products.
Geography: The company exhibits at integrated systems events in Europe and operates in professional AV markets.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: AODA
points.description: Chinese pro audio electronics company building professional power amplifiers and DSP equipment.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that builds professional power amplifiers, equalizers, analyzers, digital signal processors, crossovers, limiters and mixers for installed long-distance audio systems and custom OEM/ODM customers.
1. An equipment maker that builds professional network power amplifiers with integrated 24-bit DSP audio processing, sold as finished hardware.
2. The core technology comprises Class H amplifier circuits and 24-bit DSP audio CMOS chips designed for long-distance audio signal transmission and control.
3. The equipment delivers audio power amplification, equalization, signal analysis, digital signal processing, frequency crossover, limiting and mixing.
4. Customers get it as finished hardware products and through custom-made OEM and ODM manufacturing arrangements.
5. The products are used in long-distance audio systems and professional installed audio setups.
6. The company sells to domestic and international equipment buyers, system integrators and custom OEM/ODM clients.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly into professional audio distribution and integration channels.
8. The approach is distinguished by integrating 24-bit DSP CMOS chips and computer control directly into Class H professional power amplifiers scaled across a wide power range.
points.profile:
Organization type: The organization is a privately held company.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of professional audio equipment and custom OEM/ODM manufacturing contracts.
Scale and maturity: The company was established in 1993 and operates a product line spanning multiple amplifier models up to 2x2400W output.
Geography: It is based in Enping, China and sells domestically and across Europe, America, Asia, the Middle East and Africa.
Beyond audio: The company focuses entirely on professional audio equipment manufacturing.

points.name: APEX / AUDIOFOCUS
points.description: Belgian audio manufacturer building networked installation amplifiers and live sound loudspeakers for touring and fixed venues.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that manufactures and sells installation amplifiers with integral DSP and Dante networking, and loudspeakers for live touring and fixed installations, for audio professionals and integrators.
1. A professional audio equipment maker whose finished amplifier and loudspeaker hardware is sold to integrators and installed in venues.
2. The core technology comprises multi-channel power amplification, loudspeaker driver and enclosure design, and integral digital signal processing with Dante audio networking.
3. Audio power amplification, loudspeaker reproduction for line array, column, point source, and stage monitor configurations, and remote amplifier management and control.
4. Finished hardware products.
5. Live touring events, immersive environments, multi-zone fixed installations, and professional venues.
6. Audio system integrators, touring sound professionals, and fixed installation contractors.
7. Its finished hardware is installed directly into venues and touring rigs by audio professionals and system integrators.
8. It combines CloudPower installation amplifiers featuring integral DSP and Dante networking with a full range of complementary Belgian-manufactured loudspeakers under common ownership.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The organization is owned by Community Europe S.A. and its products are compatible with Dante networking and ACW series touchscreen controllers.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand owned by a holding company.
Business model: Finished hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: An established manufacturer producing a full range of professional audio hardware.
Geography: Based and manufactured in Belgium.
Beyond audio: It is a pure-play professional audio manufacturer.

points.name: Arbane Groupe
points.description: French pro audio manufacturer building loudspeakers for public address systems, live concerts, and fixed installations.
points.bullets:
A professional audio equipment manufacturer that designs and makes loudspeakers and sound reinforcement systems for public address, events and fixed installations, operating two subsidiary brands.
1. A professional audio equipment maker whose finished loudspeakers and sound reinforcement systems run in live venues and installed spaces.
2. Column loudspeakers and sound reinforcement systems designed to increase voice intelligibility in difficult acoustics.
3. Voice intelligibility enhancement and sound reinforcement for difficult acoustics.
4. Finished hardware products including loudspeakers and sound reinforcement equipment.
5. Difficult acoustics spaces, concerts, events and fixed installations.
6. Integrators and operators of public address, event and fixed-installation sound systems.
7. Its finished loudspeakers and sound reinforcement systems are installed in venues and event productions.
8. The company offers solutions spanning public address to professional event loudspeakers under two subsidiary brands.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: 3WM Communications.
Organization type: A privately held manufacturer formed by the merger of two professional audio brands.
Business model: Hardware sales of professional loudspeakers and sound reinforcement equipment.
Scale and maturity: A French manufacturer established in 2002 and expanded through a 2020 merger.
Geography: Based in France.
Beyond audio: The organization's entire focus is professional audio equipment.

points.name: Areal
points.description: Audio technology company building hardware and software for monitoring and creating immersive spatial soundscapes.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and sells finished hardware and proprietary software for immersive spatial audio, including headphones with multiple discrete drivers per earcup and an accompanying upmixing engine.
1. An equipment maker that builds spatial audio headphones and a desktop controller and sells them as finished hardware products.
2. Proprietary Acoustic Image Mapping and Realtime Immersive Stereo Expansion signal processing technologies drive the spatial rendering.
3. The company delivers multichannel spatial audio monitoring over headphones and real-time upmixing of stereo audio into immersive formats.
4. Customers get the technology as finished hardware products and proprietary software.
5. The products are used in studios and venues for monitoring Dolby Atmos and other multichannel audio formats.
6. The company sells to creators, engineers and venues.
7. Its finished hardware products are distributed to end users through regional audio equipment distributors.
8. The approach is distinguished by headphones using four discrete drivers per earcup combined with proprietary spatial signal processing to monitor multichannel immersive audio.

Key partners and customers: Polar Audio is the UK distributor for the company's products.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held company.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: The company is an established manufacturer with retail products.
Geography: The company operates internationally with a UK distribution partner.
Beyond audio: The company's entire focus is on audio.

points.name: ARTSOUND
points.description: Belgian audio brand making affordable, user-friendly consumer sound products for home and public spaces.

A maker of consumer audio equipment that designs and sells affordable finished audio products for everyday use in homes, vehicles, workplaces and public spaces, aimed at consumers seeking user-friendly devices with good audio quality.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished audio hardware products sold as standalone physical devices.
2. Audio reproduction hardware and electronics designed for accessible consumer use.
3. Audio playback and sound reinforcement for daily environments.
4. Finished hardware products.
5. Homes, vehicles, workplaces and public spaces.
6. Consumers.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to end users.
points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held consumer electronics brand.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: A Belgian brand operating since 2001.
Geography: Based in Belgium and serving consumer markets.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: Ascendo
points.description: US audio company building high-performance speakers and subwoofers for home theaters and immersive cinema sound.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and manufactures high-end loudspeakers and subwoofers for residential home cinema installations. The organization builds passive and active speakers featuring coaxial point-source designs and proprietary driver technology, calibrated for immersive audio environments. It supplies finished speaker hardware directly to custom installers and home theater integrators.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished loudspeakers and subwoofers sold as physical hardware installed in residential theaters.
2. Coaxial point-source driver geometries with concentrically aligned tweeters and midrange drivers, paired with proprietary speaker management technology for transient response and active subwoofer amplification.
3. Full-range sound reproduction, infrasonic bass extension down to 3 Hz, phase-coherent point-source radiation, and wide panoramic sound coverage for immersive cinema audio.
4. Finished passive and active loudspeakers and subwoofers, accompanied by published independent laboratory measurement data.
5. Residential home cinemas, dedicated theater rooms, and multiroom music systems.
6. Custom home theater installers, integration firms, and audiophile consumers seeking high-performance residential cinema hardware.
7. Its finished loudspeakers are specified and installed by custom integration firms into residential home cinema projects.
8. It emphasizes open scientific measurement data and coaxial point-source driver alignment to eliminate phase errors and comb filtering across all seating positions.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It is a spin-off of AIA, partners with Storm Audio and Seymour-Screen Excellence for home cinema demonstrations, and is specified by integration firms including The Digital Picture, Cinema Buro, Cinemaworks with Louise Tarling Ltd, Dellicompagni, and ARLED Solutions GmbH.
Organization type: A privately held audio equipment manufacturing company and a spin-off entity.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished loudspeakers and subwoofers to custom installers and residential consumers.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 1999, with decades of research in sound generation, propagation, and perception.
Geography: Based in League City, Texas, United States, with loudspeakers handcrafted in Germany.
Beyond audio: It is a pure-play audio company focused exclusively on high-end loudspeakers and subwoofers for home cinema.

points.name: ATEIS Europe B.V.
points.description: Dutch pro audio company building certified public address and voice alarm systems for commercial and public spaces.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of public address and voice alarm systems that designs, develops and supplies EN 54-certified PA/VA and IP audio solutions along with a comprehensive loudspeaker range, for applications in transport, healthcare and commercial buildings.
1. An equipment maker that designs and supplies finished public address and voice alarm systems, IP audio solutions and loudspeakers, supported by in-house R&D and technical teams.

3. Its systems deliver certified voice alarm, public address audio distribution and IP audio across building-wide installations.
4. Customers receive finished hardware: complete PA/VA systems, IP audio products and loudspeaker ranges.
5. Its systems are installed in transport hubs, healthcare facilities and commercial buildings.
6. It sells to building owners, contractors and project teams specifying PA/VA systems for transport, healthcare and commercial construction projects.
7. Its certified PA/VA systems and loudspeakers are installed as finished equipment in commercial building, transport and healthcare projects.
8. Forty years of expertise and in-house R&D and technical teams enable it to tailor EN 54-certified systems to the specific needs of customers' projects.

Key partners and customers: Its portfolio is showcased at the ISE trade show.
Organization type: A company.
Business model: It makes money from the supply of finished PA/VA systems, IP audio products and loudspeakers.
Scale and maturity: The organization brings 40 years of expertise in PA/VA system design and supply.
Geography: It is based in Europe, as indicated by its name.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus: all of its work concerns public address, voice alarm and loudspeaker solutions.

points.name: AtlasIED
points.description: Texas-based manufacturer building commercial audio and communication systems for businesses.

A manufacturer of commercial audio and communication technology that designs, manufactures, and markets hardware and integrated systems for audiovisual professionals and integrators.

2. Digital audio platforms, amplifiers, IP endpoints, and digitally steerable loudspeakers with beam steering capabilities.

4. Finished hardware, including digital audio platforms, amplifiers, IP endpoints, loudspeakers, and equipment racks.

points.name: AUDAC

A maker of professional audio equipment that designs and sells loudspeakers, amplifiers, audio processors and control systems as a unified commercial audio ecosystem for installation professionals.
