points.bullets:
A parent company of a group of professional audio firms that designs, builds, and supplies professional monitoring speakers, studio acoustic panels, and recording microphones for recording studios, broadcast facilities, and audio engineers.
1. A parent company of professional audio equipment makers and studio design firms whose finished hardware and acoustic treatment products run in professional recording and broadcast studios.
2. The organization's subsidiaries develop loudspeaker transducers, acoustic diffusion and absorption panels, and condenser microphone capsules.
3. The group delivers studio monitoring, room acoustics correction, sound isolation, and recording microphone capabilities.
4. Customers get it as finished hardware and physical acoustic treatment products.
5. The devices and products are used in recording studios, mastering rooms, and broadcast facilities.
6. The organization sells to recording studios, musicians, audio engineers, and broadcast facilities.
7. Its subsidiaries build finished audio hardware and acoustic products that studios and engineers install in their facilities.
8. The organization unites distinct professional audio equipment, studio design, and acoustic treatment brands under a single parent company.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The organization includes Augspurger Monitors, Professional Audio Design Inc, Malekpour Design Partners, Studio Float, Jocavi USA, TAD Laboratories, and Sontronics.
Organization type: A parent company of a group of professional audio firms.
Business model: The organization makes money through hardware sales and acoustic treatment sales.
Geography: The organization operates in the United States and includes a subsidiary specifically for the United States market.
Beyond audio: Beyond equipment, the group's subsidiaries provide studio design, construction, and acoustic consulting services.

points.name: Mozilla Common Voice
points.description: Open-source initiative crowdsourcing diverse multilingual speech data for voice recognition.
points.bullets:
An open-source initiative that compiles and provides a crowdsourced, multilingual speech corpus with demographic metadata for training speech recognition systems, serving researchers and developers.
1. A data provider that builds a public dataset of donated speech recordings and provides it as an open-source corpus for machine learning training.
2. A web platform that collects volunteer-contributed voice recordings and associated demographic metadata to create a diverse corpus of spoken audio.
3. The dataset supplies diverse speech samples across multiple languages and accents for training automatic speech recognition models.
4. The speech corpus is delivered as an open-source dataset accessible to the public.
5. The data is used in training automatic speech recognition models and supporting voice technology research.
6. The organization provides data to developers, researchers, and organizations building speech technology.
7. Its dataset is used by chip and software developers to train speech recognition models that run on-device or in the cloud.
8. The corpus emphasizes inclusivity and representation by sourcing donated speech data from volunteers across diverse accents, languages, and acoustic environments.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The initiative is supported by the Gates Foundation, GIZ, and FCDO, and its data is used by NVIDIA.
Organization type: An open-source initiative managed by a nonprofit organization.
Business model: The organization operates as a grant-funded initiative providing open-source data at no cost.
Scale and maturity: The initiative aggregates donated speech data from global volunteers and has contributed hours of audio to research datasets.
Geography: The project operates globally, with specific efforts to grow digital innovation in East Africa.
Beyond audio: The initiative focuses entirely on building speech datasets for machine learning.

points.name: Segotia
points.description: Irish startup using EEG and AI to detect which person in a room a listener is focusing on.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer whose neuro-driven models decode auditory attention from EEG signals to determine which person in a room a user is trying to listen to, for hearing aid and audio device makers.
1. An AI model developer whose auditory attention decoding models run on-device in partners' chips.
2. Neural networks process EEG signals combined with AI to identify the target speaker a user is focusing on in a multi-talker environment.
3. Auditory attention decoding, speaker targeting and neural source selection.
4. AI models running on customers' devices.
5. Hearing aids and assistive listening devices.
6. Chip companies and hearing aid manufacturers.
7. Its models are integrated by chip vendors into their embedded platforms.
8. It combines EEG brain signal processing with AI to drive auditory attention decoding rather than relying on acoustic beamforming alone.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its auditory attention decoding is developed for the Gap9 embedded processor platform.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Geography: Based in Galway City, Ireland.
Beyond audio: It works on neurotechnology and brain-computer interfaces.

points.name: Smyth Research
points.description: Irish audio hardware company creating the Realiser, a headphone processor that personalizes virtual surround sound using listeners' own room measurements.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that builds dedicated hardware products for spatial audio personalization, using measured room impulse responses to create custom head-related transfer functions and head tracking for audiophile listening.
1. A professional audio equipment maker that builds dedicated spatial audio hardware units sold as finished hardware products.
2. The core technology combines personalized room impulse response measurement, custom head-related transfer function generation and head tracking.
3. The hardware delivers personalized spatial audio rendering, custom binaural headphone monitoring of specific listening environments and head-tracked virtual surround.
4. The spatial audio technology is delivered as finished dedicated hardware products.
5. The products are used in private listening environments and studios for headphone-based virtual surround monitoring.
6. The company sells to consumers seeking personalized spatial audio.
7. Its finished hardware products are purchased directly by consumers for personal listening.
points.profile:
Organization type: The organization is a private company.
Business model: The company makes money through hardware sales.
Beyond audio: Audio is the organization's entire focus.

points.name: S-Track
points.description: Chinese high-tech enterprise developing professional conference audio systems for meetings, education, courtrooms, transportation, and finance sectors.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment and solutions that develops and sells hardware and software systems for enterprise and institutional settings. The organization's products serve environments such as conference rooms, educational facilities, courtrooms, transportation hubs, and financial institutions.
1. An equipment maker that builds professional audio products and solutions sold as finished hardware and software systems deployed in customer facilities.
2. Professional audio hardware and software systems developed in-house and protected by patents and software copyrights.
3. Audio capture, processing, routing, and management for conferences and institutional communications.
4. Finished hardware and integrated software solutions sold directly to end-user organizations.
5. Conference rooms, educational facilities, courtrooms, corporations, transportation hubs, and financial institutions.
6. Enterprises and public-sector institutions including corporations, courts, schools, and financial organizations.
7. Its finished audio systems are deployed directly into enterprise and institutional facilities.
8. The organization combines proprietary hardware and software protected by patents into sector-specific solutions tailored to institutional use.
points.profile:
Organization type: A high-tech enterprise specializing in research and development, production, and sales.
Business model: Hardware and software system sales to enterprises and institutions.
Scale and maturity: An established enterprise with a research and development, production, and sales operation.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on professional audio products and solutions.

points.name: Seer Audio
points.description: Chinese audio manufacturer building amplifiers, speakers, mixers, and PA systems.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that designs, manufactures, and exports loudspeakers, power amplifiers, line arrays, and PA systems for live sound and fixed installations.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished professional audio hardware sold as complete speaker systems, amplifiers, and processors.
2. Analog and digital power amplification circuits, transducers, line array acoustics, and digital signal processing running on dedicated SHARC DSP chipsets.
3. Sound reinforcement, high-output low-frequency reproduction, long-throw acoustic dispersion, and multi-channel audio signal routing and equalization.
4. Finished hardware products comprising loudspeaker cabinets, subwoofers, power amplifiers, standalone digital audio processors, and portable all-in-one PA systems.
5. Large-scale performances, touring live shows, churches, convention centers, concert halls, clubs, outdoor events, and fixed venue installations.
6. Audio equipment wholesalers, event production companies, venue owners, system integrators, and international brand buyers seeking OEM and ODM manufacturing services.
7. Finished hardware is manufactured and exported to wholesale distributors and brand owners who supply live events and installed sound markets.
8. Provides deep OEM and ODM customization services alongside a broad standard catalog of certified professional audio products with integrated rigging hardware.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: OEM and ODM brand partners and international wholesale distributors.
Organization type: A privately held manufacturing company.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished audio equipment, wholesale manufacturing contracts, and OEM or ODM production fees.
Scale and maturity: A professional sound equipment manufacturer established in 1997 with an associated manufacturing entity founded in 2004.
Geography: Based in China, operating as a manufacturer, supplier, and exporter to international markets.
Beyond audio: The company focuses entirely on professional audio manufacturing.

points.name: Acustica Audio
points.description: Italian software company developing analog-modeled audio plugins and immersive mixing tools for headphones.
points.bullets:
A software developer that builds analog-modeled audio processors, stereo and multiband dynamics plugins, and psychoacoustic mixing tools for audio production and mixing engineers.
1. A software developer whose audio processing plugins and cloud platform run as native plugins in digital audio workstations and in the cloud behind a web application.
2. Analog circuit modeling algorithms and psychoacoustic spatial rendering algorithms running as digital signal processing software.
3. The specific audio capabilities it delivers are equalization, multiband dynamics processing, stereo imaging enhancement, headphone monitoring with room simulation, stem separation, and voice conversion.
4. Customers get it through software licenses and subscriptions for plugins, desktop applications, and a cloud-based web application.
5. The devices, products or settings it is used in are digital audio workstations, live performance rigs, and cloud-based production workflows.
6. The types of customer it sells to are producers, mixing engineers, and musicians.
7. Its software is used directly by audio engineers to process, mix, and master recorded audio.
8. What distinguishes its approach from others doing similar work is its use of specific analog circuit modeling for hardware emulation alongside its cloud-based collaboration and AI processing platform.
points.profile:
Organization type: The organization is a privately held company.
Business model: It makes money through software licenses and subscriptions.
Beyond audio: What the organization does beyond audio is provide cloud-based file storage, transfer, and collaboration infrastructure.

points.name: D+M Group
points.description: US audio technology company owning brands like Denon and Marantz while building home theater receivers and speakers.
points.bullets:
A consumer and professional audio equipment company that designs, markets, and sells finished audio products under multiple brand portfolios for home and automotive environments.
1. A consumer electronics equipment maker that builds finished audio hardware and sells it to end users.
2. Acoustic transducer and amplifier designs engineered for home theater and automotive sound reproduction.
3. High-fidelity audio playback and sound reinforcement for residential and commercial listening spaces.
4. The company provides finished physical hardware products and audio systems.
5. Its products are used in home theaters, living rooms, recording studios, and automotive audio systems.
6. The organization sells directly to consumers and professional audio installers.
7. Its finished hardware products are distributed through consumer retail channels and professional audio dealers.
8. The company leverages a portfolio of established legacy audio brands consolidated under a single corporate engineering and planning structure.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its portfolio includes the Denon, Marantz, and Boston Acoustics brands.
Organization type: It is a privately held corporate entity operating as a holding company for multiple audio brands.
Business model: The organization generates revenue through the sale of finished audio hardware.
Scale and maturity: It is an established, multi-brand corporate group undergoing organizational restructuring across its global operations.
Geography: The company is based in Mahwah, New Jersey, USA, and operates across North American and international markets.
Beyond audio: Audio hardware product planning, engineering, sales, and marketing constitute the entire focus of the business.

points.name: Human, Inc.
points.description: Seattle-based startup designing multifunctional wireless earpieces with active noise cancellation and built-in external speakers.
points.bullets:
A maker of consumer audio equipment that designs completely wireless earpieces with integrated software for augmented listening experiences, selling multifunctional hearables that combine active noise cancellation, ambient sound control, and external speaker capabilities directly to consumers.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished consumer earphones running integrated embedded software.
2. Audio hardware and embedded software combining acoustic drivers, active noise cancellation, and ambient sound amplification.
3. Active noise cancellation, ambient sound volume control, audio sharing, portable external speaker playback, and sound amplification.
4. Finished hardware products containing integrated software.
5. True wireless earbuds and hearables worn in everyday environments.
6. Consumers.
7. Its finished hardware products are sold directly to end users.
8. A total-encapsulation earpiece form factor that doubles as a portable external speaker and merges multiple audio functions into a single wearable.
points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: A seed-stage startup backed by over five million dollars in funding.
Geography: Based in Seattle.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on audio hardware and software for augmented listening.

points.name: TaiwanCarol
points.description: Taiwanese audio company manufacturing microphones for recording studios and live performances.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional audio equipment that produces microphones for recording studios, live performances, and music creation.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished microphones sold as physical hardware.
2. The microphones use large diaphragm capsules and patented transducer designs.
3. The microphones capture vocals and instruments for recording and live sound reinforcement.
4. Customers get the microphones as finished hardware products.
5. The microphones are used in recording studios and live performance venues.
6. The company sells to musicians, recording engineers, and live sound professionals.
7. Its finished microphones are sold to recording studios and performers.
points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held company.
Geography: The company is based in Taiwan.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: Seeburg Acoustic Line
points.description: German pro audio manufacturer building professional loudspeaker systems and amplifiers for live sound and permanent installations.
points.bullets:
A manufacturer of professional audio equipment that designs and builds loudspeakers, line arrays, subwoofers and digital power amplifiers for mobile applications and permanent installations.
1. An equipment maker that builds finished professional loudspeaker systems and power amplifiers sold as physical hardware.
2. Passive and active transducer designs, line array acoustics and Class D amplification with built-in digital signal processing.
3. High sound pressure level reproduction, controlled coverage, natural sound reproduction and deep bass response.
4. The company provides finished hardware products including passive and active speakers, subwoofers and amplifiers.
5. The products are used in live sound stages, mobile sound reinforcement and permanent audio installations.
6. The organization sells to professional audio retailers and sound reinforcement system integrators.
7. Its finished hardware is sold through retail channels to live sound engineers and installation professionals.
8. The company focuses on natural sound reproduction and reliability across loudspeaker and amplifier lines for mobile and installed professional use.
points.profile:
Organization type: The organization is a privately held company.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of finished professional audio equipment.
Scale and maturity: The company was founded in 1985 and operates as an established manufacturer.
Geography: It is based in Germany.
Beyond audio: Audio is its entire focus.

points.name: Blaupunkt
points.description: Historic German electronics brand making car multimedia systems, head units, and audio components.
points.bullets:
A maker of automotive audio equipment that develops and sells integrated in-car multimedia and entertainment systems, including head units, tuners, microphones, and built-in amplifiers, for original equipment manufacturers, aftermarket distributors, and retail consumers.
1. An equipment maker that builds integrated automotive multimedia and audio systems sold as finished hardware installed in vehicles.
2. The core technology comprises connected Android OS platforms paired with audio amplification, tuning, and microphone components integrated into in-car head units.
3. The systems deliver integrated in-cabin audio playback, amplification, infotainment control, and connected vehicle entertainment.
4. Customers receive the systems as finished hardware units distributed through factory-gate sales to automakers, aftermarket channels, and retail.
5. The equipment is used in automobiles for in-cabin infotainment and audio playback.
6. The organization sells to automotive original equipment manufacturers, aftermarket distributors, and direct retail consumers.
7. Its finished hardware is designed into vehicles by automakers and distributed to consumers through aftermarket and retail channels.
8. Its approach combines modern connected Android OS platforms with a historic German engineering and motorsport pedigree.
points.profile:
Organization type: A legacy brand entity operating within the consumer and automotive electronics market.
Business model: The organization generates revenue through hardware sales of multimedia systems and audio accessories.
Geography: The organization is globally focused and actively expands its footprint in emerging markets while operating from a base rooted in Germany.
Beyond audio: Audio technology is the primary and overarching focus of the organization's entire commercial business and product development efforts.

points.name: Mirelo
points.description: Software company generating sound effects from video footage.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer that builds generative audio models for video-to-audio synthesis, providing sound effects, Foley, and ambience generation for content creators, video editors, and developers.
1. An AI model developer whose generative sound models run in the cloud behind an API, in plugins for video editing software, and on a web platform.
2. Large generative video-conditioned audio models and open-weight multi-instrument transcription neural networks running in the cloud.
3. Video-conditioned sound effects generation, Foley synthesis, ambience generation, and multi-instrument audio transcription.
4. Cloud APIs, video editing software plugins, a web platform, and open-weight models.
5. Video editing workflows, film post-production, and creative content pipelines.
6. Video editors, content creators, developers, and creative professionals.
7. Its generative models and APIs are integrated by creators and developers into video editing pipelines and creative applications.
8. It focuses on generating sound effects, Foley, and ambience directly from video footage rather than from text or audio prompts.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It co-develops models with Kyutai and integrates its plugins with Adobe Premiere Pro and DaVinci Resolve.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: It generates revenue through API usage, software products, and platform access.
Scale and maturity: An early-stage company operating around a second-generation sound generation model.
Geography: The company operates in the generative audio market.
Beyond audio: It co-develops open-weight models for audio transcription alongside its core sound generation focus.

points.name: Sonilo
points.description: San Francisco AI audio startup generating synchronized music and sound effects for short-form videos.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer whose cloud-based generative audio models create music and sound effects synced to video for short-form video creators and developer platforms.
1. An AI model developer whose text-to-music and video-to-music models run in the cloud behind APIs.
2. Multimodal generative AI models that tie video comprehension to audio generation and timing.
3. Video-to-music generation, text-to-music generation, sound effect generation, and AI dubbing with lip-sync.
4. Cloud APIs and developer workflows.
5. Short-form video platforms and developer products.
6. Short-form video creators, developer platforms, and developers.
7. Its cloud APIs are integrated by developers into their video creation workflows and platforms.
8. Its multimodal system produces music and sound effects that react to video timing, pacing, and visual energy.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: B Capital and Redpoint are investors, Shutterstock provides licensed training music, and fal, ComfyUI, and TapNow are distribution and API partners.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: API usage and revenue sharing.
Scale and maturity: An early-stage startup that raised $11 million in funding.
Geography: Based in San Francisco, California, USA.
Beyond audio: Its entire focus is generative audio.

points.name: Shutterstock
points.location: New York City, New York, USA
points.description: New York stock media company licensing music for AI model training.
points.bullets:
A stock media company and data licensing provider that supplies rights-cleared audio tracks, among other multimodal content, for AI model training, and offers end-to-end model training partnerships for technology developers.
1. A stock media company that curates and licenses rights-cleared datasets, sold as licensed data services and AI training partnerships to AI developers.
2. A vast library of rights-cleared stock media assets, including audio recordings and metadata, structured as multimodal training datasets for machine learning.
3. Provision of licensed instrument-only music tracks and other audio content for training generative audio models.
4. Licensed datasets, data licensing services, and end-to-end AI model training partnerships delivered via enterprise agreements.
5. Generative AI model training, AI research and product development, and text-to-image generation platforms.
6. AI model developers, generative AI platforms, and technology companies building machine learning systems.
7. Its licensed media is consumed by AI developers as training data to build generative models.
8. Its model is built on a vast library of contributor-uploaded, rights-cleared stock media, allowing it to offer legally compliant training data and revenue sharing with content creators.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Has data licensing agreements with Meta, OpenAI, ElevenLabs, Black Forest Labs, Runway, LG, and Nvidia, and owns Pond5, Amper Music, and Giphy.
Organization type: A publicly traded stock media and data licensing company.
Business model: Media licensing, dataset licensing, enterprise subscriptions, and end-to-end AI model training services.
Scale and maturity: A large, established global platform with over 2 million contributors, customers in over 150 countries, and offices worldwide.
Geography: Based in New York City, New York, USA, operating globally.
Beyond audio: A global provider of stock photography, footage, music, and other media assets that has evolved into a multimodal data licensing partner for AI model training.

points.name: Sony AI
points.description: Japanese AI research organization developing generative sound effect models and audio search tools for gaming and film.
points.bullets:
An AI research organization that develops foundation models for sound effects and music generative models, as well as audio search and generation tools, for professional use in gaming, film, and interactive media.
1. An AI model developer whose generative audio and alignment models run as software tools integrated into game audio middleware.
2. Latent diffusion models, multimodal text-audio alignment models, and latent encoders/decoders based on neural network architectures.
3. Text-to-audio generation, video-to-audio generation, and similar sound search.
4. Software tools, foundation models, and datasets provided to developers and integrated into audio middleware.
5. Games, film, and interactive media.
6. Game developers and interactive media professionals.
7. Its models and tools are integrated into game audio middleware used by developers.
8. It trains its foundation models on commercially licensed professional sound libraries and develops multimodal models conditioned on both text and video.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It collaborates with Audiokinetic, Pro Sound Effects, and Boom Library, and operates under Sony Group Corporation.
Organization type: A research organization and subsidiary of a publicly traded company.
Scale and maturity: It is a corporate research arm operating with the resources of a large global technology and media conglomerate.
Geography: It is based in Japan.
Beyond audio: It conducts artificial intelligence research in domains beyond audio, including a racing game AI agent.

points.name: 25-Seven Systems
points.description: Subsidiary of the Telos Alliance building audio processing and monitoring tools for broadcast watermarking.
points.bullets:
A maker of professional broadcast equipment that develops audio delay, time compression, time-shifting, and watermark monitoring and processing products for radio and television broadcasters.
1. A maker of professional audio equipment whose analyzers and processors are sold as finished hardware units with analog inputs that run in broadcast facilities.
2. Digital signal processing hardware and software implementing audio time-shifting algorithms alongside real-time watermark detection and density analysis engines.
3. Audio delay, time compression, time-shifting, audio watermark detection, watermark density monitoring, and watermark enhancement optimization.
4. Finished hardware products and companion processing units installed in broadcast signal chains.
5. Radio and television broadcast facilities and audio programming distribution chains.
6. Radio and television broadcasters and broadcast engineering teams.
7. Its monitoring and processing hardware is installed directly by broadcasters in their transmission and studio signal chains.
8. It enables broadcasters to optimize the tradeoff between robust audio watermarking and clean audio quality by automatically adjusting enhancement levels.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It is a division of the Telos Alliance.
Organization type: A subsidiary brand within a privately held broadcast equipment company.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished broadcast analyzers and processors.
Scale and maturity: An established division operating within a long-standing broadcast industry equipment group.
Geography: Based and operating within the United States broadcast market.
Beyond audio: It is a pure-play audio technology company focused entirely on broadcast audio processing and watermark monitoring.

points.name: 思必驰
points.description: Chinese voice technology company providing conversational AI solutions and chips for smart cars, homes, and enterprises.
points.bullets:
An AI model and software developer that builds full-stack Chinese and English voice interaction solutions, including speech recognition, natural language processing and voice chips, for automotive, smart home and enterprise customers.
1. An AI model developer whose speech and natural language models run in the cloud behind APIs and on-device in chips, alongside a developer platform engineers use to build voice applications.
2. Neural networks for speech recognition, voiceprint recognition and natural language understanding integrated into a full-chain voice processing stack.
3. Voice search, far-field and near-field voice interaction, wake words, voiceprint recognition, in-car voice control and conversational enterprise assistants.
4. Cloud APIs, SDKs, a voice application developer platform, finished software assistants and AI voice chips.
5. Cars, smart home devices, screen-equipped devices, robots, story machines and enterprise conference and recruitment services.
6. Automakers, consumer electronics brands, robot manufacturers and enterprises.
7. Its models and platforms are integrated by automakers and device makers into their products, and its chip designs are co-developed with a semiconductor foundry partner.
8. It holds proprietary full-chain capabilities across both Chinese and English voice language technology within a single stack.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its investors and partners include Alibaba, MediaTek, Foxconn, FAW, Great Wall, Volkswagen, XPeng Motors and SMIC.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Software licenses, platform usage, enterprise service contracts and chip sales.
Scale and maturity: A mature company backed by multiple major corporate and venture investors.
Geography: Based in China and operating domestically.
Beyond audio: The organization focuses entirely on intelligent voice and natural language interaction technology.

points.name: 科大讯飞
points.description: Chinese technology company developing speech recognition, text-to-speech, and translation software and hardware.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer that builds voice recognition, speech-to-text, text-to-speech and natural language processing models for developers, enterprises and government clients.
1. An AI model developer whose speech processing models run in the cloud behind APIs and are licensed as enterprise software.
2. Large neural network models for speech and language processing trained on computing infrastructure.
3. Voice recognition, speech-to-text, text-to-speech and natural language processing.
4. Cloud APIs, enterprise software licensing, platform services and finished consumer hardware.
5. Large model deployments, productivity tools and communication systems.
6. Application developers, enterprises and government agencies in the automotive, aviation and financial sectors.
7. Its models are integrated by application developers into their software and by enterprises into their internal systems.
8. It trains its general-purpose models entirely on domestically produced computing infrastructure.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Local hardware manufacturers.
Organization type: A publicly traded artificial intelligence company.
Business model: Direct-to-consumer hardware sales, enterprise software licensing and artificial intelligence platform services.
Scale and maturity: A mature, established enterprise with over 10 million application developers and billions of yuan in bid-winning projects for 2025.
Geography: Based and operating primarily in China.
Beyond audio: It develops broader artificial intelligence applications that combine speech, language and handwriting recognition to enhance productivity and communication.

points.name: 云知声
points.description: Chinese AI technology company developing voice interaction chips and models for smart homes, cars, and hospitals.
points.bullets:
An AI and chip technology company that provides a full-stack intelligent voice offering, developing large language models, edge AI chips, and integrated software solutions for the medical, automotive, smart home, and transportation sectors.
1. An AI model and chip developer whose vertically integrated edge AI chips and voice models run on-device in terminal equipment and whose large language models run in the cloud.
2. Transformer-based large language models and edge AI chips integrated with voice algorithms, signal processing, and semantic understanding systems.
3. Speech recognition, speech synthesis, wake word detection, voice biometrics, multi-zone voice recognition, natural language understanding, and medical voice transcription with automated summarization.
4. Edge AI chips, cloud-based large AI models, and finished software solutions for specific industry applications.
5. Smart home appliances, automotive intelligent cockpits, and medical facilities requiring electronic medical records.
6. Consumer electronics brands, automakers, and healthcare institutions.
7. Its chips and models are designed into consumer appliances and automotive cockpits by device manufacturers, and its software is deployed directly in medical facilities.
8. It delivers a full vertical technology stack spanning from proprietary edge AI chips to large language models and finished industry applications.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It partners with automaker brands including Geely, appliance brands including Gree, Midea, and Haier, and over 500 medical institutions including Peking Union Medical College Hospital and Beijing Friendship Hospital.
Organization type: A publicly traded technology company listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.
Business model: It generates revenue through chip sales, model licensing, and the deployment of enterprise software systems.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2012 and listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2026, it is a large-scale enterprise with deployments across hundreds of medical institutions and multiple vehicle models.
Geography: Based in Beijing, it operates in China.
Beyond audio: Its large models also support non-audio tasks including text generation, logical reasoning, mathematical calculation, and code generation.

points.name: 讯飞
points.description: Chinese technology company developing speech recognition and voice AI for consumer hardware.
points.bullets:
A technology company that develops voice and audio algorithms, speech-to-text and text-to-speech engines, and finished audio hardware for consumer, enterprise, and government markets.
1. An AI model and software developer whose speech and language models run in the cloud behind an API, complemented by a line of finished end-user audio hardware.
2. Large generative speech and language models, speech recognition, and speech synthesis engines running in the cloud.
3. Speech-to-text transcription, text-to-speech synthesis, and large language model-powered structured meeting summarization.
4. Cloud APIs, enterprise software-as-a-service subscriptions, direct hardware sales, and technology licensing.
5. Meeting transcription, enterprise voice services, and end-user audio hardware deployments.
6. Consumers, enterprises, telecom operators, broadcasters, and government organizations.
7. Its AI models and speech engines are integrated by telecom operators, broadcasters, and enterprises into their services, while its hardware is sold directly to end users.
8. Deep vertical specialization in high-accuracy Chinese speech processing paired with proprietary large language model-generated summaries and specialized hardware integration.
points.profile:
Organization type: A publicly traded, established technology company.
Business model: Subscription-based software-as-a-service, enterprise technology licensing, technology integration, and direct hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: A mature, highly profitable market leader with research and development spending exceeding RMB 3 billion in the first half of 2026.
Geography: Based in China, operating and maintaining a strong competitive focus across the nation's consumer, enterprise, and government segments.
Beyond audio: Beyond audio technology, the company leverages its proprietary large language model to power AI companion services.

points.name: International Organization for Standardization
points.description: Geneva-based standards organization developing universal audio coding formats like MP3 and AAC for digital music and broadcast.
points.bullets:
A standards body that develops generic, industry-agnostic audio coding standards for the global technology ecosystem. It defines the technical specifications for audio compression and encoding profiles used across consumer, broadcast, and software applications. It provides the foundational rules that allow patent holders to collect royalties from companies implementing the standards.
1. A standards body whose audio coding specifications are adopted by chip companies, software developers, and broadcasters.
2. Audio compression and coding specifications, including perceptual coding standards and spectral band replication.
3. Audio compression, encoding, and profile standardization across various bitrates and fidelity levels.
4. Published technical standards that companies implement in chips, software products, and broadcast systems.
5. Digital audio players, broadcast systems, and multimedia software.
6. Technology companies, broadcasters, and software developers that implement the standards.
7. Its standards are implemented by chip vendors, software developers, and broadcasters into consumer products and media platforms.
8. It develops high-performance standards utilizing the best available technologies regardless of existing patents to encourage widespread market adoption.
points.profile:
Organization type: A global, non-commercial standards body.
Business model: It does not sell products directly but enables patent holders to collect royalties from companies that implement its standards.
Geography: It operates globally across different industries and countries.
Beyond audio: It develops standards across multiple industries beyond audio, including video, film, information technology, and general industrial manufacturing.

points.name: Ellipsis Health
points.description: Health tech startup developing AI voice tests to detect depression and anxiety.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer that builds cloud-based voice analysis models for healthcare providers, using vocal biomarkers to screen for depression and anxiety.
1. An AI model developer whose vocal biomarker models run in the cloud behind an API.
2. Machine learning models analyze acoustic and linguistic features of human speech to detect mental health conditions.
3. Vocal biomarker extraction for depression and anxiety screening.
4. Cloud APIs integrated into care management platforms.
5. Care management programs and mental health screening workflows.
6. Healthcare providers and care management organizations.
7. Its models are integrated into digital health platforms used by care providers.
8. It focuses on voice as a biomarker for clinical mental health conditions rather than general speech recognition or voice cloning.
points.profile:
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: API usage and enterprise software licensing.
Scale and maturity: A startup that has raised $30 million in total funding.
Geography: Based and operates in the United States.
Beyond audio: The organization's entire focus is applying audio analysis to clinical mental health.

points.name: Kintsugi
points.description: AI health startup analyzing voice audio for signs of depression and anxiety.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer that builds cloud-based voice biomarker models for mental health screening and voice fraud detection. It licenses these models to clinical and security customers, and is open-sourcing its core technology while shutting down commercial operations.
1. An AI model developer whose voice models run in the cloud behind an API, providing behavioral health scoring and fraud detection.
2. Deep learning and signal processing models trained on a large global dataset of voice recordings to identify acoustic markers of mental distress.
3. Detection of depression and anxiety from short voice clips, plus real-time synthetic and impersonated voice detection.
4. Cloud APIs, consumer-facing mobile applications, and open-source model releases.
5. Clinical settings, outbound call centers, contact centers, and carrier networks.
6. Healthcare providers, clinical workflows, security platforms, and carrier networks.
7. Its models are integrated by healthcare providers into clinical workflows and by security platforms into fraud detection systems.
8. The models use language-agnostic acoustic signals rather than speech content to identify clinical markers of distress.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Notable partners include Hugging Face, Children's Hospital Colorado, Joe DiMaggio Children's Hospital, Growth xPartners, Acrew Capital, Insight Partners, and the National Science Foundation.
Organization type: A privately held startup that is shutting down commercial operations.
Business model: API usage and open-source contributions.

points.name: Hyfe
points.description: Digital health company using acoustic AI to monitor coughs via mobile and wearable devices.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer that builds acoustic AI models for detecting and monitoring coughs, providing continuous cough tracking software for clinical trials, digital therapeutics, and individual wellness.
1. An AI model developer whose acoustic AI models run on-device at the edge on smartphones and wearables.
2. Acoustic AI systems using simple binary classifiers trained on billions of real-world data points to distinguish cough from non-cough sounds.
3. Continuous cough detection, cough frequency tracking over time, and cough sound classification.
4. Software products and models running on customers' edge devices like smartphones and wearables.
5. Clinical trials, digital therapeutics, individual wellness apps, and respiratory health monitoring.
6. Pharmaceutical companies, medical device manufacturers, academic institutions, healthcare organizations, and individual consumers.
7. Its AI models and software are integrated by pharmaceutical companies and medical device manufacturers into clinical trials and therapeutic products.
8. Its models are trained on billions of real-world data points and use simple binary classifiers to run on small edge devices.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Academic institutions, pharmaceutical companies, and medical device manufacturers.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Software licenses and subscriptions.
Geography: Serves healthcare organizations worldwide.
Beyond audio: Publishes a monthly email newsletter called Cough Science News providing expert-curated cough research and insights.

A maker of professional audio equipment and accessibility systems that develops and sells sound transmission products and personal audiological assistance systems for public spaces and hearing-impaired individuals.

2. Inductive, radio frequency, and infrared transmission systems that deliver audio signals to hearing aids and receivers in public venues.
3. Assistive listening, audio transmission via inductive loops, radio frequency, and infrared, and accessibility signalling for hearing-impaired users.
4. Finished hardware products, components, and accessories, with consulting and support for planning, installation, and operation.
5. Public spaces, professional audio transmission installations, and assistive listening venues.
6. Venues, public facilities, integrators installing professional audio transmission systems, and hearing-impaired end users.
7. Its finished hardware and systems are planned and installed by integrators into public spaces for accessibility.
8. Its approach combines assistive listening transmission hardware with planning, installation, and operational consulting for professional deployments.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The parent organization of the AUDIOropa brand, overseeing seven European subsidiaries and a Canadian company.
Organization type: A privately held company and parent organization of multiple subsidiaries.
Business model: Hardware sales, components, accessories, and consulting services for professional system installation.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 1985, operating as a group with multiple European subsidiaries and described as a leading provider in Germany.
Geography: Based in Weil am Rhein, Germany, with operations across Europe and Canada.
